children.text: Chapter 1

śam upaśāntāśeṣopatāpaparamānandādvayamayasvacaitanyasphārapratyabhijñāpanasvarūpam anugrahaṃ karoti yas tam imaṃ svasvabhāvaṃ śaṃkaraṃ stumas taṃ viśvotkarṣitvena parāmṛśantas tatkﾱptakalpitapramātṛpadanimajjanena samāviśāmaḥ tatsamāveśa eva hi jīvanmuktiphala iha prakaraṇa upadeśyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We praise that <s>Śaṅkara</s>, this own nature, who bestows grace whose form is the expansive recognition of one's own consciousness, made of supreme bliss, non-dual and free from every affliction; contemplating him as excelling the universe, we enter into him by sinking into the state of the cognizer imagined as fashioned by him. For that very immersion is the fruit of liberation while living taught here in this treatise.

children.text: bahuvacanam anugrahadṛṣṭikaṭākṣitāśeṣānugrāhyābhedaprathanāya ||
children.translated_text: The plural is used in order to make manifest the non-difference of all those fit to receive grace, who have been glanced upon by the look of grace.

children.text: tam ity anena yad asya asāmānyatvam api dhvanitaṃ tat prathayati yasyety ardhena ||
children.translated_text: By the word 'him' even his uncommonness has been suggested; this he sets forth with the half-verse beginning 'of whom'.

children.text: iha parameśvaraḥ prakāśātmā mahādevaḥ śabdarāśiparamārthapūrṇāhantāparāmarśasāratvāt sadaivānandaghanasphurattātmakobhayavisargāraṇiparāśaktyātmakapūrṇasvātantryasvarūpas tata eva citsvābhāvyād acalasyāpi śrībhagavataḥ svātantryaśaktir avibhaktāpy aśeṣasargasaṃhārādiparamparāṃ darpaṇanagaravatsvabhittāv eva bhāviyuktyānadhikām apy adhikām iva darśayantī kiṃcic calattātmakadhātvarthānugamāt spanda ity abhihitā tena bhagavān sadāspandatattvasatattvo na tv aspandaḥ yad āhuḥ kecit aspandaṃ paraṃ tattvam iti ||
children.translated_text: Here the Supreme Lord, <s>Mahādeva</s>, whose nature is light, because his essence is the reflective awareness of the full 'I' that is the ultimate reality of the mass of sound, is always a compact mass of blissful flashing forth; he has as his nature the full freedom consisting of the supreme power, the fire-stick of the two emissions. Therefore, from the very nature of consciousness, the power of freedom of the blessed Lord, though unmoving and though undivided, displays on its own surface, like a city in a mirror, the whole sequence of emanation, withdrawal, and so on, although by the proper reasoning it is not additional, as though it were additional. Since it follows the verbal root meaning 'to move a little,' it is called <s>spanda</s>. Thus the Blessed One has as his true essence the principle of eternal spanda, and is not without spanda, as some say: 'The supreme reality is motionless.'

children.text: evaṃ hi śāntasvarūpatvād anīśvaram evaitad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For in that case, since it would have the nature of quiescence, this reality would be without lordship.

children.text: sphurattāsāraspandaśaktimayaśaṃkarātmakasvasvabhāvapratipādanāyaiva cedaṃ śāstraṃ samucitaspandābhidhānaṃ mahāgurubhir nibaddham ||
children.translated_text: And precisely in order to teach one's own nature as <s>Śaṅkara</s>, consisting of the power of spanda whose essence is flashing forth, this treatise, bearing the fitting name <s>Spanda</s>, was composed by the great teachers.

children.text: etac ca vyaktībhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And this will become clear.

children.text: sā caiṣā spandaśaktir garbhīkṛtānantasargasaṃhāraikaghanāhantācamatkārānandarūpā niḥśeṣaśuddhāśuddharūpāmātṛmeyasaṃkocavikāsābhāsanasatattvā sarvopaniṣadupāsyā yugapad evonmeṣanimeṣamayī ||
children.translated_text: This power of spanda, whose form is the bliss of the wondrous realization of the compact 'I' that contains endless creation and dissolution within itself, whose true essence is the manifestation of all contraction and expansion of subject and object, whether pure or impure, which is worshipped by all the Upaniṣads, is at once made of opening and closing.

children.text: tathā hi śivādeḥ kṣityantasyāśeṣasya tattvagrāmasya prāksṛṣṭasya saṃhartṛrūpā yā nimeṣabhūr asāv evodbhaviṣyaddaśāpekṣayā sraṣṭurūponmeṣabhūmis tathā viśvanimeṣabhūś cidghanatonmeṣasārā cidghanatānimajjanabhūmir api viśvonmeṣarūpā ||
children.translated_text: For the ground of closing, which is the withdrawing form of the whole group of principles from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth that had previously been created, is itself, with reference to the state about to arise, the ground of opening in the form of the creator. Likewise, the ground of the universe's closing has as its essence the opening of compact consciousness, while the ground of immersion in compact consciousness also has the form of the universe's opening.

children.text: yad āgamaḥ
children.translated_text: As scripture says:

children.text: lelihānā sadā devī sadā pūrṇā ca bhāsate ||
children.translated_text: 'The goddess, ever licking forth, ever full, shines.'

children.text: ūrmir eṣā vibodhābdheḥ śaktir icchātmikā prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'This wave of the ocean of awakening is the Lord's power whose nature is will.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: śrīmān maheśvaro hi svātantryaśaktyā śivamantramaheśvaramantreśvaramantravijñānākalapralayākalasakalāntāṃ pramātṛbhūmikāṃ tadvedyabhūmikāṃ ca gṛhṇānaḥ pūrvapūrvarūpatāṃ bhittibhūtatayā sthitām apy antaḥsvarūpāvacchādanakrīḍayā nimeṣayann evonmeṣayati uttararūpatām avarohakrameṇa ārohakrameṇa tūttarottararūpatāṃ nimeṣayann eva jñānayoginām unmeṣayati pūrvapūrvarūpatām ata evottaram uttaraṃ pūrvatra pūrvatra saṃkocātmatāṃ jahadvikasitatvenāsāv ābhāsayati pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ tu rūpaṃ yathottaraṃ vikasitatāṃ nimajjayan saṅkucitatvena darśayati ||
children.translated_text: For the glorious <s>Maheśvara</s>, through his power of freedom, taking up the levels of the knowing subject ending with <s>Śiva</s>, mantra, maheśvara, mantreśvara, mantra, vijñānākala, pralayākala, and sakala, and also the levels known by them, opens them while closing the prior forms, which remain as their ground, by the play of concealing the inner nature. In the descending order he opens the later form while closing the earlier and earlier form; but in the ascending order, for the jñānayogins, he opens the earlier and earlier form while closing the later and later form. Therefore each later form, abandoning contraction in relation to the earlier, he makes appear as expanded; but each earlier form, immersing its expansion in accordance with the later, he shows as contracted.

children.text: evaṃ ca sarvaṃ sarvamayam eva prathayati kevalaṃ tadavabhāsitasaṃkocamātrata iyaṃ bhedapratipattir iva yad uddalanāyehatya upadeśa ity āstāṃ tāvad etat ||
children.translated_text: Thus he manifests everything as consisting of everything. Difference-cognition is only as it were, owing merely to the contraction manifested by him. The instruction here is for uprooting that; let this much suffice for now.

children.text: nīlasukhādyābhāsonmeṣamayy api ca saṃvit pramātrekātmakatatsvarūpanimeṣarūpāvabhātacarapītādyābhāsopasaṃhārarūpā ceti svasaṃvedanasiddhām imāṃ yugapad evonmeṣanimeṣobhayarūpāṃ pratibhāṃ bhagavatīṃ vicinvan tu mahādhiyaḥ saṃsāravicchedāya ||
children.translated_text: And although consciousness consists of the opening of appearances such as blue and pleasure, it is also the withdrawal of appearances such as moving and yellow, which shine as the closing of its own nature, unitary with the knowing subject. Therefore the great-minded should investigate this goddess <s>pratibhā</s>, established by self-awareness, whose form is at once both opening and closing, for the cutting off of saṃsāra.

children.text: ata evonmeṣanimeṣābhyām ityetatpadaṃ nijavṛttau bhaṭṭaśrīkallaṭena saṃkalpamātreṇā ity avibhaktam evecchaśaktirūpatayā vyākhyāyi ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in his own commentary, <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Kallaṭa</s> explained the phrase 'by opening and closing' as 'by mere resolve,' as undivided and precisely as the power of will.

children.text: saṃgrahakṛtāpi ekacintāprasaktasya yataḥ syād aparodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The author of the summary too says: 'When, for one intent on a single thought, another arising should occur,

children.text: unmeṣaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ svayaṃ tam upalakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: that is to be known as opening; one should observe it for oneself.'

children.text: ity atra prārabdhacintāsaṃharaṇam eva parasvarūpodayahetur unmeṣa ity abhidhāsyate pravṛttacintāsaṃhāraṃ vinā parasvarūpodayābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Here it will be stated that opening is just the withdrawal of the thought already begun, as the cause of the arising of the supreme nature, because without the withdrawal of the thought that has set in, there is no arising of the supreme nature.

children.text: etac ca tatraiva vitaniṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And we shall explain this at length in that very place.

children.text: parāmṛtarasāpāyas tasya yaḥ pratyayodbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The loss of the taste of supreme nectar, which is the arising of a cognition for him,

children.text: tenāsvatantratām eti sa ca tanmātragocaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: by that he comes to non-independence, and that has only that limited object as its field.'

children.text: ity atrāpy udayaḥ pralayaparamārtha iti spaṣṭam eva vakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: There too it will be said quite plainly that arising has dissolution as its highest reality.

children.text: yadā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta tadā syāt paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: 'When agitation is dissolved, then the supreme state comes to be.'

children.text: ity atrāpi kṣobhapralayātmā nimeṣaḥ parapadonmeṣarūpa ity api nirūpayiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: There too it will also be explained that closing, whose nature is the dissolution of agitation, has the form of the opening of the supreme state.

children.text: tad evam ekaivobhayarūpāpi śaktiḥ kadācid unmeṣapradhānatayā vyavahriyate kadācin nimeṣapradhānatayā ||
children.translated_text: Thus the one power, although it has both forms, is sometimes spoken of with opening predominating and sometimes with closing predominating.

children.text: tataś ca yasya saṃbandhinyāḥ svarūpanimeṣātmanaḥ kāryonmeṣapradhānāyāḥ śakter hetor jagato viśvasya śivāder dharaṇyantasyodayo 'bhedasāratānimajjanasattvo nānāvaicitryaśālī bhedarūpaḥ sargaḥ svarūponmeṣātmanaś ca bāhyatānimeṣapradhānāyāḥ śakter jagataḥ pralayo 'bhedamayatodayātmā vicitrabhedarūpatāsaṃhāra ita pralayo 'py udayarūpa udayo 'pi ca pralayarūpa iti vyākhyeyam vastutas tu na kiṃcid udeti vyayate vā kevalaṃ spandaśaktir eva bhagavaty akramāpi tathātathābhāsarūpatayā sphuranty udetīva vyayata iva ceti darśayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is to be explained as follows. For the one to whom it belongs, because of the power whose nature is the closing of its own form and whose predominance is the opening of effects, there is the arising of the world, the whole universe from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth: creation, diverse and variegated, having the form of difference, yet having as its real being immersion in the essence of non-difference. And because of the power whose nature is the opening of its own form and whose predominance is the closing of externality, there is the dissolution of the world: the reabsorption of its variegated form of difference, whose nature is the arising of non-difference. Thus dissolution too has the form of arising, and arising too has the form of dissolution. But in reality nothing at all arises or passes away. Rather, the blessed power of <s>spanda</s> alone, although without sequence, flashing forth in the form of appearances now as this and now as that, appears as if it arises and as if it passes away. We shall show this.

children.text: sthitivilayānu grahāṇāṃ viśiṣṭapralayodayarūpatvān nādhikyam iti pralayodayābhyām eva pañcavidhaṃ pārameśvaryaṃ kṛtyaṃ saṃgṛhītam ||
children.translated_text: Since maintenance, dissolution, and grace have the form of particular modes of dissolution and arising, there is no excess beyond these. Thus the fivefold act belonging to the Supreme Lord is included simply by dissolution and arising.

children.text: nirṇītaṃ caivaṃprāyaṃ mayaiva prathamasūtramātravivaraṇe spandasaṃdohe ||
children.translated_text: And something of this sort has already been determined by me in the <s>Spandasaṃdoha</s>, in the explanation of only the first sūtra.

children.text: nanu śrīmanmahārthadṛṣṭyā sṛṣṭyādidevatābhir eva vicitrā jagataḥ pralayodayāḥ saṃpādyante tat katham etad uktaṃ yasyetyādi ityāśaṅkyāha taṃ śakticakravibhavaprabhavām iti ||
children.translated_text: But one may object: From the viewpoint of the glorious <s>Mahārtha</s>, the manifold dissolutions and arisings of the world are accomplished by the deities of creation and the rest themselves. How then has this been said, 'of whom,' and so on? Anticipating this doubt, he says: 'him who is the source of the manifestation of the wheel of powers.'

children.text: śaktīnāṃ sṛṣṭiraktādimarīcīdevīnāṃ cakraṃ dvādaśātmā samūhas tasya yo vibhava udyogāvabhāsanacarvaṇavilāpanātmā krīḍāḍambaras tasya prabhavaṃ hetum ||
children.translated_text: The powers are the goddesses, such as <s>Sṛṣṭiraktā</s> and the other <s>Marīcī</s> deities. Their wheel is the group consisting of twelve. Its manifestation is the splendid play consisting of exertion, illumination, enjoyment, and dissolution; he is the source, the cause, of that.

children.text: etā hi devyaḥ śrīmanmanthānabhairavaṃ cakreśvaram āliṅgya sarvadaivajagatsargādikrīḍāṃsaṃpādayantīty āmnāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For tradition teaches that these goddesses, embracing the glorious <s>Manthānabhairava</s>, the lord of the wheel, always accomplish the play of the creation and other acts of the universe.

children.text: atha ca kasmāt parameśvarasya jagatsargasaṃhārādihetutvam ity āśaṅkāyām etad evottaraṃ śakticakreti ||
children.translated_text: And again, if the question is raised, 'Why is the Supreme Lord the cause of the creation, withdrawal, and so on of the world?', this very phrase, 'the wheel of powers,' is the answer.

children.text: yāvaddhi kiṃcid viśvaṃ saṃbhavati tatprakāśamānatvena prakāśamayatvāt svāminaś cātmasaṃsthasya bhāvajātasya bhāsanam ||
children.translated_text: For whatever universe comes into being, because it is manifested, is made of manifestation; and there is the shining of the whole class of entities established in the self of the Lord.

children.text: asty eva na vinā tasmād icchāmarśaḥ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, without that, the reflective awareness of will does not come into operation.

children.text: iti vipaścinniścitanītyā parameśvarasyāntaḥprakāśaikātmyena prakāśamānaṃ sthitaṃ sacchakticakram ity ucyate yataḥ parameśvarasyāgameṣv anantaśaktitvam uddhoṣyate ||
children.translated_text: According to this principle established by the wise, because the Supreme Lord is one with inner manifestation, what abides as manifest is called the real wheel of powers; for in the Āgamas the Supreme Lord is proclaimed to possess infinite powers.

children.text: tasya śakticakrasyābhāsaparamārthasya viśvasya yo vibhavaḥ parasparasaṃyojanāviyojanāvaicitryam anantaprakāraṃ tasya prabhavaṃ kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: That wheel of powers, whose ultimate reality is appearance, is the universe. He is the source, the cause, of its manifestation, the endlessly varied diversity of mutual conjunctions and disjunctions.

children.text: sa eva hi bhagavān vijñānadehātmakān svātmaikātmyena sthitān viśvān ābhāsān anyonyaṃ nānāvaicitryeṇa saṃyojayan viyojayaṃś ca viśvodayapralayahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that blessed Lord himself, joining and separating in manifold variety the universal appearances that have the nature of bodies of consciousness and that abide as one with his own self, is the cause of the universe's arising and dissolution.

children.text: tad uktaṃ śrībhaṭṭakallaṭena vijñānadehātmakasya śakticakraiśvaryasyotpattihetutvam ||
children.translated_text: This has been stated by the venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa</s>: 'He is the cause of the arising of the sovereignty of the wheel of powers, whose nature is a body of consciousness.'

children.text: ity etad vṛttyakṣarāṇām atra vyākhyādvaye 'py ānurūpyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the words of the commentary are appropriate here in both interpretations.

children.text: api ca śaktayo 'sya jagat kṛtsnam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'His powers are the entire universe.'

children.text: ity āgamadṛṣṭyā tasmāc chabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From this Āgamic viewpoint, and from the principle stated here, 'In reflections on word and meaning there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>,'

children.text: itīhatyasthityā ca jagadātmanaḥ tatkhecaryūrdhvamārgasthaṃ vyoma vāmeśigocaram ||
children.translated_text: and from the esoteric principle, 'The space established on the upper path of that <s>Khecarī</s> is the domain of <s>Vāmeśī</s>,' with regard to the self of the world,

children.text: iti rahasyanītyā ca vāmeśvarīkhecarīgocarīdikcarībhūcarī rūpasya mayaiva spandasandohe samyaṅ nirṇītasya aprabuddhadhiyas tv ete svasthitisthaganodyatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because the forms <s>Vāmeśvarī</s>, <s>Khecarī</s>, <s>Gocarī</s>, <s>Dikcarī</s>, and <s>Bhūcarī</s> have been correctly determined by me in the <s>Spandasaṃdoha</s>; and because, in the statement 'But these, their understanding unawakened, are intent on blocking their own state,' this too is to be determined there;

children.text: ity atrāpi nirṇeṣyamāṇasyaitadvyākhyādvayavyākhyātaśakticakraprapañcabhūtasya ca yataḥ karaṇavargo 'yaṃ ||
children.translated_text: and because this expansion of the wheel of powers, explained by these two interpretations, is the group of instruments in the statement, 'Since this group of instruments ...',

children.text: iti sthityendriyagrāmātmanaḥ tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and because, according to the principle 'Having mastered that power, the mantras ...', it has the nature of the group of senses in their state,

children.text: iti nityamantrātmanaḥ śabdarāśisamutthasya śaktivargasya ||
children.translated_text: and because it has the nature of the eternal mantras, the class of powers arisen from the mass of sound,

children.text: iti nītyā brāhmyādidevatāsvabhāvasyaivam āder anantaprakārasyāpi mayaiva spandasandohe vitatya nirṇītasya śakticakrasya yo vibhavo māhātmyaṃ tatra prabhavatīti prabhavaṃ svatantraṃ na tu paśuvat paratantram ||
children.translated_text: and because, according to this principle, it has the nature of deities such as <s>Brāhmī</s>, and because even the wheel of powers of infinite kinds such as these has been determined at length by me in the <s>Spandasaṃdoha</s>: its manifestation is its greatness, and he is the one who has mastery there, independent, not dependent like a bound creature.

children.text: śakticakrasya raśmipuñjasya yo vibhavo 'ntarmukho vikāsas tataḥ prabhava udayo 'bhivyaktir yasyeti bahuvrīhiṇāntarmukhatatsvarūpanibhālanād ayatnena parameśvarasvarūpapratyabhijñānaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The manifestation of the wheel of powers, the cluster of rays, is its inward expansion; from that, by a possessive compound, he is the one whose source, arising, or manifestation comes forth. The meaning is that through effortless inward contemplation of that very nature, recognition of the nature of the Supreme Lord occurs.

children.text: kiṃ ca yasya cidānandaghanasyātmana unmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ svarūponmīlananimīlanābhyāṃ yad antas tad bahiḥ iti yuktyā jagataḥ śarīrarūpasya tadanuṣaṅgeṇa bāhyasyāpi viśvasya pralayodayau yathāsaṃkhyaṃ majjanonmajjane bhavatas taṃ śakticakravibhavasya parasaṃviddevatāsphārasya prabhavaṃ bhaktibhājām etatsvarūpaprakāśakaṃ śaṃkaraṃ stumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, by the opening and closing of his own form, that is, by the unfolding and folding of the self whose nature is a compact mass of consciousness and bliss, and according to the reasoning 'what is within is outside,' the dissolution and arising of the world, which has the form of the body, and along with it of the external universe as well, occur respectively as immersion and emergence. We praise that <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the source of the manifestation of the wheel of powers, the expansion of the deity who is supreme consciousness, who reveals this nature to those endowed with devotion.

children.text: tathā yasya svātmanaḥ saṃbandhino bahirmukhatāprasararūpād unmeṣāj jagata udayo 'ntarmukhatārūpāc ca nimeṣāt pralayas taṃ viśvasargādikāryunmeṣādisvarūpasaṃviddevīmāhātmyasya hetuṃ śaṃkaraṃ stuma iti yathāsaṃbhavam api yojyam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, this may also be construed, as far as possible, as follows: we praise that <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the cause of the majesty of the goddess of consciousness whose nature is the opening and the rest that are the creation of the universe and so on; from the opening of his own self, in the form of the outward expansion connected with it, there is the arising of the world, and from the closing, in the form of inwardness, there is dissolution.

children.text: dehādyāviṣṭo 'pi parameśvaraḥ karaṇonmīlananimīlanābhyāṃ rūpādipañcakamayasya jagataḥ sargarsaṃhārau karoti ||
children.translated_text: Although the Supreme Lord has entered the body and the rest, by the opening and closing of the instruments he brings about the creation and withdrawal of the world made of the fivefold set beginning with form.

children.text: yad uktaṃ rahasyatattvavidā tad evaṃ vyavahāre 'pi prabhur dehādim āviśan ||
children.translated_text: What was said by the knower of the secret reality is this: even in ordinary activity, the Lord, entering the body and so forth,

children.text: bhāntam evāntararthaugham icchayā bhāsayed bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by his will makes the very mass of objects that shines within shine outwardly.

children.text: evaṃvidhārthaparigrahāyāpi yasya svātantryaśaktyā iti tyaktvā yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyām iti nyarūpi guruṇā ||
children.translated_text: Even in order to take hold of this kind of meaning, the teacher abandoned the wording 'by whose power of freedom' and formulated it as 'by whose opening and closing.'

children.text: atra ca śaṃkarastutiḥ samāveśarūpā prāpyatvenābhidheyā śakticakravibhavāt prabhavo yasyeti bahuvrīhiṇā śakticakravikāsas tatprāptāv upāya uktaḥ śakticakravibhavasya parasaṃviddevatāsphārasya bhaktibhājāṃ prabhavaṃ prakāśakam iti tatpuruṣeṇa phalam uktam ||
children.translated_text: And here the praise of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, whose form is immersion, is to be stated as the attainable object. By the bahuvrīhi compound 'he from whom there is the manifestation of the circle of powers,' the expansion of the circle of powers is taught as the means to attaining him. By the tatpuruṣa compound, 'the illuminator for the devoted of the manifestation of the circle of powers, that is, of the expansion of the deity who is supreme consciousness,' the fruit is stated.

children.text: yad vakṣyati tataś cakreśvaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: As he will say, 'Then one becomes the lord of the circle.'

children.text: ity abhidheyopāyayor upāyopeyabhāvaḥ saṃbandha ity abhidheyopāya saṃbandhaprayojanāny anenaiva sūtreṇa sūtritāni ||
children.translated_text: Thus the relation between what is to be stated and the means is the relation of means and goal; the subject matter, means, relation, and purpose have been indicated by this very sūtra.

children.text: nanv evaṃbhūtaśaṃkarasvarūpasattāyāṃ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ kutaś copādānādihetuṃ vinā jagad asau janayati tasyaivopādānatve mṛtpiṇḍasyeva ghaṭena jagatā tirodhānaṃ kriyeta tirohitātirohitatāyāṃ ca bhagavataḥ svabhāvabhedaḥ syāt punar unmajjane ca hetuścintyo jagadudayeca dveetaprasaṅga ityetāḥ śaṅkā eka prahāreṇāpahartumāha ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, what proof is there for the existence of such a nature of <s>Śaṅkara</s>? And how does he generate the world without causes such as a material cause? If he himself is the material cause, then, like a lump of clay by a pot, he would be obscured by the world. And if the Blessed One were both obscured and unobscured, there would be a division in his nature. When the world emerges again, a cause would also have to be considered; and in the arising of the world there would be the consequence of duality. To remove these doubts at a single stroke, he says:

children.text: Chapter 2
tasyāsya śaṃkarātmanaḥ prakāśānandaghanasya svasvabhāvasya na kutraciddeśe kāla ākāre vā nirodhaḥ prasaravyāghāto 'sti anāvṛtarūpatvād asthagitasvabhāvatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For this self-nature whose essence is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, a compact mass of light and bliss, there is no obstruction in any place, time, or form, no impediment to its expansion, because its form is uncovered and its nature is unobscured.

children.text: ayaṃ bhāvaḥ iha yatkiṃcitprāṇapuryaṣṭakasukhanīlādikaṃ citprakāśasyāvarakaṃ saṃbhāvyate tadyadi na prakāśate na kiṃcit prakāśamānaṃ tu prakāśātmakaśaṃkarasvarūpameveti kiṃ kasya nirodhakaṃ ko vā nirodhārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: here, whatever may be supposed to cover the light of consciousness, such as the vital breath, the subtle body of eight constituents, pleasure, blue, and so on, if it does not shine, it is nothing at all; but if it does shine, it is only the nature of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, whose essence is light. What, then, could obstruct what, and what purpose would obstruction serve?

children.text: etadeva tasyetyetadviśeṣaṇena yatretyādinopapādayati ||
children.translated_text: He establishes this very point, through the qualification 'of him,' with the words beginning 'where.'

children.text: yatra yasmiṃścid rūpe svātmani idaṃ mātṛmānameyātmakaṃ sarvaṃ jagatkāryaṃ sthitaṃ yatprakāśena prakāśamānaṃ satsthitiṃ labhate tasya kathaṃ tena nirodhaḥ śakyas tannirodhe hi nirodhakābhimatameva na cakāsyādity āśayaśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In whatever form, in its own self, this entire effected universe consisting of knower, means of knowledge, and object of knowledge is situated, and by whose light it receives existence as something that shines, how could that be obstructed by that? For if that were obstructed, the very thing presumed to be the obstructer would not appear: this is the remaining intention.

children.text: yathoktam
children.translated_text: As has been said:

children.text: tadātmanaiva tasya syātkathaṃ prāṇena yantraṇā ||
children.translated_text: 'Since it is of his own self, how could there be restraint of him by the vital breath?'

children.text: ityajaḍapramātṛsiddhau ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi.

children.text: nanūtpannasya sthityātmā prakāśe bhavati utpattireva tv asya kuta ityāha yasmāc ca nirgatamiti ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, the persistence of something produced occurs in light; yet whence comes its very production? He answers with 'and from which it has gone forth.'

children.text: smṛtisvapnasaṃkalpayoginirmāṇadṛṣṭayā citaḥ svānubhavasiddhaṃ jagatkāraṇatvam ujjhitvā apramāṇakam anupapannaṃ ca pradhānaparamāṇvādīnāṃ na tatkalpayituṃ yujyate ||
children.translated_text: In view of memory, dream, imagination, and yogic creation, one should not abandon the causality of consciousness for the world, which is established by one's own experience, and imagine causality for pradhāna, atoms, and the like, which is unsupported by proof and incoherent.

children.text: kāryapadena cedameva dhvanitaṃ kartuḥ kriyayā niṣpādyaṃ hi kāryamucyate na tu jaḍakāraṇānantarabhāvi jaḍasya kāraṇatvānupapatteḥ īśvarapratyabhijñoktanītyā ||
children.translated_text: And this very point is suggested by the word 'effect.' For what is to be accomplished by an agent through action is called an effect, not what merely comes after an inert cause, since the causality of what is inert is untenable, according to the reasoning stated in the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>.

children.text: bhaviṣyati caitat ||
children.translated_text: And this will be stated later:

children.text: avasthāyugalaṃ cātra kāryakartṛtvaśabditam ||
children.translated_text: 'Here the pair of states is expressed by the words effecthood and agency,'

children.text: ityatra
children.translated_text: in that passage.

children.text: sarvaśabdenopādānādinairapekṣyaṃ karturdhvanitam ||
children.translated_text: By the word 'all,' independence from a material cause and the like is suggested for the agent.

children.text: na ca kāryaṃ ghaṭādi kartuḥ kumbhakārādeḥ kadācitsvarūpaṃ tirodadhad dṛṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Nor is an effect such as a pot ever seen to conceal the own nature of its maker, such as the potter.

children.text: nanu nirgatir avasthitasya bhavati tatkimetat kvacid ādāv eva sthitaṃ nānyatra sthitamapitu tatraiva cidātmanītyāha yatra sthitamiti ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, going forth belongs to something that is already situated. Was this, then, situated somewhere at the beginning? Not situated elsewhere, but right there in the self whose essence is consciousness; therefore he says, 'where it is situated.'

children.text: āvṛttyā caitadyojyam ||
children.translated_text: And this should be construed by repetition.

children.text: ayamarthaḥ yadi cidātmani jagadahaṃprakāśābhedena na bhavet tat katham upādānādinirapekṣaṃ tata udiyāt ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: if the world did not exist in the self whose essence is consciousness in non-difference from the light of 'I,' how could it arise from that independently of a material cause and the rest?

children.text: yatastu yathā nyagrodhabījasthaḥ śaktirūpo mahādrumaḥ
children.translated_text: For, just as the great tree exists in the banyan seed in the form of power,

children.text: tathā hṛdayabījasthaṃ jagad etac carācaram ||
children.translated_text: so this moving and unmoving world exists in the seed of the heart.

children.text: ityāmnāyasthityā ||
children.translated_text: This is the state taught by scripture.

children.text: svāminaścātmasaṃsthasya ||
children.translated_text: And, 'of the Lord who is established in his own self,'

children.text: iti pūrvoktayuktyā ca tatraitad abhedena sphuratsthitaṃ tato 'yaṃ cidātmā bhagavān nijarasāśyānatārūpaṃ jagad unmajjayatīti yujyate ||
children.translated_text: according to the reasoning stated earlier as well, this world shines there as established in non-difference. Therefore it is fitting that this divine self whose essence is consciousness makes the world emerge, the world being a solidified form of his own relish.

children.text: evaṃ ca yatra sthitameva sad yasmān nirgatamityatra yojanā jātā ||
children.translated_text: Thus the construction has been made: 'where it is situated, and from which, while being just so situated, it has gone forth.'

children.text: ca evārthe bhinnakramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The particle 'ca' has the sense of 'eva' and is displaced from its regular order.

children.text: nanu yadi tasmāt prakāśavapuṣa idaṃ jagan niryātaṃ tan na pratheta na hi prathābāhyaṃ ca prathate ceti yuktam ityāśaṅkya yasmān nirgatamapi sadyatra sthitam ity āvṛttyā saṃgamanīyam ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, if this world has issued from that body of light, then it would not appear, for it is not reasonable that what is outside appearance should appear. In response to this doubt, by repetition the words should be connected as: 'although it has gone forth from which, it remains situated where.'

children.text: co 'pyarthe bhinnakramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The particle 'ca' also has the sense of 'api' and is displaced from its regular order.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati na prasevakādivākṣoṭādi tat tasmān nirgatamapi tu sa eva bhagavān svasvātantryād anatiriktām apyatiriktāmiva jagadrūpatāṃ svabhittau darpaṇanagaravat prakāśayan sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is what has been said: it is not like a bag and the like, or a walnut and the like, that it is something issued from that; rather, that Blessed One himself, by his own freedom, stands manifesting upon his own ground the form of the universe, which is not distinct from him, as though it were distinct, like a city in a mirror.

children.text: nanu ca bhavatvevaṃ sargasthityavasthayor jagatāsyāniruddhatvaṃ saṃhārāvasthayā tv abhāvātmanā suṣuptadeśīyayā jagataḥ sambandhinyā kathaṃ naitat tirodhīyate nahi grāhyaṃ jagadvinā grāhakaścidātmā kaścidity āvṛttyaitad evottaraṃ yasmān nirgatamapi sadyatraiva sthitamutpannam api jagatsaṃhārāvasthāyāṃ tadaikātmyenaivāste na tv asyānyaḥ kaściducchedaḥ śūnyarūpastasya vakṣyamāṇayuktyā prakāśaṃ bhittibhūtaṃ vinānupapatterityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one may object: let it be so in the states of creation and persistence, that this universe is unobstructed. Yet in the state of dissolution, which pertains to the universe as having the nature of absence and resembles deep sleep, how is this not concealed? For without the graspable universe there is no conscious self as grasper. To this, with repetition, he gives this very answer: because, even though it has issued forth, it remains in that from which it issued; and even though it has arisen, the universe, in the state of dissolution, exists only in identity with that. There is not some other annihilation of it, in the form of emptiness, since, by the reasoning to be stated, such a thing is impossible without light as its supporting ground. This is the meaning.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīsvacchandaśāstre
children.translated_text: As is said in the venerable <s>Svacchandaśāstra</s>:

children.text: aśūnyaṃ śūnyamityuktaṃ śūnyaṃ cābhāva ucyate
children.translated_text: 'What is empty is said to be not empty, and emptiness is called absence.

children.text: devyabhāvaḥ sa vijñeyo yatra bhāvāḥ kṣayaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O Goddess, that absence is to be understood where entities have come to destruction.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: evaṃ sarvaṃ yasya kāryaṃ yatprakāśenaiva prakāśate saṃhṛtamapi ca sadyatprakāśaikātmyena tiṣṭhati na tasya deśakālākārādi kiṃcin nirodhakaṃ yujyate iti vyāpakaṃ nityaṃ viśvaśaktikhacitaṃ svaprakāśam ādisiddhaṃ caitattattvamiti nāsya siddhāv ajñātārthaprakāśarūpaṃ pramāṇavarākamupapadyata upayujyate sambhavati vā pratyutaitattattvasiddhyadhīnā pramāṇādiviśvavastusiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, for him whose effect is everything, by whose light alone it shines, and even when withdrawn remains in immediate identity with whose light, no obstruction whatever by place, time, form, and the like is appropriate. Thus this reality is all-pervasive, eternal, filled with the power of the universe, self-luminous, and primordial. For the establishment of it, then, a poor means of valid knowledge, whose form is the disclosure of an unknown object, is not fitting, useful, or possible. On the contrary, the establishment of valid means of knowledge and all other things in the universe depends upon the establishment of this reality.

children.text: taduktamasmadgurubhis tantrāloke
children.translated_text: That has been said by our teachers in the <s>Tantrāloka</s>:

children.text: pramāṇānyapi vastūnāṃ jīvitaṃ yāni tanvate
children.translated_text: 'Even the means of valid knowledge, which extend the life of things,

children.text: teṣāmapi paro jīvaḥ sa eva parameśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: have as their supreme life that very <s>Parameśvara</s>.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yasmān nirgatamapīdaṃ jagadyatra sthitaṃ yatprakāśena prakāśamānaṃ tathābhūtamapi yatra sthitaṃ yatprakāśaikarūpaṃ yatprakāśa eva yasya siddhyai nyakṣeṇekṣyamāṇaṃ bhavati na tv anyaj jagan nāma kiṃcit ||
children.translated_text: This universe, although it has issued from him, remains in him; shining by his light, even being such, it remains in him; it is of the single form of his light. By that light alone, for the sake of its own establishment, it becomes something seen directly; but there is no other thing called 'world' at all.

children.text: atra yatra sthitamityāvartya dvir yojyam ||
children.translated_text: Here the phrase 'in which it remains' is to be repeated and construed twice.

children.text: evaṃ ca svānubhavasiddhamevāsya tattvasya sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāramelanāvabhāsino 'tidurghaṭakāriṇaḥ sarvadā sarvatrāniruddhatvam ||
children.translated_text: And thus, for this reality, which is established by one's own experience, which illumines the conjunction of creation, persistence, and dissolution, and which accomplishes what is exceedingly difficult, there is unobstructedness always and everywhere.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīmadutpaladevācāryaiḥ
children.translated_text: As was said by the venerable teacher <s>Utpaladeva</s>:

children.text: parameśvaratā jayatyapūrvā tava sarveśa yadīśitavyaśūnyā
children.translated_text: 'Your unprecedented supreme lordship triumphs, O Lord of all, since it is empty of anything to be ruled.

children.text: aparāpi tathaiva te yayedaṃ jagadābhāti yathā tathā na bhāti ||
children.translated_text: And yours is another such power, by which this world appears in such a way that, in truth, it does not appear as such.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atrahibhāsamānameva jagad bhāsanaikaśeṣībhūtatvād bhāsanātiriktaṃ na kiṃcidbhātītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the meaning is this: the world is only appearing; because it has become nothing but manifestation alone, nothing apart from manifestation appears.

children.text: kiṃca yatra sthitam ityuktyopaśamapade yasmāc ca nirgatamiti prasarapade yato'sya na nirodhas tato nimīlanonmīlanasamādhidvaye'pi yoginā svasvabhāvasamāveśapareṇaiva bhavitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, by the statement 'in which it remains' with respect to the state of quiescence, and by 'from which it issued' with respect to the state of expansion, since there is no obstruction of this reality, the yogin, in both kinds of samādhi, closing and opening, must be intent solely on immersion into his own nature.

children.text: yadvakṣyate
children.translated_text: As will be said:

children.text: yadā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta tadā syātparamaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: 'When agitation is dissolved, then the supreme state comes to be.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: And likewise:

children.text: tasmāc chabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, among reflections on word and meaning, there is no state which is not <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: ityapi ca ||
children.translated_text: So too.

children.text: kutracidanātmavādini saugatādau pramātari kutracic ca bādhakābhimate pramāṇe sati na tasya nirodhaḥ pratiṣedho'sti yato yastasya pratiṣedhako yac ca tasya pratiṣedhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ tadyadi na siddham abhittikam etac citraṃ siddhiścāsya prakāśate iti tatsiddhyaiva bhagavān ādisiddhasvaprakāśamūrtir astīty etat pratiṣedhāyoditenāpy anakṣaramuktam ||
children.translated_text: Even when there is, somewhere, a cognizer such as a Buddhist who teaches no-self, or somewhere a means of valid knowledge considered to be a refuter, there is no obstruction or denial of it. For that which denies it, and that valid means of knowledge which is its denier: if these are not established, then this picture is without a wall; and its establishment shines forth. Therefore, by the very establishment of that, the Blessed One, whose form is primordial, established, self-luminous light, exists. Thus even by what was raised to deny him, the unspoken has been said.

children.text: bhaviṣyati caitat
children.translated_text: And this will occur

children.text: na tu yo 'ntarmukho bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the interval at the passage, 'But not that entity which is inward-facing.'

children.text: ityatrāntare ||
children.translated_text: There.

children.text: evaṃ cānena viśvottīrṇaṃ viśvamayaṃ viśvasargasaṃhārādikāri śāṃkaraṃ svasvabhāvātmakaṃ tattvam ityabhidadhatā sarveṣu pārameśvareṣu yadupāsyaṃ taditaḥ spandatattvān nādhikaṃ kevalametatsvātantryavaśenaiva tadupāsāvaicitryam ābhāsyate ||
children.translated_text: And thus, by declaring this reality as transcending the universe, consisting of the universe, effecting the universe's creation, dissolution, and so on, as belonging to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and identical with one's own nature, he indicates that what is worshipped in all teachings concerning <s>Parameśvara</s> is nothing higher than this reality of <s>spanda</s>. Only through the power of this reality's own freedom does the diversity of that worship appear.

children.text: vastutastu etadvīryasāram evāśeṣam ||
children.translated_text: In reality, however, everything without remainder has only the essence of this power.

children.text: yadvakṣyati
children.translated_text: As he will say:

children.text: tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Having mounted that power, the mantras are possessed of the power of omniscience.'

children.text: ityetadapi bhaṅgyā pratipāditam ||
children.translated_text: This too has been taught indirectly.

children.text: evaṃ ca na kaścid uktacodyāvakāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And thus there is no opening for the objection stated.

children.text: evametādṛśeṣu cintāratnaprāyeṣu śrīspandasūtreṣu yadanyaiḥ sarvair vivṛtikṛdbhir vyākhyāyi yac cāsmābhiḥ kiṃcid vyākriyate tatrāntaramamatsarā anavaliptāś ca svayameva vicinvantu sacetaso na tu tad asmābhir udghāṭya pratipadaṃ pradarśyate granthagauravāpatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, with regard to these venerable <s>Spanda</s> sūtras, which are almost wish-fulfilling jewels of thought, whatever has been explained by all the other commentators, and whatever little is explained by us, thoughtful people who are free from envy and not arrogant should examine for themselves the difference there. But we do not disclose it and show it word by word, since that would make the treatise too weighty.

children.text: nanu jāgarādidaśasv īdṛśaḥ svabhāvo nānubhūyate yadi cāyamuktayuktibhirna kenacit nirudhyate tat jāgarādyavasthā svayameva nirotsyate iti śaṅkāta uktamapyartham apratipadyamānaṃ pratibodhayann upadiśati ||
children.translated_text: But one may object: in the states such as waking, such a nature is not experienced; and if this reality is not obstructed by anyone, according to the reasonings stated, then the waking and other states themselves will obstruct it. Anticipating this doubt, he instructs while awakening one who has not understood the point already stated.

children.text: Chapter 3
jāgarāparaparyāyo jāgracchabdaḥ śiṣṭaprayuktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: The word jāgrat is a synonym of jāgarā, because it is used by cultivated speakers.

children.text: lokaprasiddhe jāgratsvapnasuṣuptānāṃ bhede yogiprasiddhe 'pi vā dhāraṇādhyānasamādhirūpe prasarpati anyānyarūpe pravahati sati arthāt tattattvaṃ nijādanapāyinaḥ sarvasyātmabhūtāc cānubhavitṛrūpāt svabhāvān naiva nivartate ||
children.translated_text: When there is a differentiation, well known in ordinary usage, among waking, dream, and deep sleep, or even one well known among yogins in the form of concentration, meditation, and samādhi, and when it spreads out, that is, flows in various forms, then, in meaning, that reality does not at all turn away from its own nature, which cannot be taken away from itself and which has the form of the experiencer, the very self of everything.

children.text: yadihisvayaṃnivarteta taj jāgradādy api tatprakāśavinākṛtaṃ na kiṃcitprakāśeta ||
children.translated_text: For if it were itself to turn away here, then even waking and the rest, deprived of its illumination, would not appear as anything at all.

children.text: upalabdhṛtā caitadīyā jāgarāsvapnayoḥ sarvasya svasaṃvedanasiddhā sauṣupte yadyapi sā tathā na cetyate tathāpy auttarakālikasmṛtyanyathānupapattyā siddhā upalabdhṛta eva ca svabhāvān na nivartate upalabhyaṃ tv avasthādi tanmāhātmyān nivartatāṃ kāmaṃ kātra kṣatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And its character as the perceiver in waking and dream is established for everyone by self-awareness. In deep sleep, although it is not noticed in that way, it is nevertheless established because later memory would otherwise be inexplicable. And it is precisely the perceiver that does not turn away from its own nature; let the perceived object, such as a state, turn away by virtue of that power if it likes. What loss is there in that?

children.text: evakāro'pyarthe bhinnakramas tadabhāve'pi na nivartata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The particle eva too has the sense of api and is out of its regular order; the meaning is, 'even in the absence of that, it does not turn away.'

children.text: jāgarādivibhedasya viśeṣaṇadvāreṇa hetustadabhinne iti tasmāc chivasvabhāvādabhedena prakāśamānatvāt prakāśarūpe ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The reason for the differentiation beginning with waking is given through the qualifier 'non-different from that': because it appears without difference from that nature of <s>Śiva</s>, it is 'of the nature of illumination.' This is the meaning.

children.text: yac ca yadekātmakaṃ tatkathaṃ tannivṛttāv avatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: And how can that which is of one nature with something remain when that thing has ceased?

children.text: yadvā taditi kartṛpadam ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the word tat is the subject term.

children.text: abhinna iti tu kevalamabhinnatvaṃ jāgarādeḥ śivāpekṣameva ||
children.translated_text: But 'non-different' means only that the non-difference of waking and the rest is precisely with reference to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: arthāttattattvaṃ jāgarādibhede'pi sati prasarpati prasarati vaicitryaṃ gṛhṇāti tan naiva svabhāvān nivartata iti yojyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in sense, it should be construed: even when there is differentiation such as waking, that reality spreads out, expands, and assumes variety, but it does not at all turn away from its own nature.

children.text: kiṃcāyaṃ jāgradādibhedaḥ pariṇāmo vivarto veti yat sāṃkhyapāñcarātraśābdikādayo manyante tadvyudāsāyāpyuktaṃ tadabhinna iti ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, in order to refute the view of the Sāṃkhyas, Pāñcarātrikas, grammarians, and others, who think that this differentiation beginning with waking is either a transformation or an apparent transformation, he also said, 'non-different from that.'

children.text: avasthāprapañco'pi yadi cinmātrāt manāgapy atiricyeta cidrūpaṃ vā tatpariṇatau manāg atiricyeta tan na kiṃcic ca kā syād iti tāvan na pariṇāmo'sti ||
children.translated_text: If the manifold of states differed even slightly from mere consciousness, or if the form of consciousness differed even slightly when it transformed into that, then it would not be anything at all; and what could it be? Therefore, to begin with, there is no transformation.

children.text: yathoktam
children.translated_text: As has been said:

children.text: pariṇāmo'cetanasya cetanasya na yujyate ||
children.translated_text: 'Transformation is not fitting for what is unconscious, nor for what is conscious.'

children.text: iti śrīkiraṇe ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the venerable <s>Kiraṇa</s>.

children.text: na ca bhāsamāno 'sāv asatyo brahmatattvasyāpi tathātvāpatteḥ ity asatyavibhaktānyarūpopagrāhitā vivarta ityapi na saṃgatam ||
children.translated_text: Nor, since this appears, is it false, for then the reality of <s>Brahman</s> too would incur the same condition. Thus an apparent transformation, which would grasp another form separated from unreality, is also not coherent.

children.text: anena cātidurghaṭakiratvam eva bhagavato dhvanitam ||
children.translated_text: By this, the Lord's very power of bringing about what is exceedingly difficult has been suggested.

children.text: yasmāj jāgarādivibhedaṃ ca prakāśayati tatraiva ca svābhedamiti bhedātmanā tadabhedātmanobhayātmanā ca rūpeṇāparāparāparāparāśaktitrayasvarūpeṇa sphuratīty anuttaraṣaḍardhatattvātmatayā bhagavān eva sphurati ||
children.translated_text: Because he illuminates the differentiation beginning with waking and, within that very differentiation, also his non-difference from himself, the Blessed One alone shines forth in the form of difference, in the form of non-difference from that, and in the form of both, as having the nature of the three powers, aparā, parāparā, and parā, and as consisting of the supreme sixfold half-principle.

children.text: ataścajāgarādidaśāvasthito 'pi evamimaṃ svasvabhāvaṃ pariśīlayan yaścinute sa śaṃkara evetyupadiṣṭaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it has been taught that even while abiding in a condition such as waking, the one who cultivates this own-nature in this way and attends to it is <s>Śaṅkara</s> himself.

children.text: atha ye ekamevedaṃ saṃvidrūpaṃ harṣaviṣādādyanekākāravivartaṃ paśyāma ityuktyā jñānasaṃtāna eva tattvamiti saugatā manyante ye cāhaṃpratītipratyeyaḥ sadaiva sukhādyupadhitiraskṛta ātmeti mīmāṃsakāḥ pratipannās tānekenaiva ślokenāpavadati ||
children.translated_text: Now, those Buddhists who hold that the stream of cognitions alone is the reality, saying, 'We see this one thing only, whose form is consciousness, as an apparent transformation into many forms such as joy and sorrow,' and those Mīmāṃsakas who accept the self as always inferable by the cognition 'I,' though concealed by limiting adjuncts such as pleasure, are refuted by him with a single verse.

children.text: Chapter 4

ya evāhaṃ sukhī sa eva duḥkhī sukhānuśāyinā rāgeṇa yuktatvād rakto duḥkhānuśāyinā dveṣeṇa sambandhād dviṣṭetyādayaḥ saṃvido jñānāni tā anyatreti avasthātary ātmatattve vartante tatraivāntarmukhe viśrāmyanti sphuṭaṃ svasākṣikaṃ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: Cognitions such as 'the very same I who am happy is unhappy,' 'because of attachment that follows pleasure, I am attached,' and 'because of connection with aversion that follows pain, I am hostile,' are elsewhere, that is, they occur in the self-reality that is the abider in the states; and there alone, turned inward, they come to rest, making this plainly self-witnessed.

children.text: anyathā kṣaṇikajñānānāṃ svātmamātrakṣīṇatvāt tatsaṃskārajanmanām api vikalpānāmanubhavāgocare pravṛttyabhāvādanusaṃdhānam idaṃ na ghaṭeta ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, since momentary cognitions are exhausted in their own mere self, and since even the conceptual constructions born from their impressions would have no activity in what is outside the range of experience, this recognition of continuity would not be possible.

children.text: cakārās tulyayogitāparā anusaṃdhānaṃ dyotayanti ||
children.translated_text: The particles ca, having the sense of equal connection, indicate this recognition of continuity.

children.text: kīdṛśe'nyatra sukhādyavasthā udayapralayinyo 'nusyūtā dṛbdhā yasmiṃs tasmin sukhādyavasthānusyūte 'ntaḥsraksūtrakalpatayā sthite ||
children.translated_text: In what kind of 'elsewhere'? In that in which states such as pleasure, arising and dissolving, are threaded and strung together; in that which remains as if it were the inner thread of a garland, threaded through the states such as pleasure.

children.text: tā ity anenānusaṃdhīyamānāvasthānāṃ smaryamāṇatām abhidadhatkṣaṇikajñānavādimate 'nubhavasaṃskārotpannatvād arthākārārūṣitatve 'pi smṛteḥ kāmam anubhavasadṛśatvaṃ bhavatu na tv anubhavānubhūtātītakālārthavyavasthāpakatvaṃ ghaṭate sarvasaṃvidantarmukhe tu pramātari sati sarvaṃ yujyata iti sūcitavān ity alaṃ sukumārahṛdayopadeśyajanavairasyadāyinībhir ābhiḥ kathābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the word 'they,' he states that the states being connected in recognition are remembered. Thus he indicates that, according to the doctrine of momentary cognition, since memory is produced from experience and its impression, even though it may be tinged with the form of the object and may, if one wishes, resemble experience, it cannot establish an object of a past time that was experienced by experience. But when there is a knower turned inward in all cognition, everything is coherent. Enough, however, of these discussions, which cause distaste in people fit to be instructed through a tender heart.

children.text: etadarthibhiḥ pratyabhijñā parīkṣyā ||
children.translated_text: Those who desire this matter should examine the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>.

children.text: granthakṛtaiva tu yata iha yuktir āsūtritā tato'smābhiḥ kiṃcid udghāṭitam iti sacetobhir nāsmabhyam asūyayitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Since the author of the treatise himself has outlined the reasoning here, we have merely opened it up a little; therefore thoughtful people should not be resentful toward us.

children.text: mīmāṃsakaparihārāya tu etad itthaṃ vyākhyātavyam ||
children.translated_text: But for the refutation of the Mīmāṃsaka, this should be explained as follows.

children.text: ahaṃ sukhītyādisaṃvido yās tā anyatreti puryaṣṭakasvarūpe pramātari sukhādyavasthābhir anusyūte otaprotarūpe sphuṭaṃ lokapratītisākṣikaṃ vartante tiṣṭhanti na tv asmadabhyupagate 'smiṃś cidānandaghane śaṃkarātmani svasvabhāve iti na sarvadā sukhādyupādhitiraskṛto 'yamātmāpi tu cinmayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The cognitions such as 'I am happy' and the like, which occur elsewhere, clearly abide in the subject whose nature is the subtle body of eight constituents, interwoven and pervaded by states such as pleasure; this is witnessed by common experience. They do not abide in what we accept here, the self-nature that is the soul of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, a compact mass of consciousness and bliss. Therefore this self is not at all times obscured by limiting adjuncts such as pleasure; rather, it is made of consciousness.

children.text: yadā tu nijāśuddhayā vakṣyamāṇayāyaṃ svasvarūpaṃ gūhayitvā tiṣṭhati tadā puryaṣṭakādyavasthāyāṃ sukhitvādirūpatāsya tatrāpi na nirodhas taiḥ sukhādibhir asyety uktam eveti na tattiraskṛto 'yaṃ kadācidapi ||
children.translated_text: But when, through its own impurity to be explained below, this self conceals its own true nature and remains so, then in the state of the subtle body and the like it has the form of happiness and so on. Even there, however, there is no suppression of it by those states such as pleasure, as has already been said; therefore it is never obscured by them.

children.text: ahaṃ kṛśo 'haṃ sthūla ityādipratītiparihāreṇa ahaṃ sukhī duḥkhītyādi vadato 'yamāśayaḥ sukhitvādipratītisaṃbhinnāṃ puryaṣṭakabhūmim antarmukhe pade nimajjayaṃs tadanuṣaṅgeṇa bāhyasyāpi dehaghaṭāder galanāt pratyabhijānāty eva svaṃ śivasvabhāvatvam iti sarvathā puryaṣṭakaśamanāyaiva yatna āstheya iti ||
children.translated_text: In avoiding cognitions such as 'I am thin' and 'I am stout,' while saying 'I am happy,' 'I am unhappy,' and the like, this is his intention: by sinking the level of the subtle body, intermixed with cognitions of happiness and the rest, into the inward state, and consequently by the melting away even of external things such as the body and a pot, one indeed recognizes one's own nature as <s>Śiva</s>. Therefore effort is to be undertaken in every way precisely for the pacification of the subtle body.

children.text: uktopapattisiddhāṃ samastavādānām anupapannatām anuvadann upapattisiddhaṃ spandatattvam evāstīti pratijānāti yuktyanubhavāgamajño rahasyagurupravaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Repeating the untenability of all doctrines as established by the reasoning already stated, the foremost teacher of the secret, who knows reasoning, experience, and scripture, declares that only the spanda principle, established by reasoning, truly exists.

children.text: Chapter 5
iha yatkiṃcidduḥkhasukhādyāntaraṃ nīlapītādikaṃ bāhyaṃ grāhyaṃ yac caitad grāhakaṃ puryaṣṭakaśarīrendriyādi tattāvatsauṣuptavad asaṃcetyamānaṃ sphuṭameva nāstīti vaktuṃ śakyam ||
children.translated_text: Here, whatever is internal, such as pain and pleasure, and whatever external object of grasping there is, such as blue and yellow, and whatever this grasper is, such as the subtle body, body, and senses, can certainly be said not to exist at all when it is not being cognized, as in deep sleep.

children.text: yadāpi tu saṃcetyate tadā saṃcetyamānasyāpy asya caitanyamayatvāc caitanyam evāstīty āyātam ||
children.translated_text: But even when it is cognized, since this too, while being cognized, consists of consciousness, the result is that consciousness alone exists.

children.text: yadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: As they have said:

children.text: prakāśātmā prakāśyo 'rthe nāprakāśaś ca sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: 'The object to be illuminated has light as its self, and what is not light is not established.'

children.text: iti rahasyatattvavido'smatparameṣṭhinaḥ śrīmadutpaladevapādāḥ śrīmadīśvarapratyabhijñāyām ||
children.translated_text: Thus speak our supreme teachers, the venerable <s>Utpaladeva</s> and others, knowers of the secret reality, in the venerable <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>.

children.text: ihāpi vakṣyate
children.translated_text: Here too it will be said:

children.text: tatsaṃvedanarūpeṇa tādātmyapratipattitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Because identity with that is understood through the form of its own awareness.'

children.text: ityato duḥkhasukhādi nīlādi tadgrāhakaṃ ca yatra nāsti tatprakāśaikaghanaṃ tattvamasti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the reality exists as a compact mass of light alone, in which pain, pleasure, blue and the like, and their grasper are absent.

children.text: nanvevaṃ sarvagrāhyagrāhakocchede śūnyātmaiva tattvamityāyātaṃ netyāha na cāsti mūḍhabhāvo 'pi iti ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, if all objects and subjects of grasping are abolished in this way, then reality turns out to have the nature of voidness. No, he says: 'Nor is there even a state of delusion.'

children.text: mūḍhabhāvo mūḍhatvaṃ śūnyarūpatāpi yatra nāsti so 'pi hi na prathate kathamasti prathate cet tarhi prathātmakatvān nāsau kaścit prathaivāsti na ca prathāyāḥ kadācidbhāvo bhavati tadabhāve prathābhāvasyāpyasiddheḥ ||
children.translated_text: A state of delusion means deludedness, even the condition of being void in form; where that does not exist, for it too does not appear. How could it exist? If it does appear, then, because it has the nature of appearance, it is not some distinct thing; appearance alone exists. Nor is appearance ever non-existent, since in its absence the non-existence of appearance too could not be established.

children.text: bhaviṣyati caitat
children.translated_text: And this will occur later:

children.text: na tu yo 'ntarmukho bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'But not the state that is turned inward,'

children.text: ityatra ||
children.translated_text: in that passage.

children.text: api ca mūḍhabhāva aiśvaryātmakavimarśaśūnyaprakāśamātratattvo brahmarūpo 'pi yatra nāsti yac chrutyantavidaḥ pratipannāḥ vijñānaṃ brahma iti tasyāpi svātantryātmakaspandaśaktiṃ vinā jaḍatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, where there is not even the state of delusion, namely the Brahman-form accepted by knowers of the end of the Veda as a reality of mere light empty of reflection whose nature is sovereignty, as in 'consciousness is Brahman,' even that, without the spanda-power whose nature is freedom, is inert.

children.text: yathoktaṃ pratyabhijñāyām
children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>:

children.text: svabhāvamavabhāsasya vimarśaṃ vidur anyathā
children.translated_text: 'They know reflective awareness to be the own nature of manifestation; otherwise,

children.text: prakāśo 'rthoparakto'pi sphaṭikādijaḍopamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: light, though colored by objects, would be like something inert such as a crystal.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: bhaṭṭanāyakastotre 'pi
children.translated_text: And also in the hymn of <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s>:

children.text: napuṃsakamidaṃ nātha paraṃ brahma phalet kiyat
children.translated_text: 'Lord, this supreme Brahman is neuter; how much could it bear fruit

children.text: tvatpauruṣī niyoktrī cen na syāttvadbhaktisundarī ||
children.translated_text: if your beautiful devotion, your masculine commanding power, did not exist?'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: evaṃ ca yatra sthitam ityataḥ prabhṛti yattattvaṃ vicāritaṃ tadevāsti tac cāstyeva paramārthato yuktyanubhavāgamasiddhena rūpeṇa paramārthata eva cākalpitena pūrṇena rūpeṇāsti na tu nīlādivat kalpitena
children.translated_text: Accordingly, the reality examined from the words 'where it is situated' onward is precisely what exists; and that indeed exists in the highest sense, in the form established by reasoning, experience, and scripture, as an unimagined and complete form in the highest sense, not as something imagined like blue and the rest.

children.text: yathoktaṃ mahāgurubhiḥ
children.translated_text: As the great teachers have said:

children.text: evamātmanyasatkalpāḥ prakāśasyaiva santy amī
children.translated_text: 'Thus these inert things, imagined as unreal, exist in the self

children.text: jaḍāḥ prakāśa evāsti svātmanaḥ svaparātmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: only as light; light alone exists, as its own self and as the selves of others.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tatrabhavadbhartṛhariṇāpi
children.translated_text: And also by the venerable <s>Bhartṛhari</s>:

children.text: yadādau ca yadante ca yanmadhye tasya satyatā
children.translated_text: 'That which is at the beginning, at the end, and in the middle has reality;

children.text: na yad ābhāsate tasya satyatvaṃ tāvadeva hi ||
children.translated_text: what does not appear has reality only to that extent.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: sāvadhāraṇatvāt sarvavākyānām evakāro 'tra trir yojyaḥ
children.translated_text: Since all the sentences are restrictive, the word 'only' should be supplied here three times.

children.text: evamanena sūtreṇa sukhādyākārasaṃvitsaṃtānavādināṃ sukhādikaluṣitapramātṛtattvavādināṃ grāhyagrāhakanānātvavādināṃ sarveṣām abhāvavādināṃ niṣparāmarśaprakāśabrahmavādināṃ ca matam anupapannatvād asattvenānūdya pāramārthikaṃ spandaśaktirūpameva tattvam astīti pratijñātam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by this sūtra, the views of all those who maintain a stream of cognitions in the forms of pleasure and the like, of those who maintain a subject-principle tainted by pleasure and the like, of those who maintain the multiplicity of object and subject of grasping, of all proponents of non-existence, and of those who maintain a Brahman that is light without reflective awareness, have been restated as unreal because they are untenable; and it has been declared that only the true reality, whose form is spanda-power, exists.

children.text: atha ca yasminn asmin sopadeśasāvadhānamahānubhāvapariśīlye sphurattāsāre spandatattve sphurati duḥkhasukhagrāhyagrāhakatadabhāvādikam idaṃ sad api na kiṃcid eva sarvasyaitac camatkāraikasāratvāt tad evaitad astīty upadiṣṭam
children.translated_text: And further, in this spanda principle, whose essence is flashing forth and which is to be cultivated with instruction, attentiveness, and great realization, when it flashes forth, all this pain, pleasure, object and subject of grasping, their absence, and so on, though existent, is really nothing at all, because all of it has wonder as its single essence. It has therefore been taught that this alone exists.

children.text: yanmahāguravaḥ
children.translated_text: As the great teachers say:

children.text: duḥkhānyapi sukhāyante viṣam apy amṛtāyate
children.translated_text: 'Even pains turn into pleasures, and even poison becomes nectar;

children.text: mokṣāyate ca saṃsāro yatra mārgaḥ sa śāṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: saṃsāra too becomes liberation where the path is that of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: śāṃkaro mārgaḥ śaṃkarātmasvabhāvaprāptihetuḥ parāśaktirūpaḥ prasaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The path belonging to <s>Śaṅkara</s> is the expansion in the form of the supreme power, the cause of attaining the intrinsic nature whose essence is <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: evam upapattiparighaṭitatattvapratyabhijñānāya sābhijñānam upāyaṃ nirūpayati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in order that the reality whose principle has been set forth by reasoning may be recognized, he explains the means together with that recognition.

children.text: Chapter 6
tannirṇītaṃ tattvam ādarāt śraddhayā prayatnena ca
children.translated_text: That determined reality is to be examined with respect, with faith and with effort:

children.text: udyamo bhairavaḥ
children.translated_text: "Effort is <s>Bhairava</s>."

children.text: iti śivasūtrapratipāditena sarvabhedopasaṃhārātmanā nijaujovṛttisphāraṇarūpeṇa paripūrṇāntarmukhasvarūpasevanātmanā bhairavarūpeṇodyamena parīkṣyam ||
children.translated_text: It is to be examined by the effort in the form of <s>Bhairava</s>, taught in the <s>Śivasūtra</s>, whose nature is the gathering up of all difference, whose form is the expansion of one's own force, and whose essence is the cultivation of a full inward-turned nature.

children.text: yata iyamiti sarvasya svasaṃviditā tasya śaṃkarātmanaḥ svasvabhāvasyākṛtrimā sahajā spandatattvarūpā svatantratā sarvatra jaḍājaḍaviṣaye sphurantī sthiteti śeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: For this freedom, directly known by everyone as "this," of that own nature whose essence is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, is unmade and innate, has the form of the principle of <s>spanda</s> (vibration), and shines everywhere in both inert and non-inert objects: this is what remains to be supplied.

children.text: kiṃ tat tattvam ityāha yata ityādi labhata ityantam ||
children.translated_text: What is that reality? He answers with the passage beginning "from which" and ending "obtains."

children.text: ayamiti lokaprasiddho golakādirūpo na tu śāstritastasya nityaparokṣatvenāyamiti nirdeśābhāvāt karaṇavargas trayodaśendriyāṇi viśeṣeṇa mūḍho māyāvaśāj jaḍābhāsībhūto 'ṇor mūḍhād apyadhikaṃ mūḍhatvaṃ prāpto 'mūḍhavac cetanavat svayaṃ pravṛttisthitisaṃhṛtīr labhate viṣayonmukhībhavati tatra rajyate tataśca nivartata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The word "this" means the commonly known one whose form is the bodily organ and so forth, not the one established by scripture, since that is always beyond direct perception and so cannot be indicated as "this." The group of instruments means the thirteen senses. Being especially deluded, under the sway of <s>māyā</s>, and having become as though inert, it has obtained a delusion even greater than that of the deluded individual soul; yet, like one undeluded, that is, like one conscious, it itself obtains activity, maintenance, and withdrawal: it turns toward objects, becomes attached there, and then withdraws from them. This is the meaning.

children.text: kathaṃ sahāntareṇa cakreṇa ihāntaraṃ cakraṃ karaṇeśvaryo nāntaḥkaraṇāni teṣāṃ vargaśabdena svīkārāt na vakṣyamāṇaṃ puryaṣṭakaṃ tatsthasyāntaḥkaraṇatrayasya vargaśabdenaiva gṛhītatvāt tanmātrāṇāṃ ca vāsanāmātrarūpāṇām upadeśyam ayoginaṃ prati sākṣāt pravṛttyādikartṛtvenāsiddheḥ yoginastu sākṣāt kṛtatanmātrasya svayameva paratattvapariśīlanāvahitasyopadeśyatvābhāvāt tasmād etadekīyamatam asat ||
children.translated_text: How could this occur together with an inner wheel? Here the inner wheel is not the goddesses who rule the instruments, since they are included by the word "group"; nor is it the eightfold subtle body to be mentioned later, since the three inner instruments belonging to it are already included by the word "group," and since the subtle elements, being merely dispositions, are not established as directly performing activity and the rest for the non-yogin who is being instructed. As for the yogin who has directly realized the subtle elements, he is himself intent on examining the supreme reality and is not someone to be instructed. Therefore this opinion of some is invalid.

children.text: vimūḍho 'mūḍhavad ityanena karaṇavarga eva saṃbandhyo natvantaramapi karaṇeśvarīcakraṃ tasya ciccamatkārarūpatvāt ||
children.translated_text: By the phrase "deluded like an undeluded one," only the group of instruments is to be connected, not another wheel of ruling goddesses of the instruments as well, because that has the nature of the wondrous relish of consciousness.

children.text: evam abhidadhānasyāyam āśayaḥ yadayaṃ śaṃkarātmā svasvabhāvo 'tidurghaṭakariṇaḥ svātantryād yugapadeva saṃvittisāraṃ ca karaṇeśvarīcakraṃ jaḍābhāsarūpaṃ ca karaṇavargam ekatayaiva nirbhāsayan pravṛttisthitisaṃhṛtīḥ kārayati yena bhagavatyaḥ karaṇeśvaryo yathā tattadbhāvasṛṣṭyādi vidadhati tathā karaṇavargo jaḍo 'pi tatkārīva lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: The intention of one who speaks thus is this: this own nature whose essence is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, by its freedom that accomplishes what is extremely difficult, simultaneously manifests in unity both the wheel of goddesses ruling the instruments, whose essence is consciousness, and the group of instruments, whose form is as though inert, and makes them perform activity, maintenance, and withdrawal. Therefore, just as the blessed ruling goddesses of the instruments carry out the creation and so on of each particular state, so too the inert group of instruments appears to do that work.

children.text: yadyapi rahasyadṛṣṭau na kaścij jaḍaḥ karaṇavargo 'sti apitu vijñānadehāḥ karaṇeśvarya eva vijṛmbhante tathāpīha suprasiddhapratītyanusāreṇopadeśyaḥ krameṇa rahasyārthopadeśe 'nupraveśya ityevam uktam ||
children.translated_text: Although, from the esoteric viewpoint, there is no inert group of instruments at all, but rather only the goddesses ruling the instruments, whose bodies are consciousness, unfold, still here, following the very familiar ordinary cognition, the person to be instructed is gradually to be led into the instruction of the esoteric meaning. Thus it has been stated in this way.

children.text: evaṃ ca golakādirūpakaraṇavargāpravṛttyādikrameṇa tadadhiṣṭhātṛrūpaṃ nijamarīcicakraṃ cinvānenaiva tadubhayapracodakaṃ śrīmacchaṃkarātmakaṃ svasvarūpaṃ parīkṣaṇīyaṃ yatas tatprāptau tadīyākṛtrimā svatantratāsya yoginaḥ syād ity apy anenaivoktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Accordingly, by discerning, through the sequence of activity and so on of the group of instruments in the form of bodily organs and the rest, one's own wheel of rays in the form of their presiding powers, one should examine one's own nature, splendid and consisting of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, which impels both of them. For when that is attained, the unmade freedom belonging to it would belong to this yogin. This too is said by this very passage.

children.text: tadetadeva parīkṣaṇārhaṃ paramopādeyatvād etadeva ca parīkṣituṃ śakyamuktayuktyā sukhopāyatvāt ata evādareṇābhilaṣitaviṣayopabhogānirodhātmanā bahumānena ||
children.translated_text: This very thing is worthy of examination because it is supremely to be appropriated; and this alone can be examined, because by the reasoning stated it is an easy means. For this very reason it is to be examined with respect, that is, with esteem whose nature is the non-obstruction of enjoying desired objects.

children.text: atra parīkṣaṇasyehatyopadeśānusāreṇa prāptakālatā ||
children.translated_text: Here, in accordance with the instruction given in this context, the proper time for examination has arrived.

children.text: yathoktaṃ rahasyagurubhiḥ
children.translated_text: As the teachers of the secret have said:

children.text: nijanijeṣu padeṣu patantv imāḥ karaṇavṛttaya ullasitā mama
children.translated_text: "Let these activities of the instruments, arisen for me, fall into their own respective stations;

children.text: kṣaṇam apīśa manāgapi maiva bhūt tvadvibhedarasakṣatisāhasam ||
children.translated_text: O Lord, may there not be, even for a moment, even slightly, the rash loss of the taste of non-difference from you."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: parīkṣyam ity arhe śakye prāptakālatāyāṃ praiṣādau ca kṛtyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The suffix <s>kṛtya</s> in "to be examined" is used in the senses of worthiness, possibility, timeliness, command, and the like.

children.text: atha ca jaḍaḥ karaṇavargo yad balād amūḍhavat pravṛttyādi labhate iti sarvasyānubhavasākṣikam abhidadhadindriyādicaitanyavādicārvākamatam apyanena vyudastavān ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, by stating what is witnessed by everyone's experience, namely that the inert group of instruments obtains activity and the rest like an undeluded one through the force of that reality, he has also thereby refuted the Cārvāka doctrine that the senses and so forth are conscious.

children.text: atha kathamuktaṃ tatas tattvāc cetanatām ivāsādyendriyāṇi svayaṃ pravṛttyādi labhanta iti yāvatāyam eva grāhaka icchayā dātrādīnīva karaṇāni prerayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, how has it been said that from that reality, as though attaining consciousness, the senses themselves obtain activity and the rest, since in fact this very perceiver impels the instruments, like sickles and the like, by his will?

children.text: yad apyuktaṃ tat tattvaṃ prayatnena parīkṣyam iti tadapi kathaṃ yato 'smākam icchā bahir evānudhāvati na tu tattvaparīkṣāyāṃ pravartitum utsahata ity āśaṅkyāha ||
children.translated_text: And what has been said, that that reality is to be examined with effort, how can that be so, since our will runs only outward and does not have the strength to engage in the examination of reality? Anticipating this doubt, he says:

children.text: Chapter 7

ayaṃ laukikaḥ puruṣa icchaiva nodanaṃ pratodastasya prerakatvena karaṇapravartanārthavyāpāraṇāya yasmān na pravartate api tu ātmanaś cidrūpasya yad balaṃ spandatattvātmakaṃ tatsparśāt tatkṛtāt kiyanmātrād āveśāt tatsamo bhavet ahaṃtārasavipruḍabhiṣekādacetano 'pi cetanatām āsādayatyeva ||
children.translated_text: This ordinary person does not proceed from will alone, which is the goad, as its impeller, for the sake of employing the instruments in activity. Rather, from contact with that power of the self whose form is consciousness and whose nature is the principle of <s>spanda</s>, from a slight immersion produced by that, he becomes equal to it; by the sprinkling of the drops of the relish of I-ness, even what is unconscious surely attains consciousness.

children.text: tatas tat tattvaṃ na kevalaṃ karaṇāni yāvat tatprerakatvena śaṅkitaṃ kalpitamapi pramātāraṃ cetanīkṛtya svayaṃ pravṛttyādipātraṃ karoti yenāsyāyam abhimāno 'haṃ karaṇāni prerayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore that reality not only vitalizes the instruments, but even the imagined knower, who is suspected of being their mover, by making him conscious as their impeller, itself makes him the vessel of activity and the rest. By it he has this conceit: 'I impel the instruments.'

children.text: spandatattvānuvedhaṃ vināpi tu sa eva na kiṃciditi karaṇānāṃ grāhakasya ca svaraśmicakraprasarānuvedhena cetanībhāvāpādakaṃ tattvaṃ parīkṣyamiti yuktameva ||
children.translated_text: But without penetration by the spanda principle, that very knower is nothing at all. Therefore it is quite proper to examine the reality that brings about conscious life in the instruments and in the grasper through penetration by the expansion of the wheel of its own rays.

children.text: yadi punar icchākhyena pratodarūpeṇa karaṇāntareṇa karaṇāni prerayet tad apīcchākhyaṃ karaṇaṃ preryatvāt karaṇāntaraṃ svapreraṇāyāpekṣeta tadapy anyad ity anavasthā syāt ||
children.translated_text: If, again, he were to impel the instruments by another instrument in the form of a goad called will, then that instrument called will, because it too would be something impelled, would require yet another instrument to impel itself; that too would require another, and so there would be infinite regress.

children.text: yat tūktam asmākamicchā na tatra pravartitum utsahate iti tatrāpyādyaṃ ślokārdham abhyupagamena paraṃ tūttaratayā yojyam ||
children.translated_text: As for what was said, 'Our will is not able to engage in that,' here too the first half-verse is to be accepted, while the latter half is to be connected as the reply.

children.text: satyaṃ nāyaṃ puruṣastattvaparīkṣārtham icchāṃ pravartayituṃ śaknoti necchayā tattvaṃ viṣayīkartuṃ kṣamas tasyāvikalpyatvād api tu viṣayān anudhāvantīm icchāṃ tadupabhogapuraḥsaraṃ praśamayya yadā tv antarmukhamātmabalaṃ spandatattvaṃ svakaraṇānāṃ ca cetanāvahaṃ spṛśati tadā tatsamo bhavet tatsamāveśāt tadvat sarvatra svatantratām āsādayatyeva yasmād evaṃ tasmāt tattvaṃ parīkṣyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: True: this person is not able to set will in motion for the sake of examining reality, nor can he make reality an object by will, because that reality is beyond conceptual determination. Rather, after quieting the will that runs after objects, together with its preceding enjoyment of them, when he inwardly touches the strength of the self, the spanda principle that carries consciousness to his own instruments, then he becomes equal to it. Through absorption into it, he indeed obtains freedom everywhere, just like it. Since this is so, therefore reality is to be examined: this is the meaning.

children.text: śaktibhūmeḥ sparśāpradhānatvād ātmabalasparśādity uktam ||
children.translated_text: Because the plane of power is chiefly a matter of contact, the text says, 'from contact with the strength of the self.'

children.text: nanu cāyaṃ kṣetrī parameśvaramayo 'pi kiṃ na sadā pāripūrṇyena sphurati kasmād antarmukhātmabalasparśam apekṣata ity āśaṅkyāha ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, if this field-knower is made of the Supreme Lord, why does he not always shine in fullness? Why does he depend on an inward contact with the strength of the self? Anticipating this doubt, he says:

children.text: Chapter 8

nijā svātmīyā svasvātantryollāsitā yeyaṃ svarūpāvimarśasvabhāvā icchāśaktiḥ saṃkucitā satyapūrṇaṃmanyatārūpā aśuddhir āṇavaṃ malaṃ tanmalotthitakañcukapañcakāvilatvāt jñānaśaktiḥ krameṇa bhedasarvajñatvakiṃcijjñatvāntaḥkaraṇabuddhīndriyatāpattipūrvam atyantaṃ saṃkocagrahaṇena bhinnavedyaprathārūpaṃ māyīyaṃ malamaśuddhir eva kriyāśaktiḥ krameṇa bhedasarvakartṛtvakiṃcitkartṛtvakarmendriyarūpasaṃkocagrahaṇapūrvam atyantaṃ parimitatāṃ prāptā śubhāśubhānuṣṭhānamayaṃ kārmaṃ malam apyaśuddhiḥ tayāsamarthasya pūryajñatvakartṛtvavikalpasya tata eva kartavyeṣu laukikaśāstrīyānuṣṭhāneṣv abhilāṣiṇo 'bhīṣṭānavāpter nityam abhilāṣavyākulasya tata eva kṣaṇam apy alabdhasvarūpaviśrānteḥ yadā uktavakṣyamāṇopapattyanubhavāvaṣṭambhato 'bhilāṣavivaśagrāhakābhimānātmā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta anātmany ātmābhimānanivṛttipuraḥsaram ātmany anātmābhimānopaśāntiparyantena prakarṣeṇa līyeta tadā paramaṃ spandatattvātmakaṃ padaṃ syād asya pratyabhijñāviṣayatāṃ yāyād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One's own impurity is as follows. This will-power, one's own, belonging to the self, flashing forth through one's own freedom, and by nature a reflective awareness of one's own form, becomes contracted and takes the form of a sense of incompleteness: this is impurity, the āṇava mala.
