Because of the obscuration caused by the five sheaths arisen from that impurity, knowledge-power, in sequence, assumes the contraction of differentiated omniscience into limited knowledge, internal organ, intellect, and sense faculties, becoming extremely contracted as the manifestation of distinct knowable objects: this is the māyīya mala, impurity itself. Action-power, in sequence, assumes the contraction of differentiated universal agency into limited agency and the organs of action, becoming extremely limited and consisting of the performance of auspicious and inauspicious acts: this too is the kārma mala, impurity. By that impurity, he is incapable, subject to concepts of being to be completed and of limited knowledge and agency; for that very reason he desires worldly and scriptural undertakings among things to be done, is constantly agitated by desire because his wished-for object is not obtained, and therefore does not rest in his own nature even for a moment. When, supported by the reasoning and experience already stated and still to be stated, the agitation whose nature is the grasper's egoity overpowered by desire is dissolved, that is, is dissolved intensely, beginning with the cessation of self-identification in what is not the self and ending with the calming of non-self-identification in the self, then the supreme state, whose nature is the spanda principle, would belong to him, that is, it would become an object of his recognition: this is the meaning.

children.text: na tu tadaiva bhavati tasya nityatvāt ||
children.translated_text: It does not come into being only then, for it is eternal.

children.text: uktaṃ ca vijñānabhairave
children.translated_text: And it has been said in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s>:

children.text: mānasaṃ cetanā śaktirātmā ceti catuṣṭayam
children.translated_text: 'The mental faculty, consciousness, power, and self: this fourfold set,

children.text: yadā priye parikṣīṇaṃ tadā tadbhairavaṃ vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: when, O dear one, it has entirely waned, then that is the body of <s>Bhairava</s>.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: nijāśuddhiśabdenamalaṃ nāma dravyaṃ pṛthagbhūtam astīti ye pratipannāste dūṣyatvena kaṭākṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the expression 'one's own impurity,' those who have accepted that mala is a separately existing substance have been glanced at as objects of refutation.

children.text: nanu ca grāhakāhambhāvātmani kṣobhe kṣīṇe nistaraṅgajaladhiprakhyam aspandameva tattvaṃ prasaktam ityāśaṅkāṃ śamayati ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, when the agitation whose nature is the grasper's 'I'-sense has waned, the reality would seem to be motionless, like an ocean without waves. He calms this doubt:

children.text: Chapter 9

tadetyupadeśyāpekṣayā akṛtrimaḥ sahajo dharmaḥ prāṅ nirdiṣṭasvatantratārūpaḥ parameśvarasvabhāvo jñatvakartṛtve sāmarasyāvasthitaprakāśānandātmanī jñānakriye lakṣaṇamavyabhicāri svarūpaṃ yasya tādṛk tadā kṣobhopaśame 'sya puruṣasya syād abhivyajyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, relative to the person being instructed, his unmade, innate nature, previously described as freedom and having the nature of the Supreme Lord, would have as its invariable characteristic, its own form, knowledge and action: these are the powers of knowing and doing, whose essence is light and bliss established in mutual harmony. At that time, when agitation is calmed, that nature would become manifest for this person: this is the meaning.

children.text: kuta etad abhivyajyata ityāha yatastadā paramapadapraveśasamaye sarvam īpsitamiti yadyaj jijñāsitaṃ cikīrṣitaṃ vāsya tat pravivikṣāyām abhūt tattaj jānāti ca karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: Whence is this manifested? He says: because then, at the time of entering the supreme state, whatever is desired, that is, whatever he wished to know or wished to do when he was about to enter it, all that he both knows and does.

children.text: cakārāv atra yaugapadyam āhatuḥ na tu yathaike cakārābhyāṃ jñānakriyayor aikātmyaṃ sūcayatīti taddhi jñatvakartṛtvalakṣaṇa ity anenaivaikadharmaviśeṣaṇena sambandhinirdeśena vāstavasvarūpābhidhāyinoktam ||
children.translated_text: The two occurrences of 'and' here express simultaneity. They do not, as some say, indicate by the two particles 'and' the unity of knowledge and action; for that has already been stated by the single qualifying property, 'whose characteristic is knowing and agency,' or by the indication of the related terms, which states their real nature.

children.text: atha yataḥ karaṇeti nijāśuddhīti sūtrapratipāditonmeṣakramasamādhānasākṣātkṛtasya spandatattvasya dṛḍhāvaṣṭambhād vyutthānamapi samādhyekarasaṃ kurvato bhavocchedo bhavatītyāha ||
children.translated_text: Now, because the spanda principle, directly realized through the gradual resolution of emergence taught in the sūtras beginning 'because the instruments' and 'one's own impurity,' is firmly supported, even emergence from meditation becomes of one taste with samādhi; therefore the cutting off of worldly existence occurs. He states this:

children.text: Chapter 10
uktopapattyupalabdhyanuśīlanapratyabhijñātaṃ taṃ spandatattvātmakaṃ svabhāvam ātmīyam adhiṣṭhātṛbhāvena vyutthānadaśāyām api vyāpnuvantam avalokayaṃś cinvānaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing and discerning his own nature, which has the essence of the spanda principle, recognized through the disciplined contemplation of the reasons already stated and through direct realization, as pervading even the state of emergence as its presiding power,

children.text: na vrajen na viśecchaktir marudrūpā vikāsite
children.translated_text: the power, whose form is breath, should neither go out nor enter when it is expanded;

children.text: nirvikalpatayā madhye tayā bhairavarūpadhṛk ||
children.translated_text: by means of it, in the middle, in a state free from conceptual construction, one bears the form of <s>Bhairava</s>.

children.text: iti tathā
children.translated_text: Thus, and likewise:

children.text: sarvāḥ śaktīś cetasā darśanādyāḥ sve sve vedye yaugapadyena viṣvak
children.translated_text: Casting all the powers of seeing and the rest by the mind, each toward its own object, simultaneously in every direction,

children.text: kṣiptvā madhye hāṭakastambhabhūtas tiṣṭhan viśvākāra eko 'vabhāsi ||
children.translated_text: standing in the middle, become like a golden pillar, you shine as one whose form is the universe.

children.text: iti śrīvijñānabhairavakakṣyāstotranirdiṣṭasampradāyayuktyā nimīlanonmīlanasamādhinā yugapadvyāpakamadhyabhūmyavaṣṭambhād adhyāsitaitadubhayavisargāraṇivigalitasakalavikalpo 'kramasphāritakaraṇacakraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the traditional method taught in the venerable <s>Vijñānabhairava-kakṣyāstotra</s>, through the samādhi of closing and opening, by firm support in the middle plane that pervades both at once, with all conceptual constructions melted away by the fire-drill of the two emissions superimposed there, and with the wheel of the instruments expanded all at once,

children.text: antarlakṣyo bahir dṛṣṭinimeṣonmeṣavarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: with the aim within, the gaze outside, free from closing and opening the eyes,

children.text: iyaṃ sā bhairavī mudrā sarvatantreṣu gopitā ||
children.translated_text: this is that <s>Bhairavī mudrā</s>, kept secret in all the tantras.

children.text: ity āmnātabhagavadbhairavamudrānupraviṣṭo mukurāntarnimajjadunmajjannānāpratibimbakadambakalpamanalpaṃ bhāvarāśiṃ cidākāśa evoditam api tatraiva vilīyamānaṃ paśyan janmasahasrāpūrvaparamānandaghanalokottarasvasvarūpapratyabhijñānāt jhaṭiti truṭitasakalavṛttiḥ smayamāno vismayamudrāpraviṣṭa iva mahāvikāsāsādanāc ca sahasaiva samuditasamucitatāttvikasvabhāvo yo yogīndra āste tiṣṭhati na tv avaṣṭambhāc chithilībhavati tasyeyamiti sakalajagatkampakāriṇī kutsitā jananamaraṇādiprabandharūpā sṛtiḥ pravṛttiḥ kuto nijāśuddhilakṣaṇasya taddhetor abhāvān naiva bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Entering the venerable <s>Bhairava mudrā</s> taught in scripture, seeing the vast mass of entities, like a cluster of many reflections sinking and rising within a mirror, as arising in the sky of consciousness itself and dissolving there itself, and, from the recognition of his own extraordinary nature as a mass of supreme bliss never known in thousands of births, having all mental activities instantly cut off, smiling as if entered into the mudrā of wonder, and through the attainment of a great expansion, the lord among yogins suddenly has his proper real nature arise in full. He remains, he stands firm, and does not become slack through loss of support. For him, how could this course of worldly existence, which shakes the whole world and is contemptible as the continuity of birth, death, and so on, occur? It certainly does not occur, because its cause, namely his own impurity, is absent: this is the meaning.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre
children.translated_text: As it is said in the venerable <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s>:

children.text: tattve niścalacittas tu bhuñjāno viṣayān api
children.translated_text: One whose mind is motionless in reality, even while enjoying sense objects,

children.text: naiva saṃspṛśyate doṣaiḥ padmapattram ivāmbhasā ||
children.translated_text: is not touched at all by faults, like a lotus leaf by water.

children.text: viṣāpahārimantrādisaṃnaddho bhakṣayannapi
children.translated_text: Even while eating poison, one who is equipped with poison-removing mantras and the like

children.text: viṣaṃ na muhyate tena tadvadyogī mahāmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: is not bewildered by it; so too is the very wise yogin.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha ye śrutyantavidakṣapādamādhyamikādayaḥ kṣobhapralaye viśvocchedarūpam abhāvātmakameva tattvam avaśiṣyata ity upādikṣan tān pratibodhayituṃ tadupagatatattvaprātipakṣyeṇa lokottaratāṃ prakaraṇaśarīrasya spandatattvasya nirūpayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, those knowers of the end of the <s>śruti</s>, followers of <s>Akṣapāda</s>, <s>Mādhyamikas</s>, and others taught that, at the dissolution of agitation, only a reality consisting of absence, in the form of the cutting off of the universe, remains. In order to awaken them, he describes the extraordinary nature of the spanda principle, which is the body of the treatise, by opposing the reality they accept.

children.text: Chapter 11
asad evedam agra āsīt ||
children.translated_text: 'In the beginning this was non-existent alone.'

children.text: ityādyuktyā śrutyantavidādyabhimato 'bhāvo bhāvyatāṃ naiti bhāvanāyā bhāvyavastuviṣayatvād abhāvasya na kiṃcittvād bhāvyamānatāyāṃ vā kiṃcittve satyabhāvatvābhāvāt kiṃca bhāvakasyāpi yatrābhāvaḥ sa viśvocchedaḥ kathaṃ bhāvanīyaḥ bhāvakābhyupagame tu na viśvocchedo bhāvakasyāvaśiṣyamāṇatvād iti na viśvābhāva eva tattvam ||
children.translated_text: By statements such as this, the absence accepted by the knowers of the end of the <s>śruti</s> and others does not become an object of cultivation, because cultivation has an existent object to be cultivated, while absence is nothing at all. Or, if it is something to be cultivated, then, since it is something, its being absence is lost. Moreover, how is that world-annihilation, in which even the cultivator is absent, to be cultivated? But if a cultivator is admitted, there is no world-annihilation, because the cultivator remains. Therefore the mere absence of the universe is not reality.

children.text: atha kalpito 'yaṃ bhāvako viśvocchedaṃ vikalpakalpyamānaṃ bhāvayan bhāvanāpariniṣpattau bhāvyatādātmyād abhāvarūpaḥ sampadyata iti pakṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now suppose this is the position: this cultivator is imagined, and, cultivating the world-annihilation imagined by conceptual construction, when cultivation is completed he becomes of the nature of absence because of identity with what is cultivated.

children.text: tatrocyate tatrābhāvabhāvanāyāṃ nāmūḍhatā na ca tatrāsty amūḍhatā api tu moha evāsti
children.translated_text: To this it is said: in that cultivation of absence there is no non-delusion, nor is there any non-delusion there; rather, there is delusion alone.

children.text: yadyad evātibhāvyate
children.translated_text: Whatever indeed is intensely cultivated,

children.text: bhāvanāpariniṣpattau tatsphuṭaṃ kalpadhīphalam ||
children.translated_text: when cultivation is completed, that becomes manifest as the fruit of the imagining intellect.

children.text: iti nyāyād viśvocchedātmanyabhāve bhāvyamāne na kadācit paramārthāptir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: According to this principle, when absence in the form of world-annihilation is cultivated, there is never attainment of the supreme reality.

children.text: athocyate
children.translated_text: Now it may be said:

children.text: sarvālambanadharmaiś ca sarvatattvair aśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Empty of all properties that serve as supports, of all principles without remainder,

children.text: sarvakleśāśayaiḥ śūnyaṃ na śūnyaṃ paramārthataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and of all latent dispositions of affliction, it is not empty in the supreme sense.

children.text: iti nāgārjunoktam īdṛśaṃ tac chūnyamiti ||
children.translated_text: This kind of emptiness was stated by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.

children.text: satyaṃ yadi cidānandaghanā svatantrā pāramārthikī bhittibhūtā bhūr abhyupeyate yathā vijñānabhairavādau pārameśvarīṃ dikkālakalanātītā ||
children.translated_text: True, if an independent, supreme ground, a mass of consciousness and bliss, is accepted as the foundational plane, as in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s> and similar texts:

children.text: ityādinā pāramārthikīṃ bhittibhūtāṃ cidbhūmim avasthāpya śūnyabhāvanoktā anyathā na śūnyam iti śūnyaiveyam uktiḥ yadyad evātibhāvyate iti pratipāditatvāt ||
children.translated_text: 'The supreme divine one, beyond the measuring out of direction and time,' and so on: having established the supreme foundational ground, the plane of consciousness, the cultivation of emptiness is taught. Otherwise, the statement 'it is not empty' is itself empty, because it has been established that 'whatever indeed is intensely cultivated' becomes so.

children.text: yattu ||
children.translated_text: But as for this:

children.text: sāvasthā kāpy avijñeyā mādṛśāṃ śūnyatocyate
children.translated_text: 'Some state, unknowable to people like me, is called emptiness;

children.text: na punar lokarūḍhyeva nāstikyārthānupātinī ||
children.translated_text: but it is not the one that follows popular usage with the meaning of nihilism.'

children.text: ityālokamālāyām uktaṃ tat tu satyaṃ tvādṛśām avijñeyā avijñeyatvād vaktum aśakyety ucyatāṃ śūnyateti tu kutaḥ śūnyatāpi ca yāvad bhāvyate tāvad vikalpollikhitatvād asau vivejñaiya ||
children.translated_text: What is said in the <s>Ālokamālā</s> is true. Let it be said that for people like you it is unknowable, and because it is unknowable, impossible to describe; but why call it emptiness? And so long as even emptiness is cultivated, to that extent, because it is marked out by conceptual construction, it is knowable by discriminating people.

children.text: yadi ca tvādṛśāṃ sā jñātumaśakyā tat tatpadasākṣātkārābhijñasadgurusaparyā kāryā na tu śūnyateti svamanīṣikayaiva vyavahṛtyātmā paraś cāgādhe mahāmohe nikṣeptavya ityalam ||
children.translated_text: And if that state is impossible for people like you to know, then service should be rendered to a true guru who knows by direct realization that state itself; but one should not, by dealing with it merely through one's own cleverness as 'emptiness,' cast oneself and others into a deep, unfathomable delusion. Enough on this point.

children.text: atha kuto jñātaṃ tatra mūḍhatāstītyatrānenottaram āha yata iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, in response to the question, 'How is it known that there is delusion there?', he gives this answer: 'because.'

children.text: abhiyogaḥ samādhānotthitasya kīdṛgaham āsamiti tadavasthābhimukhavimarśātmābhilāpas tatsaṃsparśāt tadvaśāddhetos tad āsīd iti yato niścayaḥ gāḍhamūḍho 'ham āsam iti yato 'sti pratipattiḥ ato mohāvasthaiva sā kalpitā tathā smaryamāṇatvāt sā cānubhūyamānatvād anubhavituḥ pramātur avasthātṛrūpasya pratyuta sattām āvedayate na tv abhāvamiti viśvābhāvāvasthāyāṃ cidrūpasyākhaṇḍitameva rūpaṃ tiṣṭhatīti nāmuṣyābhāvo jātucid vaktuṃ śakyata ityuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The application of the question, "What was I like?" after one has risen from samādhi, is a verbal formulation whose nature is a reflective awareness turned toward that state. From contact with it, by its force, because of that cause, there is the certainty, "That was so"; because there is the cognition, "I was deeply deluded," that condition of delusion is therefore imagined in just that way, since it is remembered. And because it is experienced, it in turn makes known the existence of the experiencer, the knowing subject whose form is the one who abides in the state, not his non-existence. Thus, in the condition in which the universe is absent, the form of consciousness remains wholly unbroken; so it is impossible ever to say that this consciousness is absent. This is what has been stated.

children.text: nanu dṛṣṭaṃ niścitaṃ nīlādi smaryate na ca śūnyabhūtasya nyagbhūtabuddhivṛtter niścayo 'sti tat kathamuktaṃ tad āsīd ityauttarakālikān niścayān mūḍhatā seti ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, what is seen and ascertained, such as blue and the like, is remembered. In the case of one who has become void, whose activity of intellect is suppressed, there is no ascertainment. How then was it said that, from the later ascertainment "that existed," that condition was dullness?

children.text: ucyate vedyasyaiṣā gatiḥ yasmāt tadidaṃtāsāramidaṃtayā yāvatpramātrā svātmopāroheṇa na niścitaṃ tāvan na smaryate vedakastu kalpitaśūnyādyavasthāsu saṃkucito 'py asāṃketikāhaṃtāparamārtha eveti na tasya svātmani pṛthaktāstīti tanniścāyako vikalpaḥ ityahaṃvimṛśyam eva tadā svasaṃvedane naiva siddhaṃ śūnyapramātṛrūpaṃ viśvapratiyogitvāc ca saṃkocasāra ||
children.translated_text: The answer is this. Such is the course of what is to be known: since this object, whose essence is objectivity, is not remembered so long as it has not been ascertained as objective by a knowing subject through its mounting upon his own self. But the knower, even when contracted in imagined states such as emptiness, is in truth a non-conventional "I". Therefore there is no separateness for him from his own self. Thus the conceptual construction that ascertains him, whose object of reflection is "I," was at that time in self-awareness by no means established as the form of an empty knowing subject; and because it stands opposed to the universe, it has contraction as its essence.

children.text: saduttarakālaṃ smaryata iti na kācid anupapattir yasmād evamatas tac chūnyātmakaṃ padaṃ kṛtrimam tasmād bhūtamabhūtaṃ vā yad yad evātibhāvyate
children.translated_text: It is remembered afterward; therefore there is no inconsistency. For, since this is so, that state whose nature is emptiness is artificial. Therefore, whatever is intensely cultivated, whether real or unreal,

children.text: iti taduktayaiva nītyā abhūtabhāvanayaivotthāpitaṃ parameśvareṇaiva jñānagopanāyai mūḍhānām upeyatayā tathā bhāsitamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: according to the very principle stated in that saying, has been made to arise only through the cultivation of what is unreal; by the Supreme Lord himself, for the concealment of knowledge in the deluded, it has been made to appear in that way as something to be approached. This is the meaning.

children.text: jñeyaṃ jñātavyaṃ jñeyarūpaṃ ca sadā suṣuptavaditi dṛṣṭāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The example is that the knowable, what is to be known, and the form of the knowable are always like deep sleep.

children.text: ayaṃ bhāvaḥ sadā suṣuptaṃ moharūpamaprayāsasiddhaṃ sarvasyāstyeva tat kim anena samādhiprayatnopārjitenānyena śūnyena kṛtyaṃ dvayasyāpyavastutvāviśeṣād iti ||
children.translated_text: The idea is this: deep sleep, whose nature is delusion and which is attained without effort, is always present for everyone. What purpose is served by this other emptiness acquired through the effort of samādhi, since both are alike in being unreal?

children.text: prāyaścāsmin śūnye duruttare mahāmohārṇava eva vedāntavidakṣapādasāṃkhyasaugatādiprāyā bahavo 'nupraviṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And generally into this emptiness, which is hard to cross and is truly a great ocean of delusion, many have entered, especially knowers of the end of the <s>śruti</s>, followers of <s>Akṣapāda</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>Saugatas</s>, and others.

children.text: spandatattvasamāvivikṣūṇām api ca śithilībhūtaprayatnānāṃ śūnyam etad vighnabhūtam ||
children.translated_text: And for those who wish to enter completely into the spanda principle, but whose effort has become slack, this emptiness is an obstacle.

children.text: yadvakṣyati
children.translated_text: For he will say:

children.text: tadā tasminmahāvyomni ||
children.translated_text: "Then in that great ether,"

children.text: ityārabhya
children.translated_text: beginning thus,

children.text: sauṣuptapadavanmūḍhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "dull like the state of deep sleep,"

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: ata etaducchede granthakārasya mahān saṃrambho lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in cutting this off, a great urgency is seen on the part of the author of the treatise.

children.text: tathā ceha heyatayaiva tan nirṇīyāpi punarapi nirṇeṣyate
children.translated_text: And accordingly, here, although that has been determined only as something to be abandoned, it will again be determined

children.text: kāryonmukhaḥ prayatno yaḥ
children.translated_text: in the passage, "The effort that is intent on an effect,"

children.text: ityatra ||
children.translated_text: and there.

children.text: tato 'smābhir etaddūṣaṇārambhaḥ kṛta iti na naḥ kopaḥ kāryo 'trabhavadbhir upadeśanibhālanadattakarṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this undertaking to refute it has been made by us; so let no anger be directed at us by you honorable ones who have lent your ears to considering instruction.

children.text: saugateṣu dūṣiteṣu śrutyantavādādayo dūṣitā eva tulyanyāyatvād iti nābhyadhikam uktam ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Saugatas</s> have been refuted, those who propound the end of the <s>śruti</s> and the others are refuted as well, because the reasoning is the same. Thus nothing further has been said.

children.text: tadidānīṃ prakṛtameva brūmahe tattu spandākhyaṃ tattvamevamiti śūnyavan na smaryamāṇatvaṃ pratipadyate tasya sarvadānusyūtopalabdhrekarūpasya kadācid apy anupalabhyatvāyogāt ||
children.translated_text: Now we state only the matter at hand. But that reality called spanda is not subject, like emptiness, to being remembered in this way, because that one form, the ever-continuous perceiver, can never possibly be unperceived.

children.text: tathā cāhuḥ
children.translated_text: And accordingly they say:

children.text: vijñātāram ere kena vijānīyāt ||
children.translated_text: "By what could one know the knower?"

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yadyapi ca samāveśadaśā vyutthitena prāṇādisaṃskāravaśāt smaryate tathāpi na tāvadeva spandatattvamapi tu sarvānusyūtānavacchinnaprakāśānandasāraparapramātṛrūpam eva tat ||
children.translated_text: And although the condition of samāveśa, after one has emerged, is remembered through the force of latent impressions of breath and the like, still the spanda principle is not merely that much. Rather, it is precisely the form of the supreme knowing subject, whose essence is all-pervasive, uninterrupted light and bliss.

children.text: yadvakṣyati
children.translated_text: For he will say:

children.text: tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Therefore, in considerations of word and meaning, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: ato'syānavacchinnacamatkārarūpasya na jātucitsmaryamāṇatvaṃ mūḍhatvaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore for this, whose form is uninterrupted wonder, there is never any rememberedness or dullness.

children.text: yastu tattattvamitīha tacchabdenāsya nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ sa ||
children.translated_text: But the designation made here of it by the word "that," as "that reality,"

children.text: svātantryāmuktam ātmānam ||
children.translated_text: is in accord with the principle stated in the venerable <s>Pratyabhijñākārikā</s>, "the self freed into its own freedom,"

children.text: iti śrīpratyabhijñākārikoktanītyā kalpitasyaivāpāramārthikasvarūpasya na tu tattvataḥ pāramārthikasya ||
children.translated_text: and refers only to an imagined, non-ultimate form, not to what is ultimately real in truth.

children.text: na pratipadyata ityanenedam āha asya tattvasya smaryamāṇatvena pratītir eva nāstīti ||
children.translated_text: By saying "does not attain," he says this: there is no cognition of this reality as something remembered.

children.text: nanu yatra sthitamityādau cidrūpasyaiva viśvakāryarūpatāgrāhitvamuktaṃ taddhyānotthāpitaṃ kṛtrimamabhāvātmakaṃ rūpaṃ te naiva gṛhītamiti katham asyānavacchinnacamatkārarūpam amūḍhatvam ityāśaṅkāyām āha ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, in the passage beginning "where it is established," the form of consciousness itself was said to be the grasper of the form of the universal effect. You have not accepted that artificial, absence-like form brought forth by meditation. How then can this have the form of uninterrupted wonder and be non-dull? In answer to this doubt, he says:

children.text: Chapter 12

atra spandatattve kāryatvaṃ kartṛtvam iti ca śabditaṃ śabdavyavahāramātreṇa bheditamavasthāyugalamasti vastuto hi tadekameva svatantraprakāśaghanaśaṃkararūpaṃ tattvaṃ kartṛsattvāvyatiriktayā prakāśātmanā kriyayā vyāptaṃ tadabhedena prakāśamānaṃ tattvabhuvanaśarīratadabhāvādirūpatvaṃ svīkurvatkāryam ityucyate tadanyasya kasyāpi kāraṇatvāyogāt ||
children.translated_text: Here, in the spanda principle, the pair of states designated as effecthood and agency, differentiated merely by verbal usage, exists. In reality, that one principle alone, whose form is <s>Śaṃkara</s>, a compact mass of independent light, is pervaded by action whose nature is illumination and which is not distinct from the existence of the agent. Shining as non-different from that, and assuming the forms of the body of the worlds of reality and their absence and so on, it is called the effect, because nothing else can possibly be its cause.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīpratyabhijñāyām
children.translated_text: As has been said in the venerable <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>:

children.text: jaḍasya tu na sā śaktiḥ sattā yadasataḥ sataḥ
children.translated_text: But inert matter does not possess that power, since the existence of the non-existent, as existent,

children.text: kartṛkarmatvatattvaiva kāryakāraṇatā tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: is precisely the principle of being agent and object; from that comes the relation of effect and cause.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tasya cedameva kāryatvaṃ yadayaṃ vicitradeśakālādyābhāsasaṃyojanaviyojanakrameṇānantān dehanīlādyābhāsāṃś cidātmanaḥ svarūpād anatiriktān api mukurapratibimbavad atiriktān ivābhāsayati yāvac ca kiṃcidābhāsayati tat sarvam ābhāsyamānatvādeva bahirmukhena rūpeṇa kṣayadharmakaṃ kṣayaś cāsyedaṃtābhāsanimajjanenāhaṃtārūpatayāvasthānam ata eva dehādergrāhakasya yo vedyāṃśaḥ sa eva bhagavatā sṛjyate saṃhriyate ca na tv ahaṃtāprakāśātmakaṃ kartṛrūpaṃ tasya dehādyāveśe 'pi bhagavadekarūpatvāt atastatra tayoḥ kāryakartṛtvayor madhyāt kāryatā kṣayiṇī kartṛtvaṃ citsvātantryarūpaṃ punarakṣayaṃ jagadudayāpāyayor api tasya svabhāvād acalanāt ||
children.translated_text: And this alone is its being an effect: by the sequence of joining and separating appearances of varied place, time, and so on, it makes manifest countless appearances such as bodies and blue objects, which, though not distinct from the own nature of the self as consciousness, appear as if distinct, like reflections in a mirror. And so long as it manifests anything, all that, simply because it is being manifested, has a perishable nature in its outward-facing form. Its perishing is its resting in the form of I-ness by sinking into the appearance of this-ness. Therefore the knowable portion of the grasper of body and so on is what the Blessed One creates and withdraws, but not the agent-form whose nature is the light of I-ness, since even when it enters body and so on it has the single form of the Blessed One. Therefore, between those two, effecthood and agency, effecthood is perishable, while agency, whose nature is the freedom of consciousness, is imperishable, because even during the arising and disappearance of the world it does not move from its own nature.

children.text: calane tu jagadudayāpāyāv api na kaucic cakāsyātām iti mūḍhādyavasthāyām apy akhaṇḍitacamatkārasāram amūḍham evaitat ||
children.translated_text: But if it did move, the arising and disappearance of the world would not shine forth at all. Thus, even in states such as delusion, this is not deluded at all, since its essence is unbroken wonder.

children.text: nanv abhāvasamādhānaniṣpattau suṣuptādau cāsya kartṛtvaṃ nopalabhāmahe kvacidapi pravṛttyadarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, when the accomplishment of absorption into absence occurs, and in deep sleep and the like, we do not perceive its agency, because no activity is seen anywhere.

children.text: satyaṃ kāryonmukha indriyādipreraṇātmakavyāpārapravaṇo yaḥ prayatnaḥ saṃrambhaḥ so 'tra kāryakṣayapade lupyate vicchidyate tasmiṃl lupte sati abudho 'bhāvasamādhyapahāritātmarūpo mūḍho vilupto 'smīti manyate ||
children.translated_text: True. The effort or impulse that is turned toward activity, whose nature is the urging of the senses and so on toward effects, is lost here, in the state where effects have perished; it is cut off. When that has been lost, the unawakened person, deluded because his own nature has been carried off by absorption into absence, thinks, 'I have been lost.'

children.text: yaḥ punarantarmukho 'haṃtāprakāśarūpaḥ svabhāvo 'ta eva sarvajñatvaguṇasyāspadam upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat sarvakartṛtvāder api tasya lopo na kadācit syād bhavatīti na kadācidapi saṃbhāvanīyo 'nyasya tallopam upalabdhuḥ kasyāpy anupalambhāt yadi sa kaścid upalabhyate sa evāsāv antarmukhaś cidrūpo na ced upalabhyate tarhi sā lopadaśāstīti kuto niścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But that inward-facing own nature, whose form is the light of I-ness, and which for that very reason is the locus of the quality of omniscience, is an indication also of universal agency and the rest: its loss never occurs, nor could it ever be imagined. For there is no perception of anyone else who might perceive its loss. If someone is perceived, then that very one is this inward-facing form of consciousness; if he is not perceived, then how can there be certainty that there is a state of its loss?

children.text: atha cānyaḥ kaścit tallopaṃ nopalabhate 'pitu sa eva prakāśātmā tatkathaṃ tasyābhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: And if some other person does not perceive its loss, but rather that very self, whose nature is light, does, then how could there be its absence?

children.text: evaṃ cānyasyānupalambhanād ity atrānyakartṛkasyopalambhasyābhāvād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the phrase 'because another is not perceived' means: because there is no perception whose agent is another.

children.text: atha ca ghaṭābhāvo yathā ghaṭaviviktabhūtalādyupalambhanān niścīyate tathaivātmābhāvo 'pyātmaviviktasya kasyacid upalambhān niścīyeta tadupalambhakasattāvaśyambhāvinīti tadupalambhakasvātmanāstitā na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: And just as the absence of a pot is ascertained from the perception of a ground-surface and the like that is devoid of a pot, so too the absence of the self would have to be ascertained from the perception of something devoid of the self. But since that necessarily entails the existence of a perceiver of that thing, the non-existence of that perceiver's own self is not established.

children.text: yadi ca kāryonmukhaprayatnalope sa lupyeta tadottarakālam anyasya kasyāpyupalambho na bhavet anyopalambhābhāvaḥ prasajyetety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And if, when effort directed toward effects is lost, it too were lost, then afterward there would be no perception of anything else at all; the consequence would be the absence of any perception of another. This is the meaning.

children.text: api cānyasya bahirmukhasya prayatnasya sauṣuptādāv anupalambhāt katham antarmukhasya tattvasya bāliśair lopa āśaṅkito yato 'nyasya lope 'nyasya kiṃ vṛttam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, since another, outward-facing effort is not perceived in deep sleep and the like, how can childish people suspect the loss of the inward-facing principle? For when one thing is lost, what has happened to another?

children.text: atha cānyasya kāryonmukhaprayatnasyānupalambhād anupalambhaprakāśanān na kadācit prakāśātmano 'ntarmukhasya tasyopalabdhur lopaḥ yato 'sāv antarmukhobhāvaḥ sarvajñatvaguṇasyāspadaṃ tām apyabhāvadaśāṃ vettyeva anyathā saiva na sidhyediti ||
children.translated_text: And since there is non-perception of the other, effect-directed effort, and since non-perception itself is illuminated, there is never any loss of that inward-facing light-self, the perceiver. For that inward-facing existence, the locus of the quality of omniscience, knows even that state of absence; otherwise that state itself would not be established.

children.text: anyasyeti kartari karmaṇi ca ṣaṣṭhī ||
children.translated_text: In 'of another,' the genitive is used both for the agent and for the object.

children.text: antarmukhe kāryatvapratiyogitām iva kartṛtvasya sambhāvyāvasthātvam uktaṃ vastutastu uktayuktyā tasyāvasthātṛtvam eva ||
children.translated_text: With regard to what is inward-facing, agency has been described as something whose abiding might be supposed, just as effecthood is the counter-correlate of it. But in reality, by the reasoning already given, it alone is what abides.

children.text: antarmukha iti antaḥ pūrṇāhaṃtātmakaṃ mukhaṃ pradhānaṃ yasyeti yojyam ||
children.translated_text: 'Inward-facing' should be construed as: that whose face, that is, whose principal aspect, is inward, consisting of complete I-ness.

children.text: evam aprabuddho bahirmukhavyāpāranirodhe grāhakasyāpyātmano 'nupapannam apyabhāvaṃ niścinuta iti pratipādya suprabuddhāprabuddhayor yādṛg ātmopalambhastaṃ nirūpayati ||
children.translated_text: Having thus explained that the unawakened person, when outward-facing activity is stopped, wrongly determines the impossible absence even of the grasping self, he now sets forth what kind of perception of the self belongs to the well-awakened and to the unawakened.

children.text: Chapter 13

tasya prākaraṇikasvabhāvasya yopalabdhiḥ anavacchinnaḥ prakāśaḥ sā kathitayuktyavaṣṭambhāt suṣṭhu prabuddhasyāprabuddhatāsaṃskāreṇāpi śūnyasya satataṃ triṣvapi jāgarasvapnasauṣuptapadeṣu nityamiti ādau madhye'nte cāvyabhicāriṇī anapāyinī syādbhavatyeva sadāsau śaṃkarātmakasvasvabhāvatayā sphuratīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The perception of that own nature under discussion, that is, the unrestricted light, by support of the reasoning stated, is, for the well-awakened person, who is empty even of the impression of being unawakened, constant in all three states, waking, dream, and deep sleep; that is, it is always unfailing at the beginning, middle, and end. It necessarily exists, meaning that it always shines as his own nature whose essence is <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: parasyāprabuddhasya punastāsāṃ daśānāṃ svocitasaṃvidrūpāṇāṃ pratyekam ādāv udbubhūṣāyām ante ca viśrāntyātmakāntarmukhatve na tu svocitārthāvabhāsāvasthitirūpe madhyapade ||
children.translated_text: But for the other, the unawakened person, it is present in each of those states, which have the form of their own proper awareness, at the beginning, when they are about to arise, and at the end, when they are inward-facing in the form of repose, but not in the middle state, which consists in the abiding manifestation of their own proper objects.

children.text: yaduktaṃ śrīśivadṛṣṭau
children.translated_text: As has been said in the venerable <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>:

children.text: yāvat samagrajñānāgrajñātṛsparśadaśāsv api
children.translated_text: As long as, even in the states of contact with the knower at the forefront of complete knowledge,

children.text: sthitaiva lakṣyate sā tu tadviśrāntyāthavā phale ||
children.translated_text: it is perceived as steadily present, that is through repose in that, or through the fruit.

children.text: bhaṭṭalollaṭenāpi tadādyanta ityevameva vyākhyāyi svavṛttau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṭṭa Lollaṭa</s> too explained it in just this way in his own commentary: 'at the beginning and end of that.'

children.text: bhaṭṭaśrīkallaṭavṛttyakṣarāṇyapekṣya vayamapi tadvṛttyakṣarānurodhena sautram artham ativimalamapi kliṣṭakalpanayā vyākartumaśikṣitāḥ yata evāsuprabuddhasya tadādyante 'sti tadupalabdhiḥ ata evāyam ihādhikārī spandopadeśaiḥ suprabuddhīkriyate ||
children.translated_text: Having regard to the words of Bhaṭṭa Śrī Kallaṭa's commentary, we too, in conformity with the words of that commentary, are not trained to explain the sūtra's meaning, though extremely clear, by strained imagination. For that very reason, for one who is not fully awakened there is apprehension of it at its beginning and end; therefore this person, qualified here, is made fully awakened by the teachings on <s>spanda</s>.

children.text: yadvakṣyati
children.translated_text: As he will say:

children.text: ataḥ satatam udyuktaḥ spandatattvaviviktaye
children.translated_text: "Therefore, constantly intent upon discerning the <s>spanda</s> principle,

children.text: jāgrat
children.translated_text: waking..."

children.text: ityādi
children.translated_text: and so on;

children.text: sauṣuptapadavanmūḍhaḥ prabuddhaḥ syādanāvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: "Deluded as in the state of deep sleep, he would become awakened, unobscured,"

children.text: iti
children.translated_text: thus;

children.text: tathā svapne'pi
children.translated_text: and likewise, "even in dream..."

children.text: ityādi
children.translated_text: and so on;

children.text: prabuddhaḥ sarvadā tiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: "The awakened one should remain so at all times,"

children.text: ityādi ca ||
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: atra hi jāgarāditriṣu padeṣu ādyantakoṭivan madhyamapy arthāvasāyātmakaṃ padaṃ turyābhogamayaṃ kartuṃ prabuddhasya suprabuddhatāpādanāyopadeśaḥ pravṛttaḥ etac ca nirṇeṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For here, in the three states beginning with waking, the teaching has begun in order to produce complete awakening in the awakened one, making even the middle state, which consists in determination of objects, just like the beginning and end points, into a state filled with the enjoyment of the fourth. And this we shall determine.

children.text: tathā ca śivasūtram
children.translated_text: And accordingly the <s>Śivasūtra</s> says:

children.text: jāgratsvapnasuṣuptabhede turyābhogasambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "In the differentiation of waking, dream, and deep sleep, the enjoyment of the fourth arises."

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: triṣu caturthaṃ tailavad āsecyam
children.translated_text: "The fourth should be poured into the three like oil,"

children.text: iti
children.translated_text: thus;

children.text: tritayabhoktā vīreśaḥ
children.translated_text: "The enjoyer of the triad is the lord of heroes,"

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: suprabuddhasya triṣu padeṣu yādṛśy upalabdhis tāṃ vibhāgena darśayati ||
children.translated_text: He shows separately what kind of apprehension the fully awakened one has in the three states.

children.text: Chapter 14
suprabuddhasya bhūmnā jñānajñeyasvarūpayā madhyame pade jñānāgraparyantayos tu svasvarūpayaiva spandatattvātmanā parāśaktyā yukto vibhuḥ śaṃkarātmā svabhāvo jāgarāsvapnarūpe padadvaye bhāti ||
children.translated_text: For the fully awakened one, in the middle state, the all-pervading nature whose self is <s>Śaṃkara</s> shines broadly as having the form of knowledge and knowable object; but at the first and final limits of knowledge, in the two states consisting of waking and dreamless sleep, it shines only in its own form as the <s>spanda</s> principle, joined with supreme power.

children.text: tatra hi viśvamasau sadāśiveśvaravatsvāṅgavat paśyati tadanyatra tu suṣupte na tu yathānye suṣuptaturyayor iti tripadāvyabhicāriṇī iti prakrānte turyasyāprastutatvāt tadupalabdher eva ca turyarūpatvāt asau vibhuś cinmaya evāsya bhāti aśeṣavedyopaśamād ity etat suprabuddhābhiprāyam eva na tu vastuvṛttānusāreṇa tadanyatra tu cinmayaḥ ity asyānupapannatvāpatteḥ loke sauṣuptasya mohamayatvāt śivāpekṣayā tu jāgratsvapnayorapi cinmayatvāt evamapi ca prakṛtānupayuktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For there he sees the universe as his own limb, like <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>. Elsewhere, however, namely in deep sleep, it is not as it is for others in deep sleep and the fourth state. Thus, since the topic is that which does not deviate from the three states, since the fourth has not been introduced, and since that very apprehension has the form of the fourth, this all-pervading one appears to him as consciousness alone, because all knowable objects have subsided. This statement is intended only with reference to the fully awakened one, not according to the actual state of things; otherwise the phrase "elsewhere, however, as consciousness alone" would become inappropriate, since in ordinary life deep sleep is made of delusion, while from the standpoint of <s>Śiva</s> even waking and dream are made of consciousness. And even so, it would be irrelevant to the matter at hand.

children.text: itaḥ prabhṛti prathamaniḥṣyandānto granthaḥ prabuddhasya suprabuddhatāyai sthito yathā ṭīkākārairna cetitas tathā parīkṣyatāṃ svayameva kiyatpratipadaṃ likhāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From here up to the end of the first effusion, the text is established for the fully awakened state of the awakened one. Examine for yourself how this was not perceived by the commentators; how much can we write word by word?

children.text: yatheyaṃ jāgarādimadhyadaśāpi prabuddhaṃ na pratibadhnāti tathopapādayati ||
children.translated_text: He explains how even this middle condition beginning with waking does not obstruct the awakened one.

children.text: Chapter 15
guṇāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi yeṣāṃ prakṛtitattvaṃ vibhavabhūte māyātattvāvasthitā ihābhipretāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The guṇas are sattva, rajas, and tamas. Here what is intended is their prakṛti principle, situated in the māyā principle, which is the sphere of manifestation.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīsvacchande māyāmasūrakavinyāse
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Svacchanda</s>, in the arrangement of the demon Māyā:

children.text: adhaśchādanam ūrdhvaṃ ca raktaṃ śuklaṃ vicintayet
children.translated_text: "One should conceive the lower covering and the upper as red and white;

children.text: madhye tamo vijānīyādguṇās tv ete vyavasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the middle one should know darkness; these guṇas are established."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: ta ādayo yeṣāṃ kalādīnāṃ kṣityantānāṃ spandānāṃ viśeṣaprasarāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ye niḥṣyandāstanukaraṇabhuvanaprasarāḥ nīlasukhādisaṃvidaś ca tathā yogyapekṣayā bindunādādayas te satataṃ jñasya suprabuddhasya kasyacid evāpaścimajanmano 'paripanthinaḥ svasvabhāvācchādakā na bhavantīti niścayaḥ yatas te sāmānyaspandamuktarūpam āśritya yatra sthitam ityatra nirṇītadṛśā labdhātmalābhās tata evotpannās tanmayāś cetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those whose beginning is these, namely the special expansions of <s>spanda</s> from kalā and the rest down to earth; their effusions, the expansions of body, instrument, and world, and consciousnesses such as blue and pleasure, and likewise, depending on the qualified person, bindu, nāda, and the like: these, for the knowing one, for the fully awakened person, for a certain one whose birth is not final, are never opponents and do not conceal his own nature. This is certain, because they have obtained their own being through the vision determined in the statement "where it is established," relying on the common form freed by <s>spanda</s>; from that very source they have arisen and are made of that.

children.text: tathāhi
children.translated_text: For so it is:

children.text: svāṅgarūpeṣu bhāveṣu patyurjñānaṃ kriyā ca yā
children.translated_text: "The knowledge and action of the Lord in entities that are forms of his own limbs

children.text: māyātṛtīye ta eva paśoḥ sattvaṃ rajastamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are, when māyā is the third, precisely sattva, rajas, and tamas for the bound soul."

children.text: iti śrīpratyabhijñoktadṛśā citiśaktireva pārameśvarī jñānakriyāmāyāśaktitritayatayā śrīsadāśivādipade sphuritvā saṃkocaprakarṣātsattvarajastamorūpaṃ krīḍāśarīraṃ śrayati yato nijacicchaktisphāramayatvāt tadadhiṣṭhitameva sarvadā sarvaṃ jānan suprabuddho guṇādiviśeṣaspandān anucchindann api spandatattvāveśamaya eva ||
children.translated_text: Thus, according to the view stated in the venerable <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, the power of consciousness itself, belonging to the Supreme Lord, flashes forth in the venerable states beginning with <s>Sadāśiva</s> as the triad of knowledge-power, action-power, and māyā-power; then, through the intensity of contraction, it assumes a play-body in the form of sattva, rajas, and tamas. Therefore the fully awakened one, always knowing everything as grounded in that because it consists in the expansion of his own consciousness-power, remains immersed in the <s>spanda</s> principle even though he does not cut off the special movements beginning with the guṇas.

children.text: yathā tv aprabuddhān badhnanty ete tat pratipādayati ||
children.translated_text: Now he explains how these bind the unawakened.

children.text: Chapter 16

aprabuddhadhiyaḥ prāyaḥ sarvān apratyabhijñātapārameśvarīśaktyātmakanijaspandatattvān dehātmamānino laukikān prāṇādyātmābhimāninaś ca mitayoginas tv ete pūrvoktā guṇādispandaniḥṣyandāḥ svasyāḥ spandatattvātmanaḥ sthiteḥ sthaganāyodyatā nityaṃ tadudyamaikasārāḥ duḥkhenottāryante 'smād daiśikair jantucakramiti duruttāre laṅghayitum aśakye ghore duḥkhamaye saṃsaraṇamārge pātayanti ||
children.translated_text: These previously mentioned effusions of <s>spanda</s> beginning with the guṇas cast most people whose intellects are unawakened, who have not recognized the <s>spanda</s> principle of their own nature as the power of the Supreme Lord, worldly people who identify the body as self and limited yogins who identify the self with breath and the like, into the terrible, painful path of transmigration, hard to cross and impossible to overleap. They are always intent only on the effort to cover their own state whose nature is the <s>spanda</s> principle; the circle of creatures is lifted out from this with difficulty by teachers.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīmālinīvijaye
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Mālinīvijaya</s>:

children.text: viṣayeṣveva saṃlīnānadho'dhaḥ pātayantyaṇūn
children.translated_text: "Sunk only in sense objects, they cast the atomic souls lower and lower;

children.text: rudrāṇūnyāḥ samāliṅghaya ghorataryo 'parāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: embracing the <s>Rudra</s>-atomic souls, they are remembered as the other, more terrible powers."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tathā hi pūrvaṃ pratipāditā yeyaṃ spandatattvātmā parāśaktiḥ saiva viśvasyāntarbahiś ca vamanāt saṃsāravāmācāratvāc ca vāmeśvarīśaktiḥ tadutthāpitāni tu khecarīgocarīdikcarībhūcarīrūpāṇi catvāri devatācakrāṇi suprabuddhasya parabhūmisaṃcārīṇi aprabuddhānāṃ tu adharādharasaraṇiprerakāṇi ||
children.translated_text: For thus: that supreme power, whose nature is the spanda principle and which was previously explained, is itself the power of <s>Vāmeśvarī</s>, because it emits the universe both inwardly and outwardly and because worldly existence is a leftward course. But the four circles of deities, raised up by her and having the forms of <s>khecarī</s>, <s>gocarī</s>, <s>dikcarī</s>, and <s>bhūcarī</s>, move in the supreme plane for the fully awakened, while for the unawakened they impel lower and still lower paths.

children.text: tathā hi yā eva suprabuddhasya khe bodhagagane carantyaḥ khecaryo 'kālakalitatvābhedasarvakartṛtvasarvajñatvapūrṇatvavyāpakatvaprathāhetavas tā evāprabuddhasya śūnyapramātṛpadacāriṇyaḥ kañcukarūpatayā sthitāḥ kālakalitatvakiṃcitkartṛtākiṃcijjhatābhiṣvaṅganiyamahetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For thus: the very <s>khecarīs</s> that, for the fully awakened, move in the sky, the firmament of cognition, and are causes of the manifestation of freedom from temporal limitation, non-difference, universal agency, omniscience, fullness, and pervasiveness, are for the unawakened those that move in the station of the empty subject; standing in the form of sheaths, they are causes of temporal limitation, slight agency, slight knowledge, attachment, and restriction.

children.text: gaur vāk tadupalakṣitāsu saṃjalpamayīṣu buddhyahaṃkāramanobhūmiṣu carantyo gocaryaḥ suprabuddhasya svātmābhedamayādhyavasāyābhimānasaṃkalpāñ janayanti mūḍhānāṃ tu bhedaikasārān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Go</s> means speech. The <s>gocarīs</s>, moving in the domains indicated by it, namely intellect, egoity, and mind, which consist of discursive speech, produce in the fully awakened determinations, self-conceptions, and intentions made of non-difference from one's own self; but in the deluded they produce those whose sole essence is difference.

children.text: dikṣu daśasu bāhyendriyabhūmiṣu carantyo dikcaryaḥ suprabuddhasyādvayaprathāsārāḥ anyeṣāṃ dvayaprathāhetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>dikcarīs</s>, moving in the ten directions, that is, in the domains of the external sense faculties, have as their essence the manifestation of non-duality for the fully awakened, while for others they are causes of the manifestation of duality.

children.text: bhūrūpādipañcakātmakaṃ meyapadaṃ tatra carantyo bhūcaryas tadā bhogamayyā āśyānībhāvatayā tanmayatvamāpannāḥ bhūcaryaḥ suprabuddhasya citprakāśaśarīratayātmānaṃ darśayantya itareṣāṃ sarvato 'py avacchinnatāṃ prathayantyaḥ sthitāḥ ity evaṃ pramātrantaḥkaraṇabahiṣkaraṇaprameyarūpatayaiva tāni catvāri cakrāṇi guṇādispandamayāny aprabuddhabuddhīṃl laukikāṃs tathā bindunādādiprathāmātrasaṃtuṣṭān yoginas tattattvaprasararūpe saṃsāre pātayanti ||
children.translated_text: The object-domain is made of the five beginning with form. Moving there, the <s>bhūcarīs</s>, when they have become identical with it through the coagulated condition of enjoyment, show themselves to the fully awakened as having the body of the light of consciousness, while for others they stand manifesting limitation on every side. Thus those four circles, precisely in the forms of subject, inner instrument, outer instrument, and object of knowledge, and consisting of spanda beginning with the guṇas, cast unawakened, worldly-minded people, and also yogins content merely with manifestations such as bindu and nāda, into worldly existence, whose form is the diffusion of the respective principles.

children.text: yata evam ||
children.translated_text: Because this is so:

children.text: Chapter 17
uktavakṣyamāṇarūpasya spandatattvasya viviktaye vimarśanāya satatam udyuktaḥ
children.translated_text: one who is constantly intent on discriminating and reflectively examining the spanda principle in the form already stated and still to be stated,

children.text: mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate ||
children.translated_text: 'those who, fixing the mind on me, worship me, ever disciplined,'

children.text: iti gītoktadṛśā satatam evāntarmukhasvarūpanibhālanapravaṇo yaḥ sa jāgradeva jāgarāvasthāsthita eva nijamātmīyaṃ śaṃkarātmakaṃ svasvabhāvam acireṇādhigacchati tathā asya śaṃkarātmā āntaraḥ svabhāvaḥ svayam evonmajjati yena prabuddho nityoditasamāveśāsādanāt suprabuddho jīvanmukto bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the manner stated in the <s>Gītā</s>, is always inclined to behold his inward-facing nature. Such a person, even while awake, that is, while remaining in the waking state, soon attains his own real nature, which consists of <s>Śaṅkara</s>. Likewise, his inner nature as <s>Śaṅkara</s> rises up of itself; awakened by this, through attaining the ever-arisen absorption, he becomes fully awakened, liberated while living: this is the meaning.

children.text: yathāsyodyuktasya balavadālambanavaśoditānāyāsatadanyasakalavṛttikṣayamayīṣu niyatāsu yāsvavasthāsu spandanidhānam unmudritam abhimukhībhūtam āste tā etāḥ prathamam udyogasya viṣayā ityupadeṣṭum āha ||
children.translated_text: In order first to teach which states are the objects of that effort for one who is intent in this way, namely those fixed states in which, by the force of a powerful support, the repository of spanda stands opened, facing him, and all other activities have effortlessly perished as soon as they arise, he says:

children.text: Chapter 18

sarvatra tāvad upāyamārge samastetaravṛttipraśamapūrvam ekāgrībhavanti yoginaḥ etāsvatikrodhādyavasthāsu svarasata eva samastāparavṛttikṣayamayīṣu yadi spandatattvaviviktaye satatam udyukto jhaṭity antarmukhībhavanti yoginas tatsamīhitam acireṇaiva labhante ||
children.translated_text: Everywhere on the path of means, yogins first become one-pointed after all other activities have been calmed. If, in these states such as extreme anger, which by their own force consist in the destruction of all other activities, yogins who are constantly intent on discerning the spanda principle suddenly turn inward, they obtain what they desire very soon indeed.

children.text: ayoginastvatra mūḍhā eveti tātparyam ||
children.translated_text: The purport is that non-yogins here remain deluded.

children.text: tathāhi samanantaravihitadāruṇopaghātaśatrudarśanān marmasparśitattadvacanākarṇanād vā prathamam evonmiṣatsaṃjihīrṣādevatābalād antarmukhībhavadraśmicakro 'tikruddhaḥ ciraprārthitaprāṇeśīvadanendudarśanād eva tatkṣaṇam evonmajjatpūrṇābhilāṣadevatāvaśavikāsitānudhāvatsamastakaraṇacakraḥ prahṛṣṭo vā balavadātatāyibalena sarvato valitatvāt kāndiśīkaḥ kiṃ karomīti mṛśan vikalpayan saṃśayadhārādhirohātmani pade 'nupraviṣṭaḥ kṣīṇasakalālambanavikasatsaṃśayasaṃvinnirālambanīkṛtavṛttiprasaro vā mattavāraṇādyanubadhyamāno dhāvan śarīranirapekṣam eva svātmapravaṇīkṛtetaravṛttiprasaradudyogadevīpreraṇayātitvaritapalāyanakriyāviṣṭo vā evam anyāsv apy evamprāyāsu siṃhājagarādyavalokanajanitamahātrāsādyavasthāsu yad vṛttikṣayātmakaṃ padaṃ gacched adhitiṣṭhet spandatattvaviviktaye satatam udyukto yo yogijanas tasya tatra vṛttikṣayātmake pade 'vasthāviśeṣe spandaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ spandatattvam abhimukhībhūtameva tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for example, an extremely angry person, because of the power of the deity of the wish to destroy that first flashes forth after he has seen an enemy who has just inflicted a terrible injury or after he has heard the enemy's words touching a vital point, has the circle of his rays turning inward. Or a delighted person, merely from seeing the moon-face of his long-desired beloved, has that very instant the whole circle of his instruments expanded and running after it under the control of the deity of full desire arising within him. Or, hemmed in on all sides by the force of powerful assailants, he is terrified, thinking and imagining, 'What shall I do?', and has entered the state whose nature is mounting the stream of doubt, with all supports exhausted and the spread of activity rendered supportless by an unfolding awareness of doubt. Or, being chased by a rutting elephant and the like, he runs, possessed by an extremely swift act of flight through the impulse of the goddess of effort, which turns the spread of other activities toward the self without regard for the body. Likewise in other states of this kind, such as great terror produced by seeing a lion, a python, and so on, whatever station whose nature is the destruction of activities he might reach and occupy: for the yogin who is constantly intent on discerning the spanda principle, there, in that station whose nature is the destruction of activities, in that particular state, spanda is established; the spanda principle remains directly facing him.

children.text: tasmād etad vṛttikṣayapadaṃ saṃcetya jhaṭiti kūrmāṅgasaṃkocayuktyā krodhasaṃśayavṛttīḥ praśamayya mahāvikāsavyāptiyuktyā vā praharṣadhāvanavṛttīr visphāryābhimukhībhūtanijaspandaśaktivimarśavatā yoginā bhayam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, having become aware of this station in which activities are destroyed, the yogin who reflectively attends to his own spanda power now facing him should instantly calm activities such as anger and doubt by the method of contracting like the limbs of a tortoise, or should expand activities such as joy and running by the method of great unfolding and pervasion; and fear...

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīvijñānabhairave
children.translated_text: As is stated in the venerable <s>Vijñānabhairava</s>:

children.text: kāmakrodhalobhamohamadamātsaryagocare
children.translated_text: In the sphere of passion, anger, greed, delusion, pride, and jealousy,

children.text: buddhiṃ nistimitāṃ kṛtvā tat tattvam avaśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: having made the intellect motionless, that reality alone remains.

children.text: ānande mahati prāpte dṛṣṭe vā bāndhave cirāt ||
children.translated_text: "When great joy has been reached, or when a relative long absent has been seen,

children.text: ānandam udgataṃ dhyātvā tallayas tanmanā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: having contemplated the joy that has arisen, one should become absorbed in it and have one's mind fixed on it.

children.text: kṣutādyante bhaye śoke gahvare vāraṇadrute
children.translated_text: At the end of sneezing and the like, in fear, in grief, in a cave, or when fleeing from an elephant,

children.text: kutūhale kṣudhādyante brahmasattā samīpagā ||
children.translated_text: in curiosity, or at the end of hunger and the like, the state of <s>brahman</s> is near at hand."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: evam etāsv avasthāsūktayuktyā prathamaṃ spandaśaktiṃ pariśīlya tadanu tām evānusaṃdadhat sarvāsvavasthāsu taddārḍhyānupraveśamayīṃ jīvanmuktatām āharet satatodyukta ityupadiśati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having first examined the <s>spanda</s>-power in these states by the reasoning that has been stated, and then continually attending to that very power, one should bring about liberation while living, consisting in firm entrance into it in all states. This is what he teaches by saying that one should be constantly intent.

children.text: Chapter 19

ayaṃ śaṃkarātmā svabhāvo yan mama vakṣyati abhivyaktaṃ sat yac cidānandaghanam anubhūtapūrvaṃ svarūpaṃ māṃ vimarśayiṣyati tadavaśyamahaṃ kariṣye bahirmukhatāṃ hitvā tatpravaṇa eva bhaviṣyāmi iti saṃkalpya niścitya yām atikrodhādyavasthāsv anubhūtacarīṃ cidānandaghanāṃ spandātmikām avasthām avalambya prāpyatvenābhisaṃdhāya tiṣṭhati śamitavikalpagatim avikalpām avasthām avicalatvena bhajate yo yogī tadīyāṃ tāmavasthāṃ samāśritya candrasūryau apānaḥ prāṇaś cobhāv api hṛdayabhūmau militvā yugapadeva sauṣumne'dhvani brahmanāḍyām ūrdhvamārgeṇodānapathenāstamitaḥ śāmyataḥ kathaṃ brahmāṇḍalakṣaṇaṃ gocaraṃ hitvā brahmabilādhiṣṭhātṛbrahmādhiṣṭhitamaṇḍaṃ muktvā ūrdhvakavāṭāntāṃ dehavyāptiṃ tyaktvā tadā collaṅghitadehavyāptike 'ta eva prakarṣeṇa līnāv uktarūpau śaśibhāskarau yatra tasmin mahāvyomni niḥśeṣavedyopaśamarūpe paramākāśe prāpte 'pi yaḥ śithilaprayatnatayā khecaryādyātmanā guṇādispandaniḥṣyandena vyāmohitatvāt sauṣuptapadavad bhavati sauṣuptena ca suptamapy upalakṣitaṃ tena ca svapnasuṣuptavat yaḥ śūnyādibhūmim evādhitiṣṭhati sa yogī samyaganabhivyaktasvasvabhāvo mūḍha ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Having resolved and determined, "This nature whose self is <s>Śaṃkara</s>, which he will state as mine, when it becomes manifest, will make me reflect upon my own form, previously experienced, compact with consciousness and bliss; therefore I shall certainly do that, abandoning outward-facingness and becoming devoted only to it," the yogin remains by relying on, and intending as something to be attained, that state which he has already experienced in states such as extreme anger, which is compact with consciousness and bliss and whose self is <s>spanda</s>; he steadfastly abides in the non-conceptual state in which the movement of thought-constructs has been pacified. Taking refuge in that state belonging to him, the moon and sun, that is, apāna and prāṇa, both meet in the ground of the heart and at the same time set out upward in the suṣumṇā path, the <s>brahman</s>-channel, by the upward way, the path of udāna, and come to rest. How? Having left behind the sphere characterized as the cosmic egg, having abandoned the sphere governed by <s>Brahmā</s>, the presiding deity of the <s>brahman</s>-aperture, and having given up the bodily pervasion ending at the upper door, then, when bodily pervasion has been transcended, precisely because those moon and sun of the stated kind are intensely dissolved in that great ether, the supreme space whose nature is the complete pacification of all knowable objects, even after that has been reached, if through slackness of effort, being bewildered by an effusion of spanda such as the guṇas in the form of <s>khecarī</s> and the rest, he becomes as if in the state of deep sleep, and by deep sleep sleep also is implied, and likewise dream, then the yogin who remains only on a plane such as emptiness is said to be deluded, because his own true nature has not been properly manifested.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrībhaṭṭakallaṭena
children.translated_text: As venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa</s> has said:

children.text: yāṃ spandātmikām avasthām avalambya
children.translated_text: "Relying on the state whose self is <s>spanda</s>,

children.text: iti yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of yogins..."

children.text: iti ca
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: yasya svasvabhāvābhivyaktir na samyak vṛttā sa svapnādinā muhyamāno 'prabuddho niruddhaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: "He whose manifestation of his own nature has not occurred properly, being bewildered by dream and the like, would be unawakened and checked."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yastu tatrāpi prayatnapāṭavād udyantṛtābalāt kṣaṇamapi na śithilībhavati sa tamasānabhibhūtatvāt cidākāśamayatvenaivāvasthitaḥ prabuddha ucyate ata eva satatodyogavataiva yoginā bhavitavyam ityādiṣṭaṃ gurubhiḥ iti śivam ||
children.translated_text: But one who, even there, through skill in effort and the strength of rising agency, does not become slack even for a moment is not overcome by darkness; remaining as made only of the ether of consciousness, he is called awakened. Therefore the teachers have instructed that the yogin must indeed be constantly energetic. Thus all is auspicious.

children.text: Chapter 20

tat spandatattvātmakaṃ balaṃ prāṇarūpaṃ vīryamākramya abhedena āśrayatayāvaṣṭabhya bhagavanto 'nantavyomavyāpyādayo mantrāḥ sarvajñabalena sarvajñatvādisāmarthyena ślāghamānā jṛmbhamāṇā adhikārāya dehināṃ pravartante sṛṣṭisaṃhāratirodhānānugrahādi kurvantītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The blessed mantras, beginning with those whose pervasion is the infinite ether, take possession of that power, the strength whose self is the <s>spanda</s> principle and whose form is prāṇa, and, holding it as their support in non-difference, they expand and glory in the power of omniscience, that is, in capacities such as omniscience, and proceed for the sake of authority over embodied beings; the meaning is that they perform creation, dissolution, concealment, grace, and so on.

children.text: sarvajñaśabdo bhāvapradhānaḥ sarvakartṛtvādy upalakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: The word "omniscient" has the state or capacity as its primary sense, and it implies omnipotence and the like.

children.text: yathā dehināṃ karaṇāny upapāditadṛśā tadbalamākramya viṣayaprakāśādau pravartante iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as the instruments of embodied beings, in the way already established, take possession of that power and proceed in acts such as illuminating objects, so this is the example.

children.text: tathā nirañjanāḥ kṛtakṛtyatvān nivṛttādhikāramalāḥ śāntaviśiṣṭavācakātmasvarūpās tatraiva spandātmake bale samyagabhedāpattyā prakarṣeṇāpunarāvṛttyā līyante adhikamalānmucyante ārādhakacittena upāsakalokasaṃvedanena saha ||
children.translated_text: So too, being stainless, since their task has been accomplished and the impurity of limited authority has ceased, and having as their own form the self that expresses the peaceful and the distinguished, they are dissolved there itself, in the power whose self is <s>spanda</s>, through complete attainment of non-difference, intensely and without return; they are freed from the impurity of limited agency, together with the mind of the worshipper, that is, with the awareness of the community of practitioners.

children.text: yathoktam
children.translated_text: As it has been said:

children.text: anugṛhyāṇusaṃghātaṃ yātāḥ padam anāmayam ||
children.translated_text: "Having bestowed grace on the aggregate of atomic souls, they have gone to the stainless state."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yataśca tata evoditāstadbalena visṛṣṭās tatraiva līyante tenaite mantramantreśvarādayaḥ śivasya parameśvarasya sambandhī dharmaḥ svabhāvo vidyate yeṣāṃ te tathā sāmānyaspandasārā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since, for that very reason, they arise from that power, are emitted by that power, and are dissolved back into that very power, these mantras, lords of mantras, and so on are such that the <s>dharma</s>, the nature, belonging to <s>Śiva</s>, the Supreme Lord, exists in them; that is, their essence is the common <s>spanda</s>.

children.text: nanu karaṇānāṃ mantrāṇāṃ ca tat udayādau tulye kimiti karaṇāni na sarvajñādirūpāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Objection: since the instruments and the mantras are alike in having their arising and so forth from that, why are the instruments not omniscient and the like?

children.text: ucyate parameśvaro māyāśaktyā śarīrakaraṇāni bhedamayāni nirmimīte vidyāśaktyā tv ākāśīyavicitravācakaparāmarśaśarīrān mantrān ||
children.translated_text: The answer is given: the Supreme Lord, through the power of māyā, fashions bodies and instruments as consisting of difference; but through the power of vidyā he fashions mantras whose bodies are the varied expressive reflections belonging to the ether.

children.text: vācakasya māyāpade 'pi ||
children.translated_text: Even in the domain of māyā, with regard to the expresser:

children.text: ghaṭo 'yam ityadhyavasā nāmarūpātirekiṇī
children.translated_text: "The determination 'this is a pot,' which is beyond name and form,

children.text: pareśaśaktirātmeva bhāsate na tv idaṃtayā ||
children.translated_text: shines as the power of the Supreme Lord, like the self, and not as objectivity."

children.text: iti pratyabhijñoktanītyā pramātṛbhūmyanatikrānter na śarīrapuryaṣṭakādivadbodhasaṃkocakatvam astīti yuktamevaiṣāṃ sarvajñatvādi ||
children.translated_text: According to the principle stated in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, because the expresser does not pass beyond the ground of the knower, it does not contract consciousness as do the body, the eightfold subtle body, and the like; therefore omniscience and the like are entirely appropriate for these mantras.

children.text: etac ca
children.translated_text: And this matter,

children.text: bhede tv ekarase bhāte ||
children.translated_text: "But when difference shines as one single essence..."

children.text: iti śrīpratyabhijñākārikāṭīkāyāṃ vitatya darśitam ||
children.translated_text: has been shown at length in the venerable commentary on the <s>Pratyabhijñākārikā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ vidyāpadāvasthitasṛṣṭyādikāryanantabhaṭṭārakādyapekṣayaitad vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: In this way this should be explained with reference to <s>Anantabhaṭṭāraka</s> and the others, whose function is creation and so on and who are established in the state of vidyā.

children.text: tathā dīkṣādipravṛttānām ācāryādīnāṃ karaṇarūpāḥ sarve mantrās tatspandatattvarūpaṃ balam ākramya anuprāṇakatvena avaṣṭabhya ācāryādīnām eva sambandhinārādhakacittena saha mokṣabhogasādhanādyadhikārāya pravartante tatraiva śāntavācakaśabdātmakaśarīrarūpā ata eva ca nirañjanāḥ śuddhāḥ samyak pralīyante viśrāmyanti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, all mantras, which function as instruments for teachers and others engaged in initiation and similar rites, lay hold of the power whose nature is that spanda principle and, supporting it as that which animates them, proceed for the authority to accomplish liberation, enjoyment, and the like, together with the mind of the worshipper connected with those very teachers and others. There itself, having the form of a body made of the word that denotes the pacified state, they are therefore stainless and pure; they completely dissolve and come to rest.

children.text: atra vyākhyāne sahārādhakacittena iti pūrvaślokena yojyam ||
children.translated_text: In this explanation, the phrase "together with the mind of the worshipper" is to be connected with the preceding verse.

children.text: evaṃ ca mantrāṇāmudayapralayakoṭivyāpi pravṛttāv api bhittibhūtamiti abhihitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been stated that this is the foundation even when the mantras function throughout the limits of arising and dissolution.

children.text: evaṃ ca daśāṣṭādaśādibhedena bhinne śaive mantrāṇāṃ spandatattvasārataivetyuktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus it follows that, although Śaiva mantras differ as ten, eighteen, and so on, they have the spanda principle as their essence.

children.text: evaṃ mantramantreśvarādirūpā śuddhābhimatā sṛṣṭiḥ śivasvabhāveti pratipādyādhunā aśuddhābhimatāpi sā māyādirūpā śivasvarūpaiva iti upapādayan śrīmataśāstrādirahasyadṛṣṭim api upakṣipati ||
children.translated_text: Having thus taught that the creation regarded as pure, in the form of mantra, mantreśvara, and so on, has the nature of Śiva, he now establishes that even the creation regarded as impure, in the form of māyā and the rest, is itself Śiva's own form, and he also introduces the secret view of the venerable scriptures and the like.

children.text: Chapter 21

yato jīvo grāhakaḥ sarvamayaḥ śivavad viśvarūpaḥ tena hetunā śabdeṣu vācakeṣu artheṣu vācyeṣu cintāsu vikalpajñānādirūpāsu ādimadhyāntarūpā sāvasthā nāsti yā śivo na bhavati sarvameva śivasvarūpam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the individual soul, the apprehending subject, consists of everything and, like Śiva, has the universe as its form, for that reason there is no state, having the form of beginning, middle, or end, among words as denoters, among meanings as denoted objects, or among thoughts in the form of conceptual cognition and so on, which is not Śiva. The meaning is that everything is indeed Śiva's own form.

children.text: yataś caivamato bhoktaiva cidātmā grāhako bhogyabhāvena dehanīlādirūpeṇa sadā nityaṃ sarvatra vicitratattvabhuvanādipade samyaganūnādhikatayā sthitaḥ na tu bhogyaṃ nāma kiṃcidbhoktur bhinnam asti ||
children.translated_text: And because this is so, the enjoyer alone, the consciousness-self as apprehender, is always and everywhere established in the form of the enjoyed, such as the body, blue, and so on, in the realm of the manifold principles and worlds, in a complete way, neither deficient nor excessive. There is not any so-called enjoyed object different from the enjoyer.

children.text: jīva ityupakramya śiva ityupasaṃhāreṇa jīvaśivayorvāstavo na ko 'pi bhedaḥ iti dehādyavasthāsu na kāsucid apyapūrṇamanyatā mantavyā api tu cidghanaśivasvabhāvataiveti bhaṅgyopadiśati ||
children.translated_text: By beginning with "individual soul" and concluding with "Śiva," he teaches in an indirect manner that there is no real difference at all between the individual soul and Śiva, and that in states such as embodiment one should not think there is any incompleteness or otherness, but rather only the nature of Śiva as a mass of consciousness.

children.text: yathoktam śarīramapi ye ṣaṭtriṃśattattvamayaṃ śivarūpatayā paśyanti arcayanti ca te sidhyanti ghaṭādikam iva tathābhiniviśya paśyanti arcayanti ca te 'pīti nāstyatra vivādaḥ iti śrīpratyabhijñāṭīkāyām ||
children.translated_text: As has been said in the venerable <s>Pratyabhijñāṭīkā</s>: "Those who see and worship even the body, made of the thirty-six principles, as having the form of Śiva, attain perfection; and there is no dispute here that those who, having fixed themselves in that way, see and worship a pot and the like also attain it."

children.text: bhaṭṭaśrīvāmanenāpyuktam
children.translated_text: And <s>Bhaṭṭaśrīvāmana</s> too has said:

children.text: ālambya saṃvidaṃ yasmāt saṃvedyaṃ na svabhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: "Since the knowable object rests on consciousness and not on its own nature,

children.text: tasmātsaṃviditaṃ sarvamiti saṃvinmayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: therefore everything that is known must be made of consciousness."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: kasmāt jīvaḥ sarvamayaḥ ityatra hetuḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ samudbhavād utpattihetutvāt apādānabhāvapradhānaśca nirdeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for the question, "Why is the individual soul made of everything?", the reason is: because all entities arise from it, since it is the cause of their production. The statement chiefly indicates its status as the material source.

children.text: pramātṛmitimānameyamayabhedajātasya te vihāra iha hetutāṃ samupayāti yasmāt tvayi
children.translated_text: "Since, in you, the multitude of differences made of knower, cognition, means of knowledge, and object of knowledge

children.text: nivṛttavivṛtau kvacit tad apayāti tenādhvādhunā nayena punarīkṣyate jagati jātucitkenacit ||
children.translated_text: comes to be the cause of your play here, and, when contraction and expansion cease somewhere, that too disappears, therefore the world is at any time seen again by someone through the present path."

children.text: iti śrījñānagarbhastotroktanītyā saṃvidyeva prasṛtāyāṃ jagataḥ sadbhāvāt sarvabhāvasamudbhavatvaṃ jīvasya yataśca jīvādeva udayati viśvamato'yaṃ sarvamayo viśvaśaktiriti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: Thus, according to the principle stated in the venerable <s>Jñānagarbhastotra</s>, because the world exists when consciousness alone has expanded, the individual soul has the quality of being the source from which all entities arise; and because the universe arises from the individual soul alone, this soul is made of everything, that is, it possesses the power of the universe.

children.text: nirṇītaṃ caitad dvitīyasūtravṛttau ||
children.translated_text: And this has been determined in the commentary on the second sūtra.

children.text: sarvamayatve hetvantaramāha tatsaṃvedana ityardhena ||
children.translated_text: With the half-verse beginning "in its cognition," he states another reason for its being made of everything.

children.text: tasya sarvasya nīlasukhāderyatsaṃvedanaṃ prakāśastena rūpeṇa svabhāvena tādātmyapratipatteḥ sarvamayatvasyopalambhāt ||
children.translated_text: The cognition, the illumination, of all that, such as blue and pleasure, belongs to it; because identity with it is apprehended in that form and nature, its being made of everything is perceived.

children.text: evamanena ślokadvayena rahasyacaryāḥ sarvabhedapādaponmūlopapattiparighaṭitāś ca jñānopadeśakathāḥ prathamacaramasūtrābhyāṃ mahārthatattvaṃ jāgradādisūtreṇa ṣaḍardhaparamārthaḥ tadākramya ity anena sarvopāsāsāratetyādyupakṣiptam iti spandatattvenaiva viśvopadeśāḥ svīkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by these two verses, the teachings on knowledge concerning the secret practice, furnished with the establishment that uproots all the trees of difference, the great reality through the first and last sūtras, the supreme meaning of the six-and-a-half through the sūtra on waking and the other states, and, through the phrase "having laid hold of that," the essence of all worship and so forth, have been introduced. In this way all teachings concerning the universe are accepted precisely through the spanda principle.

children.text: athaitatpratipattisārataiva mokṣa ityādiśati ||
children.translated_text: Now he teaches that the very essence of the realization of this is liberation.

children.text: Chapter 22
vāśabdaḥ prathamaniḥṣyandoktanimīlanasamādhiprakāraṃ vikalpayan asyāḥ samāpatter durlabhatāṃ dhvanayati ||
children.translated_text: The word "or" suggests an alternative to the type of closed-eyed absorption mentioned in the first effusion, and indicates the rarity of this attainment.

children.text: tenāyamarthaḥ īdṛśī tāvatsaṃvittiḥ durlabhā yasya kasyacid evāpaścimajanmano bhavati so 'khilaṃ jagatkrīḍātvena paśyan nijasaṃvidunmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ sṛjan saṃharaṃś ca
children.translated_text: Therefore the meaning is this: such awareness is indeed rare; it belongs only to some person whose birth is not final. Seeing the entire world as play, and creating and withdrawing it through the opening and closing of his own consciousness,

children.text: mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate ||
children.translated_text: "Those who, fixing the mind on me, worship me, ever disciplined,"

children.text: iti sthityā satatasamāviṣṭo mahāyogī jīvann eva prāṇādimān api vijñānāgninirdagdhāśeṣabandhano dehapāte tu śiva eva jīvaṃścedṛṅmukta eva na tu kathaṃcid api baddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in accordance with this condition, the great yogin who is constantly absorbed, even while living and possessing the vital breaths and the like, has all his bonds burned by the fire of knowledge. At the fall of the body he is Śiva himself; and if he lives, he is liberated in just this way. He is not bound in any manner at all.

children.text: na saṃśayaḥ ityanena idaṃ dhvanayati dīkṣādinā gurupratyayato muktiḥ īdṛśāt tu jñānāt samācārādvā svapratyayata eveti ||
children.translated_text: By the words "there is no doubt," he suggests this: through initiation and the like, liberation comes from trust in the guru; but from such knowledge, or from conduct based on it, liberation comes from one's own certainty itself.

children.text: iyameva mahāsamāpattiḥ sādhakācāryādīnām abhīṣṭaprāptihetuḥ iti ślokadvayenāha ||
children.translated_text: This very great attainment is the cause of attaining what is desired for practitioners, teachers, and others; he states this in two verses.

children.text: Chapter 23
