iha śivo bhūtvā śivaṃ yajet iti yad udghoṣyate tatra dhyāyinaś cetasi saṃvedane tasyeti na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ iti pratipāditaśivasvabhāvasya dhyeyasya anyasya vā kasyacit tattatsiddhihetor mantradevatāviśeṣasya ayam evodayaḥ prakaṭībhāvaḥ yā sādhakasya dhyāturācāryādeḥ
children.translated_text: Here, when it is proclaimed, "Having become <s>Śiva</s>, one should worship <s>Śiva</s>," in that case, in the awareness of the meditator, this very arising, this manifestation, belongs to that object of meditation whose nature as <s>Śiva</s> has been taught by the statement, "There is no state which is not <s>Śiva</s>," or else to some particular mantra-deity that is the cause of the accomplishment in question, and it belongs to the practitioner, the meditating teacher, and so on.

children.text: tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, among words, meanings, and thoughts there is no state which is not <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: iti pratipāditarūpā tadātmatāsamāpattiḥ śivaikyāveśo na tu pañcavaktrādervyatiriktasyākārasya darśanaṃ na tu niścayamātreṇa tadātmatāsamāpattiḥ api tu icchato 'vikalpaviśvāhaṃtātmakaśivaikyarūpecchāparāmarśādhirūḍhasya ||
children.translated_text: Thus what has the form just taught is attainment of absorption in identity with that, entry into unity with <s>Śiva</s>; it is not the vision of some form distinct from the five-faced one and the like. Nor is attainment of identity with that brought about by mere certainty, but rather for one who desires, that is, for one who has mounted the reflective awareness of desire whose form is unity with <s>Śiva</s> as the nonconceptual universal I-consciousness.

children.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati ahameva tatsaṃvedanarūpeṇa tādātmyapratipattito viśvaśarīraś cidānandaghanaḥ śiva iti saṃkalpo yasyāvikalpaśeṣībhūtatvena phalati tasya dhyeyamantradevatādi kiṃ na nāma abhimukhībhavati sarvasyaitadadvayaprathālagnatvāt ||
children.translated_text: This is what is meant: for the person whose resolve, "I myself, by attaining identity with that in the form of awareness, am <s>Śiva</s>, having the universe as my body and being a compact mass of consciousness and bliss," bears fruit by becoming subordinate to the nonconceptual, what object of meditation, mantra, deity, and so forth would not become manifest? For everything is attached to this nondual manifestation.

children.text: yathoktamasmatparameṣṭhipādaiḥ
children.translated_text: As our revered supreme teacher has said:

children.text: sākṣādbhavanmaye nātha sarvasmin bhuvanāntare
children.translated_text: "O Lord, when everything within the worlds is directly made of you,

children.text: kiṃ na bhaktimatāṃ kṣetraṃ mantraḥ kvaiṣāṃ na sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: what is not a sacred field for the devoted? What mantra of theirs does not become effective?"

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: iyameva ca samāpattiḥ paramādvayarūpasyāmṛtasya prāptiḥ anyasmiṃs tv amṛte katipayakālaśarīradārḍhyadāyini prāpte'pi sādhakairmaraṇamavaśyamavāpyata evety evakārāśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this very absorption is the attainment of the nectar whose form is supreme nonduality. As for any other nectar, even when it has been attained and gives bodily firmness for a certain time, death is necessarily reached by practitioners; such is the purport of the restrictive particle "alone."

children.text: evaṃ sarvatrānenaivāśayena śrīsvacchande sthūladṛṣṭyāmṛtaprāptiprakaraṇe
children.translated_text: Thus, everywhere with this same intention, in the venerable <s>Svacchanda</s>, in the section on the attainment of nectar from the gross viewpoint,

children.text: naiva cāmṛtayogena kālamṛtyujayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: "By the yoga of nectar alone there would be no conquest of time and death,"

children.text: ityuktyopasaṃhṛtya tāttvikas tatprāptiprakāraḥ
children.translated_text: having concluded with this statement, the true manner of attaining that is then taught:

children.text: athavā paratattvasthaḥ sarvakālairna bādhyate ||
children.translated_text: "Or, abiding in the supreme reality, one is not obstructed by any times,"

children.text: ityādinā ||
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: sarvaṃ śivaśaktimayaṃ smaret ||
children.translated_text: "One should remember everything as made of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>."

children.text: iti madhyena
children.translated_text: Through this middle passage,

children.text: jīvann eva vimukto 'sau yasyeyaṃ bhāvanā sadā
children.translated_text: "He is liberated while still living, he for whom this contemplation is always present.

children.text: yaḥ śivaṃ bhāvayen nityaṃ na kālaḥ kalayettu tam
children.translated_text: Time does not measure the one who constantly contemplates <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: yogī svacchandayogena svacchandagaticāriṇā
children.translated_text: The yogin, by the <s>Svacchanda</s> yoga that moves with free motion,

children.text: sa svacchandapade yuktaḥ svacchandasamatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: being joined to the state of <s>Svacchanda</s>, attains equality with <s>Svacchanda</s>.

children.text: svacchandaścaiva svacchandaḥ svacchando vicaret sadā ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Svacchanda</s> himself, as <s>Svacchanda</s>, always moves freely."

children.text: ityanena sahajasaṃdarbheṇa sapraśaṃsaṃ paścādupadiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With this natural sequence it was later taught together with praise.

children.text: ayamevātmano graho jñānaṃ yaducyate ātmā jñātavya iti tatredam eva sarvajñasarvakartṛsvatantraśivasvarūpatayā pratyabhijñānam ātmano jñānaṃ na tu
children.translated_text: This very apprehension of the self is the knowledge that is spoken of in the statement, "The self is to be known." There, this recognition of the self precisely as the form of <s>Śiva</s>, omniscient, maker of all, and free, is knowledge of the self, and not

children.text: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam ||
children.translated_text: "The person alone is all this,"

children.text: iti śrutyantaviduktam
children.translated_text: as stated by those who know only another end of scripture.

children.text: ta ātmopāsakāḥ sarve na gacchanti paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: "All those who worship the self do not go to the supreme state,"

children.text: ityāmnāyokteḥ ||
children.translated_text: according to the statement of scripture.

children.text: tathā dīkṣāvasare yojanikādyarthamayameva śiṣyātmano'nugrahaḥ imāmeva samāpattiṃ vidvānācāryaḥ śiṣyātmānaṃ śive yojayannācāryo bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, at the time of initiation, for the purpose of conjunction and the like, this very thing is the grace bestowed upon the self of the disciple. The meaning is that the learned teacher becomes a teacher by joining the disciple's self to <s>Śiva</s> through this very absorption.

children.text: iyaṃ svapratyayasiddhā putrakādeḥ śivātmanaḥ sadbhāvasya pāramārthikasvarūpasya dāyinī nirvāṇadīkṣā ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>nirvāṇa-dīkṣā</s> (initiation into liberation), established by one's own experience, which bestows on the novice and others the real nature, the ultimate reality, of being whose self is <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: yathoktam
children.translated_text: As has been said:

children.text: evaṃ yo veda tattvena tasya nirvāṇadāyinī
children.translated_text: "For one who knows thus in truth,

children.text: dīkṣā bhavatyasaṃdigdhā tilājyāhutivarjitā ||
children.translated_text: the initiation that bestows liberation is certain, even without offerings of sesame and ghee."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: hautrī dīkṣāpi dīkṣaiva tatra mā bhūt kasyacid anāśvāsa ityāśayenātraivakāro na kṛtaḥ śrīmahāgurupravareṇeti śivam ||
children.translated_text: Fire-offering initiation too is indeed initiation; so that no one should lack confidence in it, the venerable great guru did not use the restrictive particle "only" here. Thus all is auspicious.

children.text: Chapter 24

dhatte sarvamātmanīti dhātā śaṃkarātmā svabhāvaḥ sa yathā jāgrataḥ jāgarāyāmabhivyaktasvasvātantryasya dehino dehabhūmikāmeva prakaṭībhūtapiṇḍasthajñānasya yoginaḥ sambandhinyecchayābhyarthito 'ntarmukhasvarūpavimarśabalena prasādito hṛdi cetasi sthitānarthāniti bindunādādijñānapuraḥ kṣobhapratibhācālanabodhastobhajñānasaṃcārādiprayojanāni sampādayati ||
children.translated_text: Because it holds everything in itself, it is called the supporter: this nature, whose self is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, when requested by the will belonging to the embodied yogin who is awake, whose own freedom has become manifest in the waking state, whose knowledge abiding in the body has become manifest, and who occupies the plane of the body, and when propitiated by the force of inward reflection on its own nature, accomplishes the aims situated in the heart, in consciousness: the disturbance of bindu and nāda and the other knowledges, flashes of inspiration, movement, awakening, expansion of knowledge, transmission of knowledge, and the like.

children.text: kathaṃ somasūryayor jñānakriyāśaktyor udayaṃ kṛtvā jñānaśaktyā bhāsyamānaṃ hi tattatkriyāśaktyonmīlyate ||
children.translated_text: How so? Having brought about the rise of the moon and sun, that is, of the powers of knowledge and action, what is illumined by the power of knowledge is indeed unfolded by the corresponding power of action.

children.text: samāveśonmiṣatpratibhātmakamūlāvaṣṭambhayuktisphāritajñānakriyāvyāptisārasavyetaramarīcivisphāraṇakrameṇa tattadvedhasaṃkramaṇādi sampādayati yogiśarīrānupraviṣṭaḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Supreme Lord, having entered the yogin's body, accomplishes the various penetrations and transitions by the process of expanding the right and left rays, whose essence is the pervasion of knowledge and action expanded by the method grounded in the root that consists of inspiration opening through absorption.

children.text: yathā caivaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: And as this is so, likewise:

children.text: anāgatāyāṃ nidrāyāṃ vinaṣṭe bāhyagocare
children.translated_text: "When sleep has not yet come and the external field has disappeared,

children.text: sāvasthā manasā gamyā parā devī prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: that state, accessible to the mind, shines forth as the supreme goddess."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: pīnāṃ ca durbalāṃ śaktiṃ dhyātvā dvādaśagocare
children.translated_text: "Having meditated on the power as full and as weak in the sphere of the twelve,

children.text: praviśya hṛdaye dhyāyan svapnasvātantryam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: and entering into the heart while meditating, one obtains autonomy in dream."

children.text: iti sampradāyasthityā vamanagrāsasaktatadubhayavisargāraṇicitiśaktiparāmarśamukhena nityaṃ praṇayam anatikrāmato bhagavatprārthanāparasya yoganidrārūḍhasya sphuṭataram anācchāditarūpatayā madhye sauṣumnadhāmani sthito dhātā svapne 'pyabhīṣṭān evāṇavaśāktaśāmbhavasamāveśādīn anyān api samāveśābhyāsarasonmṛṣṭamatimukurasya jijñāsitān arthān avaśyaṃ prakaṭīkaroti nāsya yoginaḥ svapnasuṣuptayor vyāmoho bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, through the stability of the tradition, by way of reflective awareness of the power of consciousness as the araṇi-fire-sticks that emit, ingest, cling to, and release both, the creator who does not transgress constant devotion, who is intent on prayer to the Blessed Lord, and who is established in yogic sleep, standing in the middle, in the channel of <s>suṣumṇā</s>, with his nature quite clearly uncovered, necessarily makes manifest, even in dream, the desired absorptions of the atomic, śākta, and śāmbhava kinds, and also other objects which he has wished to know, for the mirror of his mind has been cleansed by the savor of repeated practice of absorption. The meaning is that there is no bewilderment for this yogin in dream or deep sleep.

children.text: svapnena sauṣuptam apyupalakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: Deep sleep too is indicated by the word "dream."

children.text: atrābhīṣṭārthaprakāśe āvṛttyā ayameva hetuḥ praṇayasya prārthanāyā antarmukhasvarūpapariśīlanopāsāsaṃpādyasya māyākāluṣyopaśamalakṣaṇasya prasādasya bhagavatānatikramāt ||
children.translated_text: Here, in the manifestation of the desired object, by repetition this very cause is stated: because the Lord does not transgress the favor that is devotion and prayer, produced by the worship that is repeated cultivation of one's inward-facing own nature, and characterized by the pacification of the impurity of māyā.

children.text: parameśvaro hi cidātmā yady antarmukhocitasevākrameṇārthyate tat tat saṃpādayata eva jāgrataḥ iti paratattve jāgarūkasya jāgarāvasthāsthasya ceti śleṣoktyā vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: For the Supreme Lord, whose nature is consciousness, if he is entreated according to the proper order of inward-facing service, surely accomplishes whatever is requested for one who is awake. Thus this is to be explained by a double meaning: one who is awake to the supreme reality, and one who is situated in the waking state.

children.text: yadi punarevaṃ sāvadhāno na bhavati tadā nāsya yogitetyāha ||
children.translated_text: But if, on the other hand, he is not attentive in this way, then, saying that there is no yoginhood for him, he states:

children.text: Chapter 25

yadyuktayuktyā nityaṃ nārādhyate dhātā tadā svasvarūpasthityabhāve satataṃ pratyahaṃ laukikasyeva cāsya yogino 'pi jāgarāyāṃ svapne ca sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇārthaprakāśanatanniścayanādisvabhāvā pārameśvarī sṛṣṭiḥ svatantrā syāllaukikavadyoginam api saṃsārāvaṭa evāsau pātayed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the creator is not worshipped constantly by the method that has been stated, then, when there is no abiding in one's own nature, the divine creation, which by its nature manifests both ordinary and extraordinary objects and brings about determination of them and so on, would be independent every day, constantly, in the waking state and in dream, for this yogin too, just as for an ordinary person; like an ordinary person, it would cast even the yogin down into the pit of saṃsāra. This is the meaning.

children.text: yathoktam
children.translated_text: As has been said:

children.text: pravṛttir bhūtānāmaiśvarī
children.translated_text: "The activity of beings is divine,"

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: thus.

children.text: taddharmakatvataḥ iti svapnajāgarādipadaprakāśane bhagavatsṛṣṭeḥ svātantryasvabhāvād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Because it has that nature" means: because the Lord's creation, in manifesting states such as dream and waking, has independence as its own nature.

children.text: evaṃ svapnasauṣuptanirdalanopāyaṃ svaprabuddhatāyai saṃsādhya spandatattvasamāveśopāyaṃ suprabuddhasya dṛṣṭāntayuktipūrvakaṃ nirūpayati jijñāsitārthajñaptir apītthaṃ bhavatītyādiśati ||
children.translated_text: Having in this way established the means for crushing dream and deep sleep for the sake of full awakening to oneself, he now expounds, with an example and reasoning, the means of absorption in the <s>spanda</s> principle for one who is fully awakened, and indicates that knowledge of the object one wishes to know also occurs in this way.

children.text: Chapter 26
hiśabdaḥ kilaśabdārthe ||
children.translated_text: The word <s>hi</s> has the sense of the word <s>kila</s>, "indeed."

children.text: sāvadhāne'pi cetasi dūratvādidoṣair yathā kilārtho 'sphuṭo dṛṣṭo bhūyo 'dhyakṣanirīkṣaṇātmanā svabalodyogena bhāvito bhṛśam ālokito na kevalaṃ sphuṭo yāvat sphuṭataro'pi bhāti tathā yatspandatattvātmakaṃ balaṃ yenānandaghanatātmanā paramārthena yatreti śaṃkarātmani svasvabhāve yatheti abhedavyāptyā sthitaṃ tatkartṛ tatheti svabalodyogena antarmukhatadekātmatāpariśīlanaprayatnena saṃbhāvitaṃ śīghrameva sphuṭataratvena pravartate abhivyajyate ||
children.translated_text: Just as, even when the mind is attentive, an object seen unclearly because of faults such as distance, when cultivated by one's own vigorous effort in the form of repeated direct inspection, that is, when intensely observed, appears not merely clear but even clearer, so the power whose self is the <s>spanda</s> principle, by which it is situated in its own nature, the self of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, in the form of the mass of bliss, the supreme reality, through non-different pervasion, quickly comes forth, that is, becomes manifest with greater clarity, when it is considered and cultivated in that way by one's own vigorous effort, by the effort of inward cultivation of identity with that alone.

children.text: kathamākramyārādhakasya kalpitadehādipramātṛbhūmiṃ svātmanyeva nimagnāṃ kṛtvātha ca spandātmakaṃ balamākramya sthitasya kalpitadehabuddhipramātṛbhūmim asakṛd uttejayataḥ sādhakasya yogino yajjijñāsitaṃ nidhānādi yatra deśādau yena hemādinā paramārthena yathā saṃniveśena sthitaṃ tathā tadacirād eva prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: How? Having taken possession of the worshipper's imagined ground as the knower constituted by the body and the like, and having caused it to sink into one's own self, and then, for the practicing yogin who stands having taken possession of the power whose nature is <s>spanda</s> and who repeatedly stimulates the imagined ground of the knower constituted by body and intellect, whatever he has wished to know, such as a treasure, in whatever place and the like, with whatever supreme reality such as gold, and in whatever arrangement it is situated, that very thing is soon revealed in that way.

children.text: kartṛśaktyādir apyamuta eva balāt prādurbhavatītyāha ||
children.translated_text: He says that the power of agency and the like also arise from that very power:

children.text: Chapter 27

yathā kṣīṇadhātur ṛṣiprāyaḥ so 'pi spandātmakaṃ balam ākramya spandasamāveśabalena prāṇapramātṛbhūmim asakṛd uttejya kārye 'vaśyakartavye karmaṇi pravartate aśakyam api vastu tadbalākramaṇenaiva karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as one whose bodily elements are depleted, almost like a seer, taking possession of the power whose nature is <s>spanda</s>, by the strength of absorption in <s>spanda</s>, and repeatedly stimulating the ground of the knower as prāṇa, proceeds in the task, the action that necessarily must be done; the meaning is that he does even an impossible thing precisely by taking possession of that power.

children.text: tathā yo 'pyatibubhukṣitaḥ so 'pi tadbalākrāntyā kṣutpipāsādi śamayati ||
children.translated_text: So too one who is extremely hungry, by the possession of that power, pacifies hunger, thirst, and the like.

children.text: na hi cidghanāṃ bhūmim anupraviṣṭasya dvaṃdvābhibhavaḥ kaścit prāṇādibhuva eva tadāśrayatvāttasyāś ceha cidbhūmau nimagnatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For one who has entered the ground that is a mass of consciousness is not overcome by any pair of opposites, since those depend only on grounds such as prāṇa, and since that ground has here sunk into the ground of consciousness.

children.text: yata evam uktasūtropapattikramānusāreṇedṛk siddhisamudāyo 'smād bhavatītyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because, according to the sequence of reasoning based on the sūtra just stated, such a collection of perfections arises from this, therefore:

children.text: Chapter 28

anena svasvabhāvātmanā spandatattvenādhiṣṭhite vyāpte dehe sati yathā tadavasthocitārthānubhavakaraṇādirūpāḥ sarvajñatāsarvakartṛtādayo dharmā āvirbhavanti dehinaḥ tathā yadyayaṃ kūrmāṅgasaṃkocavat sarvopasaṃhāreṇa mahāvikāsayuktyā vā svasminnanapāyinyātmani cidrūpe adhiṣṭhānaṃ karoti uktābhijñānapratyabhijñāte tatraiva samāveśasthitiṃ badhnāti tadā sarvatreti śivādau kṣityante evam iti śaṃkarataducitasarvajñatāsarvakartṛtādirūpo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: When the body is presided over and pervaded by this <s>spanda</s> principle whose self is one's own nature, just as qualities such as omniscience and omnipotence, consisting in the capacity to experience and act with respect to objects appropriate to that state, arise for the embodied one, so, if this person, like a tortoise withdrawing its limbs, by complete withdrawal of everything, or by the method of great expansion, establishes himself in his own imperishable self, whose form is consciousness, and binds his state of absorption there alone, in the recognition already known and recognized, then everywhere, from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth, he will become exactly such, that is, having the form of <s>Śaṅkara</s> and of the omniscience, omnipotence, and other qualities appropriate to him.

children.text: idam apyetatprasādenetyāha ||
children.translated_text: He says that this too occurs by that grace:

children.text: Chapter 29

mnā sarvakeśānāmāspadaṃ tataśca dehe yā glāniḥ arthāddehābhimāninaḥ puṃso yo harṣakṣayo'sau viluṇṭhikā parasaṃviddraviṇāpahāreṇa pārimityadaurgatyapradā tasyāśca glāner ajñānataś cidānandaghanasvasvarūpāpratyabhijñānāt sṛtir udbhavo 'vasthitiśca ||
children.translated_text: The seat of all miseries is thus in the body; and the weariness that occurs in the body, that is, the loss of joy belonging to a person who identifies with the body, is the plunderer. By stealing the wealth of supreme consciousness it bestows poverty in the form of limitation. And that weariness arises and persists from ignorance, that is, from non-recognition of one's own nature as a compact mass of consciousness and bliss.

children.text: tadajñānaṃ pradarśayiṣyamāṇasvarūpeṇonmeṣarūpeṇa cedviluptaṃ nikṛttaṃ tadāsau glānirajñānātmano hetorabhāvāt kutaḥ syānna bhaved ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If that ignorance, in the form whose nature is about to be shown, namely in the form of <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening of awareness), is erased and cut away, then since the cause whose nature is ignorance is absent, from where could that weariness arise? It would not arise; this is the meaning.

children.text: glānyabhāve ca dehe 'vaśyambhāvinyo vyādhyādisaṃtāpāvasthā api yathā yathā yogino 'pakṛṣyante tathā tathā hemna ivātitāpyamānasya kālikāpagame svasvarūpaṃ dedīpyata eva ||
children.translated_text: And when weariness is absent, even states of bodily affliction, such as diseases, which necessarily occur in the body, as they are progressively reduced for the yogin, cause his own nature to shine forth more and more, just as gold, when intensely heated, shines out once its blackness has departed.

children.text: evaṃ ca dehāvasthitasyāpi sarvadā glānyabhāva eva parayogino vibhūtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, even while he remains in the body, the very absence of weariness at all times is the power of the supreme yogin.

children.text: yathoktaṃ paramayoginyā madālasayā bāladārakān prayogīkurvatyā
children.translated_text: As was said by the supreme yoginī <s>Madalasā</s>, when instructing her young sons:

children.text: tvaṃ kañcuke śīryamāṇe nije'smin dehe heye mūḍhatāṃ mā vrajethāḥ
children.translated_text: "When this own garment, the body that is to be abandoned, is decaying, you should not fall into delusion.

children.text: śubhāśubhaiḥ karmabhir dehametanmadādibhiḥ kañcukaste nibaddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This body, this garment of yours, has been bound by good and bad actions, by intoxication and the rest."

children.text: iti mitasiddhyabhilāṣiṇo yoginaḥ samāveśābhyāsarasena dehaṃ vidhyato valīpalitādivyādhijayo bhavatītyapi bhaṅgyānena pratipāditam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by this indirect explanation, it has also been taught that for a yogin who desires limited accomplishments, and who pierces the body with the flavor of repeated practice of absorption, there is conquest over disease, wrinkles, gray hair, and the like.

children.text: atha yo 'yam unmeṣaḥ sa kiṃsvarūpaḥ kim upāyalabhyaś cety ākāṅkṣāyām āha ||
children.translated_text: Now, when the question arises, "What is this <s>unmeṣa</s>, and by what means is it obtained?", he says:

children.text: Chapter 30
bhāve tyakte niruddhā cinnaiva bhāvāntaraṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: "When an object has been abandoned and consciousness, being checked,

children.text: tadā tanmadhyabhāvena vikasatyatibhāvanā ||
children.translated_text: does not pass to another object, then, by the state in between them, exceedingly intense contemplation unfolds."

children.text: iti nītyā ekasyāṃ kasyāṃcid ālambanaviśeṣanibhṛtavikārātmikāyāṃ cintāyāṃ prasaktasya ekāgrībhūtasya yogino yata iti tadekāgratāprakarṣollasatsaṃvitsphāratas tadālambananimīlanājjhaṭiti grastasamastacintāsaṃtater agnīṣomāvibhedātmanaḥ spandatattvādapara evodayaściccamatkārātmānya eva lokottara ullāsaḥ syāt sa taccamatkāronmeṣakatvād evonmeṣo vijñātavyo 'nveṣaṇīyaḥ ittham eva yoginā jñātuṃ śakyaḥ tataśca svayamiti idaṃtāviṣayatvābhāvād akṛtakaprayatnātmanāvadhānenāhaṃtayaivopetyātmani lakṣayet asādhāraṇena camatkārātmanā pratyabhijānīyāt ||
children.translated_text: According to this principle, a yogin who has become concentrated, being absorbed in some one thought whose nature is a modification closely bound to a particular support, may, because of the expansion of consciousness flashing forth through the intensity of that one-pointedness, and because the support then closes, have the whole stream of thought suddenly swallowed up. From the <s>spanda</s> principle, whose nature is the non-difference of fire and soma, there arises an extraordinary emergence, a marveling of consciousness itself, a distinct supramundane delight. This should be understood and sought as <s>unmeṣa</s>, precisely because it opens that marvel. It can be known by the yogin only in this way. Therefore, he should mark it in himself by himself: since it is not an object of 'this-ness,' it is approached as 'I-ness' through attention whose nature is unconstructed effort, and is recognized as an uncommon marvel.

children.text: yata ekasyāṃ viṣayavicārādicintāyāṃ prasaktasya aparasyāś cintāyā jhaṭityudayaḥ syāt sa cintādvayavyāpaka unmeṣaḥ ityanye ||
children.translated_text: Others say: when one is absorbed in a single thought such as reflection on an object, and another thought suddenly arises, that <s>unmeṣa</s> is what pervades the two thoughts.

children.text: idānīṃ mitayogijanaprayatnasādhyāsvapi tāsu tāsu siddhiṣūnmeṣaṇapariśīlanamātroditāsu parayogino heyatvam eva mantavyam ityādiśati ||
children.translated_text: Now he instructs that, for the supreme yogin, those various attainments, even though attainable by the effort of limited yogins and produced merely by the cultivation of <s>unmeṣa</s>, are to be regarded only as things to be abandoned.

children.text: Chapter 31

ata unmeṣād upalakṣyamāṇād apralīyamānasthūlasūkṣmādidehāhambhāvasya yogino 'cireṇaiva bhrūmadhyādau tārakāprakāśarūpo bindur aśeṣavedyasāmānyaprakāśātmā nādaḥ sakalavācakāvibhediśabdanarūpo 'nāhatadhvanirūpo rūpamandhakāre 'pi prakāśanaṃ tejaḥ rasaśca rasanāgre lokottara āsvādaḥ kṣobhakatvena spandatattvasamāsādanavighnabhūtatāvatsaṃtoṣapradatvena vartante ||
children.translated_text: From that discernible <s>unmeṣa</s>, for a yogin whose sense of 'I' in the gross and subtle bodies has not dissolved, there soon arise, at the point between the brows and so forth, a bindu in the form of starlike light, a nāda whose nature is the general illumination of all knowable things, an unstruck sound in the form of a word not different from all denoters, illumination even in darkness, and a taste, a supramundane savor at the tip of the tongue. Because they agitate him, they act as obstacles to the attainment of the <s>spanda</s> principle, while also granting a certain satisfaction.

children.text: yadāhuḥ
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: te samādhāv upasargā vyutthāne siddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: "In samādhi they are disturbances; in emergence they are powers."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: evamunmeṣanibhālanodyuktasyāpi dehātmamānino yogino bindunādādayaḥ kṣobhakā bhavantītyuktam ||
children.translated_text: In this way it has been said that, even for a yogin intent on observing <s>unmeṣa</s>, if he identifies the self with the body, bindu, nāda, and the rest become agitators.

children.text: idānīmatronmeṣātmani svabhāve dehapramātṛtāṃ nimajjayati tadākārāmapi parapramātṛtāṃ labhata ityāha ||
children.translated_text: Now he says that when, in this nature whose self is <s>unmeṣa</s>, one sinks the status of being a bodily subject, then one obtains supreme subjectivity, even while having that form.

children.text: Chapter 32

yathā paśyantīrūpāvikalpakadidṛkṣāvasare didṛkṣito 'rtho 'ntarabhedena sphurati tathaiva svacchandādyadhvaprakriyoktān dharādiśivāntāntarbhāvino 'śeṣānarthān vyāpyeti sarvam aham iti sadāśivavat svavikalpānusaṃdhānapūrvakam avikalpāntam abhedavimarśāntaḥkroḍīkāreṇācchādya yadāvatiṣṭhate asyāḥ samāpatterna vicalati tāvad aśeṣavedyaikīkāreṇonmiṣattāvadvedyagrāsīkārimahāpramātṛtāsamāveśacamatkārarūpaṃ yat phalaṃ tat svayam evāvabhotsyate svasaṃvidevānubhaviṣyati kim atra bahunā pratipāditena ||
children.translated_text: Just as, at the moment of non-conceptual desire-to-see in the form of <s>paśyantī</s>, the desired object flashes forth without internal difference, so too, when one pervades all objects included within earth up to <s>Śiva</s>, as taught in the procedures of the paths in the <s>Svacchanda</s> and other scriptures, and, like <s>Sadāśiva</s>, stands in the form 'All this is I,' covering them by an enclosure within the nondual reflection that ends in non-conceptuality, preceded by the investigation of one's own concepts; so long as one does not slip from this absorption, one will oneself realize the fruit whose form is the marvel of absorption into great subjectivity, which, by unifying all knowable objects, opens out and devours all those knowables. One's own consciousness itself will experience it. What is the point of explaining much here?

children.text: tasyopalabdhiḥ satatam iti pratijñāya tadanantaram upapāditam upāyajātaṃ pariśīlayataḥ satataṃ spandatattvasamāviṣṭatvaṃ suprabuddhasya bhavatīti tadanantaprameyasaṃbhinnatvād upadeśyahṛdaye smārayann anupraveśayuktyupasaṃhārabhaṅgyāha ||
children.translated_text: Having promised, "Its apprehension is constant," and then explained the set of means for it, he now reminds the heart of the one to be instructed that, for one who continually cultivates it and is fully awakened, there is constant immersion in the <s>spanda</s> principle, because it is interpenetrated with endless knowables; and he speaks by way of concluding through the method of entry:

children.text: Chapter 33
sarvadā jāgarāsvapnasuṣuptasaṃvidādimadhyāntapadeṣu prabuddhas tiṣṭhet unmīlitaspandatattvāvaṣṭambhadivyadṛṣṭiḥ suprabuddhatām eva bhajeta ||
children.translated_text: At all times, in the beginning, middle, and end positions of the awarenesses of waking, dream, deep sleep, and so on, one should remain awakened, supported by the divine vision whose basis is the opened <s>spanda</s> principle, and should abide only in the state of being fully awakened.

children.text: kathaṃ jñānena bahirmukhenāvabhāsena sarvaṃ gocaraṃ nīlasukhādirūpaṃ viṣayam ālokya
children.translated_text: How? By knowledge, that is, by outward-facing illumination, having looked upon every range of experience, every object in the form of blue, pleasure, and so on,

children.text: tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, in reflections on word and meaning, that is no state which is not <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: ityupapāditadṛśā vimṛśya ekatra sraṣṭari śaṃkarātmani svabhāve sarvam āropayet nimīlanonmīlanadaśayos tadabhedena jānīyāt pūrvāparakoṭyavaṣṭambhadārḍhyān madhyabhūmim api cidrasāśyānatārūpatayaiva paśyed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Considering this with the vision that has been established, one should superimpose everything upon the one creator, upon the nature whose self is <s>Śaṅkara</s>; in the states of closing and opening the eyes one should know it as non-different from him; and, because of the firmness that supports the prior and posterior extremes, one should see even the middle ground as nothing but having the form of the condensed essence of consciousness. This is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ ca na kenacid anyena vyatiriktena vastunā bādhyate sarvasmin svātmanaḥ svīkṛtatvāt ||
children.translated_text: And thus it is not obstructed by any other distinct reality, because in everything one has accepted one's own self.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīpratyabhijñākāreṇa
children.translated_text: As has been said by the venerable author of the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>:

children.text: yo 'vikalpam idam artham aṇḍajaṃ paśyatīśa nikhilaṃ bhavadvapuḥ
children.translated_text: "O Lord, he who sees this whole object born from the egg, without conceptual construction, as your body,

children.text: svātmapakṣaparipūrite jagatyasya nityasukhinaḥ kuto bhayam
children.translated_text: for him, eternally happy, with the world filled by the side of his own self, whence could there be fear?"

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tato 'nyena na pīḍyate iti yaduktaṃ tatra ko 'sāv anyaḥ pīḍakaḥ kaś ca pīḍyo yataḥ śivātmakam eva viśvamuktam ityāśaṅkya pāśānāṃ paśośca svarūpaṃ nirṇetum āha ||
children.translated_text: Then, regarding what was said, "he is not afflicted by another," one might object: who is this other afflicter, and who is afflicted, since the universe has been said to have <s>Śiva</s> as its self? Anticipating this, in order to determine the nature of the bonds and of the bound soul, he says:

children.text: Chapter 34
iha yo 'yaṃ prakāśātmā svasvabhāvaḥ śāṃkara uktaḥ asau
children.translated_text: Here, this own nature, whose self is luminosity and which has been described as belonging to <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: vyavasthitaḥ karotyeṣa viśvakāraṇam īśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: "This Lord, established as the cause of the universe, performs

children.text: sṛṣṭiṃ sthitiṃ ca saṃhāraṃ tirodhānamanugraham ||
children.translated_text: creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment, and grace."

children.text: iti śrīsvacchandaśāstradṛṣṭyā nijaśaktyāśliṣṭaḥ sadā pañcavidhakṛtyakārī svatantraḥ spandalaliteśvarādiśabdair āgameṣūdghoṣyate ||
children.translated_text: According to the view of the venerable <s>Svacchandaśāstra</s>, he is embraced by his own power, always performs the fivefold act, is free, and is proclaimed in the Āgamas by words such as <s>Spanda</s>, <s>Laliteśvara</s>, and the like.

children.text: svātantryaśaktir evāsya sanātanī pūrṇāhaṃtārūpā parā matsyodarī mahāsattā sphurattormiḥ sāraṃ hṛdayaṃ bhairavī devī śikhā ityādibhir asaṃkhyaiḥ prakārais tatra tatra nirucyate ||
children.translated_text: His power of freedom itself, eternal and having the form of full I-ness, is described here and there in countless ways as the supreme one, <s>Matsyodarī</s>, great Being, a wave of flashing manifestation, essence, heart, the goddess <s>Bhairavī</s>, the crest, and so forth.

children.text: pūrṇāhaṃtaiva cāsyānuttarānāhataśaktisaṃpuṭīkārasvīkṛtādikṣāntavarṇabhaṭṭārikā tata eva svīkṛtānantavācyavākarūpaṣaḍadhvasphāramayāśeṣaśakticakrakroḍīkārāntaḥ kṛtaniḥśeṣasargapralayādiparamparāpyakramavimarśarūpaiva nityoditānuccāryamahāmantramayī sarvajīvitabhūtā parā vāk ||
children.translated_text: And this full I-ness itself is his supreme speech: the venerable goddess of letters from a to kṣa, accepted by being enclosed in the powers called anuttara and anāhata; therefore expanded as the sixfold path consisting of the accepted infinite denotable objects and denoting words; embracing the whole wheel of powers; having within herself the entire series of creations, dissolutions, and the rest; nevertheless consisting only of non-sequential reflective awareness; made of the great unutterable mantra that is eternally arisen; and being the life of all.

children.text: eṣaiva bhagavata iyadviśvavaicitryacalattām iva svātmani prathayantī spandate ityarthānugamāt spanda iti ihocyate ||
children.translated_text: This very power, because it manifests within itself, as it were, the motion of the Lord's vast variety of the universe, vibrates; from following this meaning it is here called <s>spanda</s>.

children.text: evaṃ ceyad viśvaśaktikhacitaparāśaktisundarasya svātmanaḥ svarūpagopanakrīḍayā svātmabhittāv evāṃśāṃśikayā nirbhāsanaṃ bhagavān yāvaccikīrṣati tāvadekaivābhinnāpyasau tadīyā vimarśaśaktiricchātvaṃ pratipadya jñānakriyārūpatayā sthitvā śivaśaktiparāmarśātmakabījayonibhedena dvidhā bhūtvā vargabhedena tatkalābhedena ca navadhā pañcāśaddhā ca sphurantī tadvimarśasārair aghoraghoraghorataraiḥ saṃvittidevatātmabhiḥ rūpaiḥ prathamānā bhagavataḥ pañcavidhakṛtyakāritāṃ nirvahati ||
children.translated_text: And thus, for as long as the Blessed Lord wishes to make, upon the wall of his own self, a manifestation part by part through the play of concealing his own nature, although his own self is beautiful with the supreme power inlaid with all these powers of the universe, for that long this one reflective power of his, though undivided, assumes the state of will, abides as knowledge and action, becomes twofold through the distinction of seed and womb whose nature is the apprehension of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, and, flashing as ninefold by the distinction of classes and fiftyfold by the distinction of its kalās, appearing through forms whose selves are deities of consciousness, aghora, ghora, and ghoratara, and whose essence is that reflective awareness, accomplishes the Lord's performance of the fivefold act.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīmālinīvijayottare
children.translated_text: As has been said in the venerable <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s>:

children.text: yā sā śaktirjagaddhātuḥ kathitā samavāyinī
children.translated_text: "That power of the creator of the world, which has been taught as inherent,

children.text: icchātvaṃ tasya sā devī sisṛkṣoḥ pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: that goddess assumes the condition of will when he wishes to create.

children.text: saikāpi satyanekatvaṃ yathā gacchati tacchṛṇu
children.translated_text: Hear how she, though being one, attains multiplicity.

children.text: evametaditi jñeyaṃ nānyatheti suniścitam ||
children.translated_text: This is to be known as exactly so; it is firmly settled that it is not otherwise.

children.text: jñāpayantī jagatyatra jñānaśaktirnigadyate
children.translated_text: When she makes known in this world, 'This is so,' she is called the power of knowledge.

children.text: evaṃ bhavatvidaṃ sarvamiti kāryonmukhī yadā ||
children.translated_text: When, being oriented toward effect, she says, 'Let all this come to be thus,'

children.text: jātā tadaiva tadvastu kurvatyatra kriyocyate
children.translated_text: then, having become that very thing and producing that reality here, she is called action.

children.text: evameṣā dvirūpāpi punarbhedair anantatām ||
children.translated_text: Thus this goddess, though having two forms, again goes to infinity through distinctions,

children.text: arthopādhivaśād yāti cintāmaṇiriveśvarī
children.translated_text: by force of limiting adjuncts that are objects, like a wish-fulfilling jewel.

children.text: tatra tāvatsamāpannā mātṛbhāvaṃ vibhidyate ||
children.translated_text: There, first, having entered the state of the measurer, <s>Mālinī</s> is divided

children.text: dvidhā ca navadhā caiva pañcāśaddhā ca mālinī
children.translated_text: into two, into nine, and into fifty.

children.text: bījayonyātmakādbhedāddvidhā bījaṃ svarā matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the distinction whose nature is seed and womb, she is twofold; the vowels are regarded as seed,

children.text: kādayaśca smṛtā yonirnavadhā vargabhedataḥ
children.translated_text: and the consonants beginning with ka are remembered as the womb. She is ninefold by the distinction of classes,

children.text: pṛthagvarṇavibhedena śatārdhakiraṇojjvalā ||
children.translated_text: and, by the separate distinction of letters, she shines with fifty rays.

children.text: bījamatra śivaḥ śaktir yonir ityabhidhīyate
children.translated_text: Here the seed is <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Śakti</s> is called the womb.

children.text: vargāṣṭakamiti jñeyamaghorādyamanukramāt ||
children.translated_text: The set of eight classes is to be known in sequence as beginning with <s>Aghora</s>.

children.text: tadeva śaktibhedena māheśvaryādi cāṣṭakam
children.translated_text: That same set, through the distinction of powers, is also the group of eight beginning with <s>Māheśvarī</s>.

children.text: śatārdhabhedabhinnā ca tatsaṃkhyānāṃ varānane ||
children.translated_text: And divided by the distinctions of fifty, O fair-faced one,

children.text: rudrāṇāṃ vācakatvena kalpitā parameṣṭhinā
children.translated_text: it was fashioned by the Supreme Lord as the denoter of the corresponding number of <s>Rudras</s>;

children.text: tadvadeva ca śaktīnāṃ tatsaṃkhyānāmanukramāt ||
children.translated_text: and likewise, in sequence, of the powers of the same number."

children.text: ityādi ||
children.translated_text: And so on.

children.text: tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: viṣayeṣveva saṃlīnānadho'dhaḥ pātayantyaṇūn
children.translated_text: "Those that, merged in the objects themselves, cast the atomic souls lower and lower down,

children.text: rudrāṇūnyāḥ samāliṅgya ghorataryo 'parāstu tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those others that embrace the rudra-souls, are the more terrible ones.

children.text: miśrakarmaphalāsaktiṃ pūrvavajjanayanti yāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those that, as before, produce attachment to the fruit of mixed actions

children.text: muktimārganirodhinyastāḥ syur ghorāḥ parāparāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and obstruct the path of liberation are the terrible, both supreme and non-supreme.

children.text: pūrvavajjantujātasya śivadhāmaphalapradāḥ
children.translated_text: Those that, as before, bestow on the multitude of beings the fruit of the abode of <s>Śiva</s>

children.text: parāḥ prakathitās tajjñair aghorāḥ śivaśaktayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are declared by the knowers to be the supreme, the non-terrible powers of <s>Śiva</s>."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: evaṃ śabdarāśeḥ samutthito varganavakarūpo yo brāhmyādidevatāvargaḥ śivasahitastasya bhogyatāṃ pāśyatāṃ gataḥ sansa eva śaṃkarātmā svabhāvaḥ paśuḥ smṛtaḥ āgameṣu tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, the class of deities beginning with <s>Brāhmī</s>, consisting of the nine classes and arisen from the mass of sound, together with <s>Śiva</s>, has become something to be enjoyed, has come to the condition of a bond; and that very nature whose self is <s>Śaṅkara</s> is remembered as the bound soul and is so described in the Āgamas.

children.text: nanu kathaṃ bhoktā maheśvara imāmavasthāṃ prāptaḥ ityāśaṅkāśāntyai viśeṣaṇadvāreṇa hetumāha kalāviluptavibhava iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, to quiet the doubt, 'How has the enjoyer, <s>Maheśvara</s>, come to this condition?', he states the cause by means of the qualifier: 'because his greatness has been obscured by kalā.'

children.text: kalayati bahiḥ kṣipati pārimityena paricchinattīti kalā māyāśaktiḥ tayā viluptavibhavaḥ svamāyayā gūhitaiśvaryaḥ sthita ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Kalā" is so called because it measures, casts outward, and delimits by limitation; it is the power of māyā. By that he is "of obscured greatness," that is, his lordship is concealed by his own māyā, and he remains so.

children.text: atha ca kalayā kiṃcitkartṛtvopodbalanātmanā śaktyā tadupalakṣitena kalāvidyākālaniyatirāgātmanā kañcukena viluptavibhavaḥ sthagitapūrṇatvakartṛtvādidharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And further, through kalā, the power whose nature is the strengthening of a small degree of agency, and through the sheath indicated by it, whose nature is kalā, vidyā, time, niyati, and attachment, his greatness is obscured; the qualities such as fullness and agency are covered over.

children.text: bhavatvevaṃ bhogyatāṃ tu kathamasau śaktivargasya gataḥ ityatraitad evottaram ||
children.translated_text: Let this be so. But how has he come to be an object of enjoyment for the group of powers? To this, precisely this is the answer.

children.text: kalābhir akārādivargādhiṣṭhāyikābhir brāhmyādibhis tadvarṇabhaṭṭārakādhiṣṭhātṛbhūtābhiś ca śrīmālinīvijayoktadevatārūpābhiḥ kalābhir akārādivarṇair viluptavibhavaḥ saṃkucito'smi apūrṇo 'smi karavāṇi kiṃcididam upādade idaṃ jahāmi ityādivicitravikalpakāvikalpakapratipattikadambakāntaranupraviṣṭasthūlasūkṣmaśabdānuvedhakadarthito harṣaśokādirūpatāṃ nenīyamāna iva kṣaṇam api svarūpasthitiṃ na labhate yataḥ ato'sāv uktarūpaḥ śaktivargeṇa bhujyamānaḥ paśur uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the kalās that preside over the classes beginning with a, such as <s>Brāhmī</s> and the others, and by the kalās that are the forms of the deities taught in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijaya</s>, presiding over the revered letters, and by the letters beginning with a, he is of obscured greatness. Tormented by the gross and subtle words that penetrate the mass of various determinate and indeterminate apprehensions, such as "I am contracted," "I am incomplete," "What little thing shall I do?" "I take this up," and "I abandon this," and as if being led into states such as joy and sorrow, he does not gain abiding in his own nature even for a moment. Therefore the bound soul of the stated kind is said to be enjoyed by the group of powers.

children.text: kalayā akhyātyātmanāṃśena viluptavibhavaḥ saṃkucita iva na tu tattvataḥ śivātmā svabhāvo 'sya kvāpi gataḥ tadabhāve hi sa eva na sphuret ||
children.translated_text: By kalā, by the portion whose nature is non-recognition, his greatness is obscured, as though he were contracted. But in reality his own nature, whose self is <s>Śiva</s>, has not gone anywhere; for if that were absent, he himself would not shine forth.

children.text: tathāvabhāsamānaireva kalābhiḥ saṃkucitaiḥ śabdair jñānaiś ca viluptavibhavas tathārūpam ātmānaṃ na vimraṣṭuṃ kṣama ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, by the kalās appearing in that way, and by contracted words and cognitions, his greatness is obscured, and he is unable to reflectively apprehend himself as having that nature.

children.text: adhunā paśuḥ saṃkucitadṛkśaktibādhyaḥ pāśyaś cetyetad vibhajati ||
children.translated_text: Now he explains separately that the bound soul is obstructed by contracted powers of seeing and is also bound by bonds.

children.text: Chapter 35
tasya paśoryaḥ pratyayānāṃ laukikaśāstrīyavikalpānāṃ tadadhivāsitānāṃ bhinnārthajñānānāṃ vikalpānām apyudbhavaḥ vināśāghrāta utpādaḥ sa parasyāmṛtarasasya cidghanasyānandaprasarasyāpāyo nimajjanam ||
children.translated_text: For that bound soul, the arising of pratyayas, that is, of worldly and scriptural conceptual constructions, imbued by them, and of differentiated cognitions of distinct objects, an arising touched by destruction, is the disappearance, the sinking, of the supreme immortal nectar, the dense mass of consciousness and expansion of bliss.

children.text: uditeṣu bhinnārtheṣu pratyayeṣu cidbhūmiḥ sthitāpy aparāmṛśyamānatvād asthiteva lakṣyate tata evam uktam ||
children.translated_text: When pratyayas concerning differentiated objects have arisen, the ground of consciousness, though present, appears as if absent because it is not reflectively apprehended. For that very reason this has been said.

children.text: tena ca pratyayodbhavenāyam asvatantratām eti tadvaśaḥ sampadyate ||
children.translated_text: And through that arising of pratyayas this person reaches dependence; he becomes subject to their control.

children.text: yaduktaṃ śrīśivasūtreṣu jñānaṃ bandhaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: This is what was stated in the venerable <s>Śivasūtras</s>: "Knowledge is bondage."

children.text: śrīmadvyāsamunināpi mātāpitṛmayo bālye iti ||
children.translated_text: And also by the venerable sage <s>Vyāsa</s>: "In childhood one is made of mother and father," and so on.

children.text: śrīmadālasayāpi ||
children.translated_text: And also by the venerable <s>Ālasā</s>:

children.text: tāteti kiṃcittanayeti kiṃcit ambeti kiṃciddayiteti kiṃcit
children.translated_text: "Do not speak of the material aggregate in many ways, as 'father' in one respect, 'son' in another, 'mother' in another, 'beloved' in another,

children.text: mameti kiṃcin na mameti kiṃcit bhautaṃ saṃghaṃ bahudhā mā lapethāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'mine' in one respect and 'not mine' in another."

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: pratyayasyodbhavastanmātrāṇi tīvrātīvrabhedasāmānyavṛttayo gocaro yasya tathābhūto bhinnavedyaviṣaya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The arising of pratyaya is that whose field is the tanmātras, the general functions distinguished as intense and not intense; the meaning is that it has as its object what is knowable as differentiated.

children.text: anenedamāha yāvadiyaṃ bhinnavedyaprathā tāvad baddha eva yadā tūktopadeśayuktyā sarvam ātmamayam evāvicalapratipattyā pratipadyate tadā jīvanmukta iti ||
children.translated_text: By this he says the following: as long as this manifestation of differentiated knowables exists, one is bound. But when, through the instruction and reasoning already stated, one apprehends with unwavering conviction that everything is simply made of the self, then one is liberated while living.

children.text: yathoktam iti vā yasya saṃvittiḥ ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Or, as in the statement "as has been said: he whose awareness ..." and so on.

children.text: evaṃ ca yat pūrvam uktaṃ tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ ityādi na tena saha parāmṛtarasāpāyas tasya yaḥ pratyayodbhavaḥ ityasya vaiṣamyaṃ kiṃcit ||
children.translated_text: And so what was previously said, "there is no state in thoughts of word and object that is not <s>Śiva</s>," and the like, is not in any conflict with the statement that the arising of pratyaya for him is the disappearance of the supreme immortal nectar.

children.text: nanu yadi pratyayodbhavo 'pyasya parāmṛtarasāpāyaḥ tatkatham uktaṃ śaktivargasya bhogyatāṃ gata ityāśaṅkāṃ pariharati ||
children.translated_text: But if even the arising of pratyaya is for him the disappearance of the supreme immortal nectar, how was it said that he has become an object of enjoyment for the group of powers? He removes this objection.

children.text: Chapter 36
caḥ śaṅkāṃ dyotayan tatparihārarūpaṃ prameyāntaraṃ samuccinoti ||
children.translated_text: The word ca, indicating the doubt, adds another object of knowledge that has the form of answering it.

children.text: asya paśoḥ svasya śivātmano rūpasyāvaraṇe bhittibhūtatvena prathamānasyāpi samyagaparāmarśane tannimittaṃ vyākhyātarūpāḥ śaktayaḥ satatam utthitāḥ yāvaddhi parāmṛtarasātmakasvasvarūpapratyabhijñānam asya na vṛttaṃ tāvad etāḥ svasvarūpāvaraṇāyodyacchantyeva ||
children.translated_text: For this bound soul, the powers explained in the manner stated, whose cause is the lack of proper reflective apprehension even though his own form, the self whose nature is <s>Śiva</s>, is manifesting as the wall-like basis for its covering, are constantly arisen. For so long as recognition of his own nature, whose essence is the supreme immortal nectar, has not occurred for him, these powers keep striving to cover that very own nature.

children.text: yato'sya yaḥ pratyayodbhavo vikalpakāvikalpakajñānaprasaraḥ sa śabdānuvedhena ahamidaṃ jānāmi ityādinā sūkṣmāntaḥśabdānurañjanena sthūlābhilāpasaṃsargeṇa ca vinā na bhavati iti tiraścām apyasāṃketikaḥ nirdeśaprakhyaḥ svātmani ca śironirdeśaprakhyo 'ntarabhyupagamarūpaḥ śabdanavimarśo 'styeva anyathā bālasya prathamasaṃketagrahaṇaṃ na ghaṭeta antarūhāpohātmakavimarśaśūnyatvāt
children.translated_text: Because the arising of pratyaya for him, the expansion of determinate and indeterminate cognition, does not occur without being penetrated by word, through the coloring of subtle inner word, as in "I know this," and through contact with gross expression. Thus even among animals there is surely a word-reflection that is not based on convention and resembles indication; and within oneself there is a word-reflection resembling a pointing to the head, having the form of inner acceptance. Otherwise a child's first grasping of convention would not be possible, since it would lack inner reflection in the form of supposition and exclusion.

children.text: sthūlaśabdānuvedhamayas tu vikalpaḥ sarvasya svānubhavasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But determinate cognition made of penetration by gross words is established by everyone's own experience.

children.text: ślokatrayoktam artham upasaṃharanniyataḥ prameyasya sāmānyaspandatattvādabhinnatāṃ prāguktām anubadhnan tatpratyabhijñānāpratyabhijñānamayau bandhamokṣau iti lakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, summing up the meaning stated in the three verses and carrying forward the previously stated non-difference of the specific object of knowledge from the general <s>spanda</s> principle, he characterizes bondage and liberation as consisting in non-recognition and recognition of that.

children.text: Chapter 37

seti ślokatrayanirṇītatvāt iyamiti prameyaparyantena rūpeṇa sphurantī svasvabhāvarūpasya cidātmanaḥ śivasya sambandhinī spandatattvātmikā parābhaṭṭārikaiva viśvavaicitryāvasthitikāritvāt kriyāśaktiḥ prāṅnirṇītadṛśā śiva eva gṛhītapaśubhūmike vartamānā prāṇapuryaṣṭakarūpam amuṃ kartṛtātmanāhaṃtāvipruṣā prokṣitaṃ kurvāṇā tathārūpeṇāpratyabhijñāya svarūpāvārakatvād dhānādānādiparikleśahetutvācca bandhayitrī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because the three verses have determined this point, this very Supreme Lady, whose nature is the <s>spanda</s> principle, shines forth in the form extending to the object of knowledge and belongs to <s>Śiva</s>, the consciousness-self whose form is his own nature. Since she brings about the abiding of the manifold variety of the universe, she is the power of action, already determined in the manner explained above. When she is present in <s>Śiva</s> after he has assumed the plane of the bound soul, making this entity consisting of prāṇa and the puryaṣṭaka into an agent, sprinkled with drops of I-ness, then, because he does not recognize her in that form, she becomes the binder, since she veils his own nature and causes the afflictions of rejection, acceptance, and the rest.

children.text: yadā tu svasya śivātmano rūpasya yo mārgaḥ
children.translated_text: But when the path of his own form as the self that is <s>Śiva</s> is as follows:

children.text: śaktyavasthāṃ praviṣṭasya nirvibhāgena bhāvanā
children.translated_text: "For one who has entered the state of power, contemplation without division

children.text: tadāsau śivarūpī syācchaivī mukham ihocyate ||
children.translated_text: then he would be of the form of <s>Śiva</s>; here the <s>śaivī</s> is called the mouth."

children.text: iti śrīvijñānabhaṭṭārakoktanītyā prāptyupāyaḥ parāśaktistadātmatayāsau kriyāśaktirjñāyate yoginā yadā vā vikalpakāvikalpakaprasare 'pi śivasvarūpasya svātmano 'ṃśabhūtam evāśeṣavedyam anenekṣyate tadāsyāsau parānandamayīṃ parāṃ siddhim upapādayati ||
children.translated_text: According to this rule stated by the venerable <s>Vijñānabhaṭṭāraka</s>, when that power of action is known by the yogin as the supreme power, the means of attainment, because it has that as its own nature, or when, even amid the expansion of conceptual and nonconceptual cognition, everything knowable is seen by him as only a portion of his own self, whose form is <s>Śiva</s>, then this power brings him to the supreme attainment, filled with supreme bliss.

children.text: Chapter 38
puryaṣṭakotthitaṃ bhogaṃ bhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: He experiences the enjoyment arisen from the puryaṣṭaka.

children.text: yata eva pratyayeṣu sukhādipratyayodbhavaḥ ata evāsau pratyayodbhavāt paśuḥ paravaśaḥ śabdānuvedhakrameṇa pade pade brāhmyādidevībhir ākṣipyamāṇaḥ na tu suprabuddhavat svatantraḥ tasya puryaṣṭakasya bhāvādeva punaḥpunarudbodhitavicitravāsanaḥ saṃsaret tattadbhogocitabhogāyatanāni śarīrāṇyarjayitvā gṛhṇāti cotsṛjati ca ||
children.translated_text: Precisely because the arising of cognitions such as pleasure occurs in the cognitions, therefore, because he arises from cognition, he is a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), dependent on another, dragged at every step by the goddesses such as <s>Brāhmī</s> through the sequence penetrated by words, and not free like one who is fully awakened. By the very existence of that puryaṣṭaka, with varied latent impressions awakened again and again, he transmigrates; after acquiring bodies that are suitable seats of enjoyment for each particular experience, he takes them on and casts them off.

children.text: yataś caivam ato 'sya puryaṣṭakasaṃruddhasya yā saṃsṛtis tasyā yaḥ prakṛṣṭo layaḥ puryaṣṭakātmakamalocchedena vināśaḥ tasya kāraṇaṃ samyak sukhopāyaṃ pracakṣmahe samanantaram eva brūmaḥ tathā sampracakṣmahe prakaraṇe 'smin svayaṃ pratipāditavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because this is so, we shall explain the excellent dissolution of his transmigration, he who is confined by the puryaṣṭaka, namely its destruction through the eradication of the impurity consisting of the puryaṣṭaka, and the cause of that dissolution, the true and happy means. We shall state it immediately afterward; indeed we have explained it ourselves in this treatise.

children.text: vartamānasāmīpye vartamānavad vā ||
children.translated_text: Or the present is used as if the thing were close to the present.

children.text: iti vartamānaprayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus there is the use of the present tense.

children.text: etat pratipādayan ādyasūtroktamarthaṃ nigamayati ||
children.translated_text: While explaining this, he concludes the meaning stated in the first sūtra.

children.text: Chapter 39

yadā punarayamuktāḥ paratattvasamāveśopadeśayuktīḥ pariśīlayan ekatra pūrṇāhaṃtātmani spandatattve samyagavicalatvena rūḍhaḥ samāviṣṭas tanmayo bhavati tadā tasyeti pūrvasūtranirdiṣṭasya puryaṣṭakasya taddvāreṇaiva viśvasya nimīlanonmīlanasamāveśābhyāṃ layodayau niyacchan prathamasūtranirṇītadṛśā ekasmād eva śaṃkarātmanaḥ svabhāvāt saṃhāraṃ sargaṃ ca kurvan bhoktṛtām eti dharādiśivāntasamagrabhogyakavalanena paramapramātṛtāṃ satīm eva pratyabhijñānakrameṇāvalambeta ||
children.translated_text: But when this person, cultivating the already stated instructions and reasonings for absorption into the supreme reality, becomes firmly rooted without wavering in the one <s>spanda</s> principle whose self is full I-ness, becomes absorbed in it, and becomes identical with it, then, by means of the contraction and expansion of that puryaṣṭaka mentioned in the preceding sūtra, and thereby of the universe itself, he controls its dissolution and arising. Making destruction and creation from the one very nature whose self is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, in the manner determined in the first sūtra, he attains enjoyership; through the swallowing of the entire field of objects to be enjoyed, from earth up to <s>Śiva</s>, he would take hold, by the process of recognition, of supreme subjecthood, which is already real.

children.text: tataś ca prathamasūtranirṇītasya śakticakrasya svamarīcinicayasyeśvaro 'dhipatir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And consequently he would become the lord, the ruler, of the wheel of powers determined in the first sūtra, the mass of his own rays.

children.text: anenaiva ca dehena maheśvaratvam avāpnotyeveti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: That is to say, with this very body he certainly attains the state of <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: evaṃ copakramopasaṃhārayor mahārthasaṃpuṭīkāraṃ darśayan tatsāratayā samastaśāṃkaropaniṣanmūrdhanyatām asyāviṣkaroti śāstrasya śrīmān vasuguptācāryaḥ iti śivam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, showing the enclosing of the great meaning at the beginning and conclusion, the glorious teacher <s>Vasugupta</s> reveals that this scripture, by virtue of that essence, stands at the head of all the <s>Śaṅkara</s>-Upaniṣads. Thus, auspiciousness.

children.text: Chapter 40
tāmasāmānyāṃ bhagavatīṃ guruṃ śaivī mukham ihocyate iti sthityā śivadhāmaprāptihetutvād ācāryarūpām ||
children.translated_text: I bow to the Blessed Lady, the uncommon dark one, the guru, in the sense of having the form of the teacher, because she is the cause of attaining the abode of <s>Śiva</s>, according to the established statement, "here the <s>śaivī</s> is called the mouth."

children.text: atha ca guruṃ paśyantyādikroḍīkārāt mahatīṃ bhāratīṃ parāṃ vācam tathā guror ācāryasya sambandhinīm upadeṣṭrīṃ giraṃ citrāṃ lokottaracamatkārarūpāṃ vande sarvotkṛṣṭatvena samāviśāmi ||
children.translated_text: And further, I honor the guru as great <s>Bhāratī</s>, the supreme speech, because she embraces <s>paśyantī</s> and the other levels; likewise, I enter into the guru's speech, that of the teacher, the instructress, variegated and possessing the form of extraordinary wonder, because she is supreme above all.

children.text: atha ca sarvāvasthāsu sphuradrūpatvād abhivadantīm udyantṛtāprayatnenābhivādaye svarūpavimarśaniṣṭhāṃ tāṃ samāveṣṭuṃ saṃmukhīkaromi ||
children.translated_text: And further, because she shines forth in all states, I salute her as speaking; with the effort of raising her up, I bring her face to face so as to enter into her, who is established in reflective awareness of her own nature.

children.text: kīdṛśīm agādho duruttaro yaḥ saṃśayaḥ pūrṇāhaṃtāniścayābhāvātmā vicitraḥ śaṅkākalaṅkaḥ sa eva vitatatvenāmbhodhis tasya samyaguttaraṇe yā tāriṇī naur iva tām ityubhayatrāpi yojyam
children.translated_text: What sort of one? She is like a ship that carries one across the unfathomable and hard-to-cross ocean, namely the vast and varied stain of doubt, whose nature is the absence of certainty in full I-ness. This should be construed in both places.

children.text: tathā vicitrārthāni nānācamatkāraprayojanāni padāni viśrāntayo yasyāṃ parasyāṃ vāci tāṃ vicitrāṇi ramyaracanānupraviṣṭāni arthapadāni vācyavācakāni yasyāṃ guruvāci tām ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, I honor that supreme speech in which there are words, rests, with varied meanings and many purposes of wonder; or that guru's speech in which there are varied and meaning-bearing words, signifieds and signifiers, entered into a lovely composition.

children.text: prasiddhaprabhāvasvanāmodīraṇāt sambhāvanāpratyayenārthinaḥ pravartayan gūhanīyatayā mahāphalatām asya śāstrasya nirūpayati śāstrakāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: By uttering the well-known powerful name, he induces seekers to proceed through the conviction that it is possible, and the author of the scripture shows the great fruitfulness of this scripture by presenting it as something to be kept secret.

children.text: Chapter 41

etacchāstroktam etajjñānam eva puruṣārthaprāptihetutvād dhanam alabhyam api duṣprāpam api labdhvā śaṃkarasvapnopadeśasāraṃ śilātalād avāpya prakāśavimarśātmakaṃ hṛdayam eva viśvāntaḥpraveśāvakāśapradatvād guhā tasyām antena niścayena kṛtā nihitiḥ sthāpanā yena arthāttasyaiva jñānadhanasya tasya svāminaḥ śrīvasuguptābhidhānasya guroryathaiva tacchivāya jātaṃ tadvadadhikāriniyamasaṃkocābhāvāt sarvalokasyāpi hṛdguhāntakṛtanihiter yatnād asāmayikāt gopayataḥ dṛḍhapratipattyā ca svātmīkurvataḥ sadā śivāya bhavati nityaśaṃkarātmakasvasvabhāvasamāveśalābhāya sampadyata iti śivam ||
children.translated_text: This knowledge taught in this scripture is itself wealth, because it is the cause of attaining the human goal. Though hard to obtain, hard indeed to acquire, having obtained it from the surface of the rock as the essence of <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s instruction in a dream, he made a deposit of it in the cave, that is, in the heart whose nature is manifestation and reflective awareness, because it grants space for entry into the whole universe, with an end, that is, with certainty. In other words, for that very treasure of knowledge, for that lord, the guru named venerable <s>Vasugupta</s>, just as it became for the good, so too, because there is no contraction by restriction to qualified persons, it becomes for the good of all people also: for one who, with effort and outside fixed occasions, guards it as deposited in the end of the cave of the heart, and who makes it his own by firm realization, it always conduces to <s>Śiva</s>, that is, to the attainment of absorption into one's own nature whose essence is eternal <s>Śaṅkara</s>. Thus, auspiciousness.

children.text: yadyapyasmin vivṛtigaṇanā vidyate naiva śāstre lokaścāyaṃ yadapi matimān bhūyasottānavṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: Although in this scripture there is no reckoning of a detailed exposition, and although this world of people, even when intelligent, is for the most part inclined toward superficial explanation,

children.text: jānantyete tadapi kuśalāste 'smadukter viśeṣaṃ kecit sāragrahaṇanipuṇāś cetanārājahaṃsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: still, skillful people know the distinctive point of our statement: some swan-kings of consciousness are expert in grasping the essence.

children.text: anantāparaṭīkākṛnmadhye sthitim amṛṣyatā
children.translated_text: Unable to tolerate our standing among those who compose countless other commentaries,

children.text: vivṛtaṃ spandaśāstraṃ no guruṇā no mayāsya tu ||
children.translated_text: this Spanda scripture has not been expounded by our guru, nor by us; rather, of it

children.text: viśeṣaleśaḥ saṃdohe darśitaḥ pūrvamadya tu
children.translated_text: only a slight particular distinction was shown before in the collection, but now,

children.text: rudraśaktisamāveśaśālinaḥ śivarūpiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of the very earnest request of his own disciple named <s>Śūra</s>, who possesses absorption into <s>Rudra</s>'s power and has the form of <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: śūranāmnaḥ svaśiṣyasya prārthanātirasena tat
children.translated_text: that has been determined by <s>Kṣemarāja</s>,

children.text: nirṇītaṃ kṣemarājena sphārānnijaguror guroḥ ||
children.translated_text: from the abundance of his own guru's guru.

children.text: yeṣāṃ no dhiṣaṇopadeśaviśadā saddaiśikairdarśitā śrīmacchāmbhavaśāsanopaniṣadā yeṣāṃ na bhagno bhramaḥ
children.translated_text: Those for whom our instruction, made clear by true teachers, has not been shown through the Upaniṣad of the glorious <s>Śāmbhava</s> teaching, and whose delusion has not been broken,

children.text: ye nāsvāditapūrviṇo mṛdudhiyaḥ śrīpratyabhijñāmṛtaṃ tenātrādhikṛtāḥ paraiḥ punar idaṃ pūrṇāśayaiś carvyatām ||
children.translated_text: those tender-minded ones who have not previously tasted the nectar of the glorious Pratyabhijñā are qualified here. But let this be chewed over again by others whose intentions are full.

children.text: śivādikṣityanto vitatavitato yo 'dhvavibhavaḥ sphurannānāsargasthitilayadaśācitritatanuḥ
children.translated_text: May that supreme Spanda of consciousness be victorious, the ground and abode of shining unequalled happiness: the expanse of the path, spread out from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth,

children.text: iyadviśvaṃ yasya prasarakaṇikāsau vijayate paraḥ saṃvitspando lasadasamasaukhyāyatanabhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose body is variegated by the manifesting many states of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, and of whom this whole universe is only a small particle of expansion.
